item.title: Court ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​⁠⁠​​​​‍‌​dismisses Sowore’s request seeking DSS DG to testify in his defence
item.description: The Federal High Court in Abuja on Monday dismissed an application by Omoyele Sowore, publisher of Sahara Reporters, seeking an order compelling the Director-General (DG) of Department of State Services (DSS), Mr Oluwatosin Ajayi, to testify in his defence. Justice Mohammed Umar, in a ruling, held that the application by Sowore, the presidential candidate of Action Action Congress (AAC), would not serve the interest of justice. Justice Umar held that the DG or any designated officer of the service who had full knowledge of its official and other relevant business could testify before this court for the defendant (Sowore). The News Agency of Nigeria (NAN) reports that Sowore is being prosecuted by the DSS on allegations bordering on cybercrime. The defendant was alleged to have, in August 2025, published posts on X (formerly Twitter) and Facebook, describing President Bola Tinubu as a “criminal” and accusing him of lying about the level of corruption in the country. Sowore, through his lawyer, Adeyinka Olumide Fusika, SAN, had sought an order of the court compelling the DG’s appearance to testify relating to the cyberbullying case instituted against him. The DSS’ lawyer, Akinlolu Kehinde, SAN, had opposed the move, arguing that another official of the agency could testify on his behalf. The senior lawyer argued that it was absurd for Sowore to insist on the DSS DG’s appearance in court in an action that was purely official and not personal. In his ruling, Justice Umar agreed with Kehinde’s argument that the subpoena concerned an official act of the DSS and that the expected testimony was not personal to the DG. According to the judge the testimony that is expected from the Director General is not personal, but in respect of an official act or engagement. Justice Umar consequently ruled that another DSS official could appear to give evidence on the agency’s behalf. Following the ruling, defence counsel called the 3rd defence witness, Michael Jego, an investigating officer with the DSS. Jego said he was a member of the DSS investigation team which flagged the controversial post of Sowore on X and Facebook and subsequently advised him to retract it. ‎ ‎The witness said the posts made on 26 Aug. 2025 had the potential of posing a significant threat to national security. The witness told the court that he was part of an investigation team that monitored reactions with relation to the post. (NAN) The post Court ​‌‍‍‍‍⁠⁠‍​⁠⁠​​​​‍‌​dismisses Sowore’s request seeking DSS DG to testify in his defence appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Ukraine deploys drone to airlift wounded soldier in 'world-first' operation
item.description: Ukraine has evacuated a wounded soldier from the front line using an aerial drone in what a Ukrainian army brigade has described as a world-first operation. The successful mission highlights the growing role of unmanned technology in battlefield evacuations as drones continue to shape the conflict between Ukraine and Russia.

item.title: Amazon is funding a new nuclear plant in Indiana
item.description: It’ll be several years before the facility is complete, but this digital rendering gives us some idea of what it’ll look like. | Image: Amazon Amazon has signed an agreement with X-energy and American Electric Power (AEP) to fund the building of a new nuclear energy facility in Indiana. The proposed plant , which would replace the now defunct coal-fueled Breed Generating Station in Fairbanks, Sullivan County, aims to provide up to 960 megawatts of carbon-free energy for both the regional power grid and Amazon's data centers. No timeline for construction or operation has been announced for the facility, which Amazon says "could" create 1,000 construction jobs and 100 permanent roles. The facility in Indiana is targeting to build 12 Xe-100 SMR's, an advanced (but unproven) reactor th … Read the full story at The Verge.

item.title: Peyton Manning a favorite candidate for Colts’ GM job
item.description: The Indianapolis Colts fired general manager Chris Ballard on Monday, one day after blowing a 13-0 halftime lead in a 26-20 loss at Lucas Oil Stadium to the previously winless Tennessee Titans . The move came after a 2-4 start to Ballard’s 10th season. Ballard, 57, had held the job since January 2017, signed a five-year extension in 2021 and led Indianapolis to two playoff appearances, in 2018 and 2020. Owner and CEO Carlie Irsay-Gordon said “a change in leadership is necessary” to meet the franchise’s standard of competing for championships. A familiar name from the franchise’s past has already entered the conversation. MORE: 3 NFL teams that should be worried after Week 6 Colts explore Peyton Manning for general manager job Peyton Manning in field before Miami Dolphins and the Indianapolis Colts game. Credit: Grace Hollars-USA TODAY Network via Imagn Images. The Colts are considering Peyton Manning for the general manager vacancy, according to Dan Patrick on The Dan Patrick Show. Indianapolis is exploring whether Manning would be interested in the job and a potential ownership stake down the line. "The Colts' first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning." — DP shares what his source has told him. pic.twitter.com/MgTbuJIxhW — Dan Patrick Show (@dpshow) October 19, 2026 Before his retirement, Manning spent 14 seasons with the Colts, throwing for 54,828 yards and 399 touchdowns and winning Super Bowl XLI before Indianapolis released him in 2012. Irsay-Gordon called the in-season timing deliberate and said the Colts will conduct a thorough search, taking the time necessary to find the right leader. Has Peyton Manning turned down the Colts’ GM job before? He has. Then-owner Jim Irsay said in 2019 that he and Manning came close to an agreement on a president or general manager role before the 2017 season. Manning ultimately passed. Assistant general manager Ed Dodds, who joined the Colts in 2017, also remains with the team and has interviewed for GM jobs elsewhere. Indianapolis visits the Minnesota Vikings on Sunday, Oct. 25, at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. Head coach Shane Steichen will lead the team without the GM who hired him, and Irsay-Gordon said the firing does not change the Colts’ goals for the season. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: The Post's Girls Athlete of the Week: Vote on the best of Oct. 12 - 17
item.description: Welcome to Athlete of the Week voting from The Palm Beach Post! Congratulations to last week's winner, Elle Travers of Benjamin cross country. The sophomore paced the field in the Benjamin Invite, running 22:48.91 to take first place. Each week, The Post will highlight the best boys and girls high school student-athlete performances in Palm Beach County. The polls will be open until noon Friday. Nominees are accepted via email or phone, but will be selected by staff in the absence of submission. Is your team or athlete missing? Send nominations to deputy sports editor Eric J. Wallace (ejwallace@usatodayco.com) and high school sports writer Alex Peterman (apeterman@usatodayco.com). Here's a look at the best girls performances from the the most recent week of high school competition: Voting will be open until Friday, Oct. 23 at noon. Volleyball: Alexa Arenson, Sr., Dwyer ― Paced the Panthers with 17 kills on a .586 kill percentage in a district championship 3-0 sweep of Seminole Ridge Volleyball: Amelie Fortinho, Jr., Spanish River ― Contributed seven kills and a team-high five blocks to help Spanish River beat Western in a 3-2 district championship win Volleyball: Delaney Leite, So., Dr. Joaquín García ― Led the Bulldogs with 15 kills and 23 assists in a 3-1 district championship victory over Wellington Golf: Sara Valentine, Fr., Cardinal Newman ― Paced the field with a 37 in a regular season match against Dwyer Golf: Sofia Clay, Sr., Park Vista ― Paced the field with a 35 in a regular season victory over Olympic Heights Alex Peterman is a high school sports reporter for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at apeterman@usatodayco.com. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: The Post's Girls Athlete of the Week: Vote on the best of Oct. 12 - 17

item.title: Eagles QB Jalen Hurts Out for Season as Blood Clot Spreads to Lungs
item.description: - Jalen Hurts (Vince Mignott/DeFodi Images/DeFodi via Getty Images) Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts will miss the remainder of the 2026 NFL season after doctors discovered blood clots in his lungs. The news, first reported Monday by ESPN ‘s Adam Schefter and NFL Network ‘s Ian Rapoport , marks a major escalation in a medical situation that developed late last week. On Thursday, October 15, the Eagles announced that Hurts would miss Week 6 due to a superficial blood clot in his calf, stemming from an injury suffered against the Los Angeles Rams in Week 4. By Saturday, after consulting with medical specialists, Philadelphia placed the athlete on injured reserve, initially sidelining him for at least four weeks. However, follow-up testing revealed that the clot had progressed into deep vein thrombosis and bilateral pulmonary emboli—forming clots in both lungs. https://t.co/aBfyK55oxd — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 19, 2026 Hurts hasn’t spoken out about the health update, but his agent, Nicole Lynn, along with the Eagles, released a joint statement regarding his diagnosis and expected treatment plan, which was shared across all official social media accounts. While Hurts remains “clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations,” he must undergo a blood-thinning regimen lasting at least three months. League and medical guidelines strictly prohibit players from participating in contact sports while taking anticoagulation medication. While many fans in the comments expressed support, a few expressed anger about why Hurts wasn’t taken out sooner. The Go Birds News account on Twitter commented: “Why was he ever allowed to play in the London game? Complete malpractice.” Another user commented, “JFC, how can you let our star player fly with such a condition. Get better Jalen. go birds.” Despite the sudden end to his season, medical experts expect a complete recovery for the 28-year-old player. “Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery,” the joint statement concluded. “We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.” Read the latest entertainment news on TV Insider .

item.title: Palm Beach County girls weightlifting: Players to know, preseason poll
item.description: The winter season has officially arrived, at least in Florida high school sports . The FHSAA girls weightlifting regular season began Monday, Oct. 19, marking the start of the winter sports season, which also includes soccer, basketball and wrestling. With the 2026 season underway, it's time to take a look at some of the strongest high school athletes in Palm Beach County. This year's competitors include Wellington's Amelia Ciriaco , the reigning Palm Beach Post Player of the Year, and Oxbridge Academy's Sienna Burroughs , who helped establish the ThunderWolves' program. Don't forget to have your say by voting in our girls weightlifting preseason Player of the Year poll, which will be open until noon on Friday, Oct. 23. Girls Weightlifting: Palm Beach County Preseason Watch List Amelia Ciriaco, Sr., Wellington Last season: State runner-up in the Olympic and fourth in traditional in the Class 3A 119-pound division. Regional champion in Traditional, Olympic; District champion in Traditional, Olympic. Sienna Burroughs, Sr., Oxbridge Academy Last season: Fifth-place finisher in the Olympic and 10 th in traditional in the Class 1A 101-pound division. Runner-up in Olympic, fourth place in Traditional at regionals. District champion in Traditional, Olympic. Audrey DellaVecchia, Sr., Wellington Last season: 10 th -place finisher in the traditional lift in the Class 3A 129-pound division. Ashlyn Martin, Sr., King’s Academy Last season: Eighth-place finisher in the traditional lift in the Class 1A 139-pound division. Regional champion in Traditional, runner-up in Olympic; District champion in Traditional, runner-up in Olympic. Taikha Jean-Claude, So., Boynton Beach Last season: Seventh place finish in Class 2A 199-pound Olympic lift; Regional champion in Olympic lift; District champion in Olympic. Eric J. Wallace is deputy sports editor for The Palm Beach Post. He can be reached at ejwallace@usatodayco.com. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Palm Beach County girls weightlifting: Players to know, preseason poll

item.title: Brentford contact police after rugby ball kicked into stadium from high-rise flat during Liverpool match
item.description: Brentford have made contact with the police after a video went viral of a rugby ball being kicked into the Gtech Community Stadium from a high-rise flat during their 2-1 defeat to Liverpool . The club have commented after footage of the incident was spread around on social media, condemning the actions as “dangerous and potentially very harmful”. The ball appeared to initially hit the roof of the Gtech’s East Stand but footage later emerged of a coach inside the ground removing it from inside the ground, indicating that it had bounced down to the pitch. “Brentford Football Club is aware of an incident involving an item being kicked from a height towards the field of play during Saturday’s match against Liverpool,” the club said in a statement. “Such behaviour is dangerous and potentially very harmful. Someone really kicked a rugby ball into Brentford’s stadium from a nearby building while the Bees hosted Liverpool 😳🏉 🎥: Instagram/st_fancy777 ↳ Premier League. Every Match. Live & Exclusive with 4K on Stan Sport. Stream now. #StanSportAU #PremierLeague pic.twitter.com/nwNipczeSa — Stan Sport Football (@StanSportFC) October 19, 2026 “The matter has been referred to the police and the club is supporting the relevant authorities in their investigation to help identify those responsible and take appropriate action, which may result in criminal prosecution. “The matchday safety of fans, staff, players and officials is of utmost importance, and the club will support all efforts to ensure action is taken.” The Gtech, which has hosted the Bees since they moved from Griffin Park in August 2020, is part of a wider development project for the Brentford East district and is therefore surrounded by blocks of flats and other commercial buildings. Alexander Isak struck a late winner as Liverpool came from behind to beat nine-man Brentford, eight minutes after a wonderful Victor Munoz goal cancelled out Keane Lewis-Potter’s opener for the hosts. The victory carried Liverpool above Brentford into fifth, with the Bees one place back in the Premier League table.

item.title: RI's State Championship Super Bowl has a new home | Exclusive
item.description: The ride home for whoever wins the 2026 Rhode Island high school football state championship just got a little longer. Cranston Stadium wasn’t big enough to hold the crowd at last year’s Rhode Island Interscholastic League State Championship game between Hendricken and La Salle, but the RIIL has found a solution to ensure that doesn’t happen again. Per a source, plans have been finalized for this year’s RIIL State Championship game at Bryant University’s Beirne Stadium, with the game being held on Friday, Nov. 20. Why the change? The move comes as no surprise to anyone who was at last year’s state championship game. Cranston Stadium was packed to the gills, with every seat in the bleachers filled and overflow crowds looking for anywhere to stand to watch a game Hendricken won, 13-3. That many people in a small space also created a parking nightmare in the surrounding neighborhood. The stadium lists a capacity of 5,000, but last year’s paid attendance was around 4,100 with estimates of 4,300 people on site with absolutely no room for any more bodies. Crowd control became an issue and the RIIL had 11 police officers on site in case things got hectic. An incredibly boring football game may have helped prevent any incidents. Cranston Stadium became the permanent host for the RIIL Super Bowls in 2008 and served admirably. item.content:encoded: The ride home for whoever wins the 2026 Rhode Island high school football state championship just got a little longer. Cranston Stadium wasn’t big enough to hold the crowd at last year’s Rhode Island Interscholastic League State Championship game between Hendricken and La Salle, but the RIIL has found a solution to ensure that doesn’t happen again. Per a source, plans have been finalized for this year’s RIIL State Championship game at Bryant University’s Beirne Stadium, with the game being held on Friday, Nov. 20. Why the change? The move comes as no surprise to anyone who was at last year’s state championship game. Cranston Stadium was packed to the gills, with every seat in the bleachers filled and overflow crowds looking for anywhere to stand to watch a game Hendricken won, 13-3. That many people in a small space also created a parking nightmare in the surrounding neighborhood. The stadium lists a capacity of 5,000, but last year’s paid attendance was around 4,100 with estimates of 4,300 people on site with absolutely no room for any more bodies. Crowd control became an issue and the RIIL had 11 police officers on site in case things got hectic. An incredibly boring football game may have helped prevent any incidents. Cranston Stadium became the permanent host for the RIIL Super Bowls in 2008 and served admirably. In recent years, there have been questions about why the 90-year old stadium continued to be the home of Rhode Island’s most important games while surrounding states play at larger and more modern facilities. The addition of Pawtucket’s Centerville Bank Stadium added gas to the fire. While the soccer stadium – which is the home for the University of Rhode Island football team while its campus facility is being built – seemed like an obvious choice to become the state’s next host for high school championships, there were several issues preventing that from happening immediately. Cranston Stadium was convenient for the state. It worked geographically and while it dealt with large crowds for the occasional Division I Super Bowl and a Thanksgiving Day game every so often, it didn’t come to a head until last fall. Attendance has grown and Cranston Stadium hasn’t been able to keep up. Why does Bryant make sense? Bryant should, in theory, solve those problems. Beirne Stadium underwent a facelift – provided by Rhode Island FC, which used the stadium as a temporary home while Centerville Bank Stadium was being built – and re-opened in 2024 with 1,000 additional seats, bringing seating capacity to 4,400. Throw on an additional room for 600 people in standing room areas – designed purposefully – and you’re looking at 5,000 people that could safely fit inside Beirne. The stadium has hosted several high school football games in the last few years. Beirne has become the home field for Davies Tech football the last two seasons and Smithfield High School played there while its new turf facility was being built. With a La Salle-Hendricken rematch looming and excitement surrounding high school football as big as it’s been since the early 2000s, the RIIL needed to play at a stadium that could handle a large crowd and provide the necessary amenities that make the game work. Beirne Stadium’s facilities are certainly that. Bryant last hosted high school Super Bowls in 2007. While the stadium has been regarded by many as an ideal home for Super Bowls – good location, good parking, good facility – there was no way the RIIL could keep people from just walking in. The new addition limited entrance points, which gives the RIIL a chance to control the crowd from a ticketing standpoint. It’s also a massive win for Bryant football, which has fallen well behind the University of Rhode Island in terms of recruiting the state. The game gives the school a chance to show off its facilities to the two best high school teams in Rhode Island and at least a handful of players will have the potential to play at the Division I FCS level. What about the other Super Bowls? The 2026 RIIL State Championship Super Bowl is the only game that will be played at Beirne Stadium. Division II, III and IV will play their games at Cranston Stadium. While it may seem unfair, teams in those divisions had the opportunity to play for a state championship but elected to stay down in their respective divisions and play for division titles instead. Further, crowds for Division II, III and IV Super Bowls have been rather lackluster. None of the games have come close to selling out Cranston Stadium, so there was no need to move the games from the site. The current plan is to have the Division II, III and IV Super Bowls at Cranston Stadium on Saturday, Nov. 21. What will happen in 2027? Right now the move to Bryant is a temporary fix. The State Championship Super Bowl outgrew the stadium, so it had to be moved. In a perfect world, all the games would take place at the same facility. There have been rumblings in the past about Beirne Stadium, Centerville Bank and even the University of Rhode Island, once their stadium is complete. Previously, the RIIL was in a position of weakness when choosing a site. People weren’t coming to games and with low ticket sales, cost-effectiveness needed to be a part of the equation. Now the RIIL is in a position of strength. With football popularity skyrocketing, Super Bowl weekend turns into advertising for whoever the host is. Becoming the host would give Bryant or URI a chance to put their facilities and campus on display for players, students and parents, which would help enrollment. We won’t have answers for a while, but a good showing at Beirne Stadium could lead to a permanent change for the RIIL Super Bowls. We’ll know more well after the season is over. item.title: Pokémon Skateboards Officially Launch, and Scalpers Are Already Buying Them Up

Classic cards like the base-set Charizard and more modern cards like the " Moonbreon " from Evolving Skies are randomly packaged in these new products. If that sounds cool to you, here's the bad news: You're probably not going to find any of these in a store.

item.title: AI Proved the Quasi-Riemann Hypothesis. What Happens Now?
item.description: Among the 377 results that OpenAI announced on October 6, 2026, one stood out. It claimed to settle the “quasi-Riemann hypothesis” — a weaker version of the Riemann hypothesis, which is arguably the biggest open question in math. The new proof is, as Jared Duker Lichtman of Stanford University put it, “the most significant AI-for-math achievement so far, by quite a margin. Source

item.title: Jalen Hurts blood clot timeline: How Eagles QB went from controversial London start to being out for season
item.description: Jalen Hurts blood clot timeline: How Eagles QB went from controversial London start to being out for season originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Eagles are under fire for their handling of Jalen Hurts' latest diagnosis — one that is far more severe than typically seen in the sports world. On Monday, Philadelphia announced that its star quarterback was diagnosed with deep vein thrombosis. Scans discovered that the blood clot issue that affected Hurts in the lead-up to last week's game against the Rams had moved to his lungs. Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the season as a result of his diagnosis. Many are wondering how he and the Eagles got to this point. Concerns over Philadelphia's management of Hurts' ailment — including the decision to let him fly after discovering that he had a blood clot in his left calf — are scrawled across social media and message boards at present. With that, The Sporting News takes a look at the full timeline of Hurts' blood clot issue. MORE JALEN HURTS NEWS: What is a superficial blood clot? What to know about Jalen Hurts' recovery timeline Revisiting the blood clot issue that forced Chris Bosh to retire at 31 Philly's ongoing timeline of sports misery Jalen Hurts blood clot timeline Here's an exhaustive look at the timeline of Hurts' blood clot diagnosis, from its initial screening in his calf to the latest reports that clotting has been found in his lungs. Hurts request calf treatment - Thursday, Oct. 8 Hurts requested treatment on his calf after practice, explaining to Eagles staff that he was cleated in the calf during the Eagles prior game against the Rams. He was a full participant in practice in the lead-up to Philadelphia's matchup with the Jaguars in London. Hurts flies to London - Friday, Oct. 9 Hurts takes part in Eagles' final practice prior to the team's departure to London. He and his teammates board a flight to the English capital, arriving late Friday night. Hurts undergoes screening for calf - Saturday, Oct. 10 Hurts undergoes screening in London for calf issue. Specialists return with an initial diagnosis of left calf superficial vein thrombosis, per Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn. Per NFL Network's Ian Rapoport, Hurts was in the hospital until 4 a.m. BST Sunday morning. As part of the hospital's screening process, he was advised not to sleep, per Rapoport. Hurts stays awake roughly 36 hours before taking the field against Jacksonville, per The Ringer's Tom Pelissero. Doctors find that Hurts' blood clot had traveled up his bloodstream. He is advised to sit out the Eagles' Week 6 fixture against the Panthers . Hours before undergoing his scan, Hurts called his calf injury a "unique experience" while speaking with media. "I don't want to get into the details of leading up to the [Jacksonville] game and whatnot," Hurts said. (via: @MrUram) https://t.co/p8a2JeYgOP — SPORTSRADIO 94WIP (@SportsRadioWIP) October 14, 2026 Hurts' blood clot revealed - Thursday, Oct. 15 Philadelphia announces that Hurts will miss the Eagles' Week 6 clash with the Panthers, citing the results of the follow-up ultrasound as the reason for his absence. https://t.co/9SeK1XzYRL — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 15, 2026 "His health and safety are our highest priority," the organization declares. Per multiple reports, Hurts' blood clots moved to his longs. He'll miss the remainder of the year with the ailment, according to Rapoport. "He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations," the Eagles said in a statement. https://t.co/aBfyK55oxd — Philadelphia Eagles (@Eagles) October 19, 2026 The organization laid out Hurts' purported treatment plan, stating that their star quarterback will be placed on blood thinners. "Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery," Philadelphia said in a statement. "We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. ... We anticipate that he will have no long-term effects."

item.title: Simone Biles rocks all-white with 'football material' at Colts game
item.description: Simone Biles rocked an all-white look to support her husband, Indianapolis Colts safety Jonathan Owens. The gold medalist, 29, was spotted at Lucas Oil Stadium in a short-sleeved top and matching shorts at the Colts game against the Tennessee Titans on Sunday, Oct. 18. Similar to previous outfits, Biles added her beau's number, "38," in the middle of her shirt and "Owens" on the back of her bottoms. "We did the 38 and owens out of the football material & I'm obsessed," she wrote in her Instagram Stories. Biles also provided a closer look at her fall-coded ensemble. She wore a brown trench coat and leather boots with a mini Chanel purse. Simone Biles: Gold medalist promotes 'Skin to Believe In' so others won't feel embarrassed Biles continues to customize outfit with husband's number The customizations are reminiscent of her outfit at the Colts-Washington Commanders game in London earlier this month. Biles made a statement on the field with a stone-colored off-the-shoulder trench coat paired with a matching floor-length pencil skirt from PrettyLittleThing. She also added "38" and "Owens" to the look with shiny gems. In an interview with Us Magazine in September , Simone Biles spoke about being referred to as a WAG, a common term for the wife or girlfriend of a professional athlete. "It just doesn’t bother me because I know who I am and what I’ve accomplished outside of it," Biles told the outlet. She continued, "It doesn’t matter when somebody’s like, 'Oh, Simone’s one of the WAGs.' Don’t care. I know I’ve done great things on an Olympic level and for the mental health community, foster (care) community, all of this stuff. To me, it doesn’t seem derogatory because I know exactly who I am." Taylor Ardrey is a news reporter for USA TODAY. You can reach her at tardrey@usatodayco.com. This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Simone Biles rocks all-white with 'football material' at Colts game

item.title: ‘Tell Them No’ – Obi urges UK-based Nigerians to stop sending money home
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has urged Nigerians living in the United Kingdom to stop giving money to people in Nigeria who ask them for financial help, saying continued assistance may ease the effects of hardship without addressing its underlying causes. Obi attributed Nigeria’s economic hardship to poor leadership and argued that financial assistance does not address that problem, urging Nigerians in the diaspora to encourage their relatives and friends at home to vote for productive leaders. “You have people at home in Nigeria today who are begging you for money. Tell them no!” Obi said at a town hall meeting with diaspora supporters in Manchester on Sunday. He argued that people’s continued need for financial help was connected to the country’s economic difficulties, which he blamed on poor governance. In his view, sending money can cushion the hardship people face, but it does not resolve the problems that have left them seeking assistance. The former Anambra State governor also pointed to his record in public office, saying he had saved public funds during his tenure. He acknowledged that he was not perfect but argued that his record set him apart from other governors. “I’m not saying I’m a saint, but I saved money. I’ve not seen one governor who has saved 10 per cent of what I saved. No governor has done it,” Obi said. He further challenged other governors to match the savings he said he achieved while in office, saying, “I was not the only governor, and I challenge people if one governor can save 10 per cent of the money I saved, but there is nobody that did that.” The NDC presidential candidate further implored Nigerians to begin by supporting leaders they consider less corrupt. “Let’s start with this one that is less corrupt. That’s how other countries change,” he added. He also said his conversations with people reinforced the need for collective responsibility, adding that building a new Nigeria would require citizens to take an active role in addressing the country’s challenges. Obi urged Nigerians to take the 2027 election seriously, describing it as a critical moment for the country. The post ‘Tell Them No’ – Obi urges UK-based Nigerians to stop sending money home appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: How to enjoy Formula 1 race week in Austin without a ticket
item.description: Oracle Red Bull Racing driver Max Verstappen celebrates winning the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas on Sunday, Oct. 19, 2025 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Can you hear the engines revving, Austin? Race week is here, bringing celebrities like Post Malone and Adam Levine and drivers like Lewis Hamilton (cough, cough - can we get a Kim Kardashian cameo?) to town for Formula 1 at Circuit of the Americas. But even if you don't have a ticket to the action at the track, you can still get a taste of the luxurious, international vibe that comes with F1. Several teams are hosting free events around town and local bars are dressing up for the occasion. Here are a few ways to get in on the F1 fun. Oct. 19-24: Atlassian Williams F1 Team Austin fan zone Atlassian Williams Racing driver Carlos Sainz crests the turn 9 hill during qualifying for the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas on Saturday, Oct. 18, 2025 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) The Atlassian Williams F1 Team will host a six-day fan zone presented by Kraken on Congress Avenue featuring driver appearances, live question-and-answer sessions and interactive activities. Visitors can see a full-size F1 show car, try racing simulators and take part in a pit stop challenge. The event will include team merchandise and an Austin-themed Williams and Marvel comic. The event is free to attend with registration through the Williams app. Hours are 11 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Wednesday and 10 a.m. to 7 p.m. Thursday to Saturday. 800 Congress Ave. williamsf1.com/fan-zone . Oct. 22-25: Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS F1 Team fan hub Mercedes-AMG Petronas driver George Russell leads a group of cars into turn 13 during the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas on Sunday, Oct. 19, 2025 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Visitors can try changing tires on a real F1 car, drive racing simulators and explore a replica of the team's pit wall through a Meta AI activation. The hub will also have a 2026 Mercedes-AMG PETRONAS show car and the new Mercedes-AMG GT 4-Door Coupé. Local music acts, Texas food vendors, giveaways and an on-site merchandise store round out the experience. The event is free to attend. The hub is open from noon to 8:30 p.m. Thursday and Friday, 1:30 p.m. to 9 p.m. on Saturday and 10:30 a.m. to 7 p.m. on Sunday. Entry subject to venue capacity. 400 Congress Ave. mercedesamgf1.com. Oct. 22-25: Red Bull Austin Race Nights Oracle Red Bull driver Max Verstappen celebrates winning the Formula 1 United States Grand Prix at Circuit of the Americas on Sunday, Oct. 19, 2025 in Austin. (Aaron E. Martinez/Austin American-Statesman) Oracle Red Bull Racing and Visa Cash App Racing Bulls will host a four-day fan event featuring racing simulators, a pit stop challenge and a replica Formula One team garage. The event may also include appearances by drivers and surprise guest

item.title: Matthew Golden Keeps Rolling With Rare Packers Accomplishment Against Cowboys
item.description: After a challenging 2025 rookie season, Green Bay Packers wide receiver Matthew Golden is finally coming into his own. On Sunday, the former Texas Longhorns star wide receiver had yet another big performance, as he helped Green Bay take down the Dallas Cowboys in a 23-13 win at Lambeau Field in Green Bay . The 23-year-old Golden did not exactly have an efficient evening, catching only six of 13 targets from quarterback Jordan Love, but he still came away with 104 receiving yards and a touchdown on six receptions and 13 targets. He easily could have had a much bigger production to make his fantasy football owners even happier if not for a couple of drops on potential big plays. Nevertheless, Golden had a night. Matthew Golden Pulls Off Rare Achievement in Packers’ Week 6 Win Over The Cowboys Green Bay wide receiver Golden (0) is locked out of bound by Atlanta Falcons cornerback Billy Bowman Jr. (33) during the fourth quarter of their game Thursday, Sept. 24, 2026 at Lambeau Field in Green Bay, Wisconsin. Golden’s showing against the Cowboys gave him his second consecutive 100-yard outings. A week before, he posted 123 receiving yards on six receptions and seven targets during a 31-7 home win over the Chicago Bears. With his last two outings, Golden became the first Green Bay player to have such back-to-back performances. Via Underdog NFL on X : Matthew Golden last 4 games: 6-104-1 6-123-0 3-21-1 5-100-1 First Packers player with back-to-back 100+ receiving yard games within the same season since 2022. Matthew Golden now has 501 receiving yards and three touchdowns on 30 receptions through six games. He will look to sustain his form when Green Bay lock horns with the Detroit Lions at Ford Field in Detroit in Week 7. item.title: France wants curfews in some areas after weekend of riots
item.description: France's central government asked some local authorities to impose curfews and faced pressure over security failings on Monday after a weekend of riots and looting borne out of nationwide anti-government protests. Prime Minister Sebastien Lecornu did not rule out declaring state of emergency but said it was more appropriate for now to apply partial and localised curfews, without providing details of which cities would be affected.
item.dc:creator: FRANCE24

item.title: Is Mike Evans playing tonight? Injury update, fantasy advice for 49ers WR in Week 6
item.description: The San Francisco 49ers have a question mark on their hands at wide receiver with Mike Evans ahead of the Week 6 game against the Washington Commanders. Evans is dealing with a pair of injuries this week. Not only does he have the ribs issue he picked up in Week 4, but the veteran wideout had an Achilles injury added this week. The 33-year-old did not practice at all this past week before he was given the questionable tag on Saturday. Here’s everything we know when it comes to Evans’ chances of suiting up in the Week 6 game against the Commanders on Monday night. MORE: 3 best Commanders player prop bets for Week 6 vs. 49ers Is Mike Evans playing tonight? San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) during the second quarter against the Arizona Cardinals at Levi’s Stadium. Credit: Darren Yamashita-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) There is no concrete answer on Evans’ status yet, and according to Mercury News’ Cam Inman , he is “a game-time decision.” But at least two 49ers beat writers believe the veteran wide receiver is going to play. One of them is The San Francisco Standard’s David Lombardi . “Mike Evans officially listed as questionable but — again — seems based on my read of the situation that he’s on track to play,” Lombardi wrote on Saturday. And NBC Sports Bay Area’s Matt Maiocco agrees. MORE: NFL contenders and pretenders after Week 6 “At this point, I think Kyle Juszczyk and Mike Evans will play Monday night against Washington, and Nick Bosa will not,” said Maiocco. When a player doesn’t practice at all during the week, that usually means they are unlikely to play, even with a questionable tag. However, Evans is a different breed. With his wealth of experience, he does not need to practice during the week to play. We’ll know for sure what the deal is with Evans when the 49ers release their inactives an hour and a half before the 8:15 p.m. kickoff. Mike Evans fantasy advice San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Mike Evans (5) warms up prior to the game against the Miami Dolphins at Levi’s Stadium. Credit: Cary Edmondson-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Entering Week 5, Evans ranked as WR13 overall, according to Fantasy Pros , which puts him in the WR2 conversation. While Evans’ receiving yards production hasn’t been gaudy, he has scored three touchdowns to help pad his fantasy point total. The concern this week, of course, is that Evans won’t be at 100%, but that was the case last week and he had his best game of the season with 113 yards and a touchdown. Making Evans more attractive is the fact that he’s squaring off against a Commanders defense ceding the sixth-most fantasy points per game to wideouts this season, and the third-most touchdowns per contest. As long as he’s active, Evans should be in lineups. Verdict: Start — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories on The Big Lead —

item.title: France protests: Who are the people arrested during the unrest?
item.description: At least 2,400 people were arrested in France during protests over the weekend, some simply for being in the wrong place at the wrong time, others on suspicion of theft and looting. In an official address, French President Emmanuel Macron warned that “those who looted will have to pay for the damage”. But who exactly are these rioters?

item.title: Gattuso says courage helped his players embarrass Juventus
item.description: Gattuso says courage helped his players embarrass Juventus Lazio secured an impressive 3-0 victory over Juventus in Turin, with Gennaro Gattuso praising the courage shown by his players during the Serie A contest. The visitors delivered an effective performance at the Allianz Stadium, taking their opportunities and leaving the home side with plenty to consider after a disappointing defeat. Juventus had approached the match with confidence following their previous victory against Celta Vigo . However, the Bianconeri struggled to reproduce that form and were unable to make their opportunities count against a Lazio side that proved more effective in front of goal. Lazio show courage to defeat Juventus Juventus would have expected to compete strongly on home soil, but Lazio had other ideas. The visitors remained determined throughout the match, showing the resilience and conviction needed to secure all three points against a team with considerable quality in its squad. The Old Lady had opportunities to take control of the contest, but those chances ultimately went unconverted. As the match progressed, Lazio grew into the game and punished their opponents, turning what could have been a difficult evening into a convincing victory. Juventus also had to cope without Luciano Spalletti on the touchline. His absence did not help the situation, although the players still needed to demonstrate the quality and determination expected of them. Instead, they struggled to respond as Lazio maintained their momentum. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images) Gattuso praises Lazio’s mentality For Lazio, the result represented another encouraging performance in a season in which they have impressed. Juventus might have been expected to provide a stern test, but the visitors showed they were capable of handling the pressure and competing effectively away from home. Gattuso was pleased with the mentality his players displayed, particularly their willingness to endure difficult periods without losing their composure. Speaking via Tuttojuve , he highlighted the importance of their approach after the final whistle. “Courage, we didn’t get our arm today. We knew how to suffer, I really enjoyed this tonight.” Gattuso’s comments reflected his satisfaction with the way Lazio approached the contest. Their ability to withstand pressure and take advantage of their opportunities proved decisive against Juventus. For the Bianconeri, however, the defeat raises questions about their consistency and their ability to respond when matches become difficult. Spalletti will need his players to show greater determination in the coming weeks, as further disappointing results could increase the pressure on his position as manager.

item.title: Serie A official line-ups and live updates: Monza vs. Cagliari
item.description: Serie A official line-ups and live updates: Monza vs. Cagliari Dany Mota and Foe Ondoa come into the Monza side, while Cagliari pair M’Bala Nzola with Paul Mendy up front for their trip to the U-Power Stadium. It kicks off at 18:30 CET [17:30 BST] at the U-Power Stadium in Monza. Ivan Juric’s Monza have just four points from their first six games after their return to Serie A, with one win, one draw and four defeats. They lost 3-1 at Lazio last time out, and have conceded 15 goals, the second-worst defensive record in the division. Gustavo Varela has been the bright spot, scoring four goals in his first five Serie A appearances. Cagliari are one of the surprise packages of the season, with 13 points from six games, and are unbeaten in four. They held Juventus to a 1-1 draw last time out , but Fabio Pisacane is suspended after his touchline row with Luciano Spalletti, so assistant Giacomo Murelli takes his place on the bench. Daniel Maldini, who has four goals in six games, returns to face his former club. Juric has a strong record against the Sardinians, losing just one of his last nine Serie A meetings with them, with four wins and four draws. Monza are without the suspended Lorenzo Lucchesi, so Saba Goglichidze comes into the back three. Matteo Pessina, Idrissa Touré, Jan Ziolkowski, Zeballos and Mayé are all injured. Patrick Ciurria is back in the squad. Cagliari are missing Mattia Felici and Riyad Idrissi, both with cruciate ligament injuries, as well as Yael Trepy. Murelli pairs M’Bala Nzola with Paul Mendy up front, with Maldini behind them, while Yerry Mina edges captain Alessandro Deiola for a place in defence. MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Eddy Kouadio of Monza in action during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Monza vs. Cagliari – official line-ups Monza: Tornquist; Kouadio, Goglichidze, Carboni; Birindelli, Ondoa, Akinsammiro, Mangas; Robinson, Mota, Varela Coach: Juric Cagliari: Caprile; Ze Pedro, Mina, Rodriguez, Obert; Romano, Winks, Adopo; Maldini; Mendy, Nzola Coach: Murelli (Pisacane suspended)

Monza are without the suspended Lorenzo Lucchesi, so Saba Goglichidze comes into the back three. Matteo Pessina, Idrissa Touré, Jan Ziolkowski, Zeballos and Mayé are all injured. Patrick Ciurria is back in the squad. Cagliari are missing Mattia Felici and Riyad Idrissi, both with cruciate ligament injuries, as well as Yael Trepy. Murelli pairs M’Bala Nzola with Paul Mendy up front, with Maldini behind them, while Yerry Mina edges captain Alessandro Deiola for a place in defence. MONZA, ITALY – SEPTEMBER 18: Eddy Kouadio of Monza in action during the Serie A match between AC Monza and US Sassuolo at U-Power Stadium on September 18, 2026 in Monza, Italy. (Photo by Claudio Villa/Getty Images) Monza vs. Cagliari – official line-ups Monza: Tornquist; Kouadio, Goglichidze, Carboni; Birindelli, Ondoa, Akinsammiro, Mangas; Robinson, Mota, Varela Coach: Juric Cagliari: Caprile; Ze Pedro, Mina, Rodriguez, Obert; Romano, Winks, Adopo; Maldini; Mendy, Nzola Coach: Murelli (Pisacane suspended)

item.title: Colts reportedly called Peyton Manning after firing Chris Ballard for GM job
item.description: Colts reportedly called Peyton Manning after firing Chris Ballard for GM job originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Indianapolis Colts just lost to the Tennessee Titans in Week 6 of the 2026 NFL season. The 2-3 Colts drop to 2-4, and the 0-5 Titans improve to 1-5. Following such a brutal loss for the Colts, they made a big change, firing general manager Chris Ballard. The 10th year GM was fired, and now the Colts are looking for a new leader of this franchise. According to Dan Patrick on The Dan Patrick Show , the Colts have reportedly made quite an interesting call already. One source told Patrick that Peyton Manning is a name to watch, as he's already been called about the GM opening. Colts call Peyton Manning about GM opening after Chris Ballard's firing "The Colts' first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning. The call will not only get names and suggestions, but the call will explore whether or not Peyton would be interested in a general manager for the Colts as the entry point that would include ownership interest in the Colts," Patrick shared. "The Colts' first call will be/has been to Peyton Manning." — DP shares what his source has told him. https://t.co/MgTbuJIxhW — Dan Patrick Show (@dpshow) October 19, 2026 This report from Patrick is a very interesting one, and it's a whole lot more fascinating than simply hearing that the Colts will be calling Manning about the opening. While there seems to be interest from the Colts in bringing Manning in as the team's general manager, they're also looking to get advice from the Hall of Famer on the GM opening. MORE : Colts fans are calling for Daniel Jones benching after ugly Titans loss But in their pitch to hire Manning, they're rumored to be offering Manning a partial ownership stake in the Colts, which would be quite an interesting situation for the former Colts QB. Manning is still very much involved in the NFL world and could play a similar role to what Tom Brady is doing right now with the Las Vegas Raiders , acting as a key figure in the front office while also working for FOX on an NFL broadcast. Taking over GM duties would likely take Manning away from his ESPN work, as he'd need to focus on helping the team out, similar to what Matt Ryan is doing with the Atlanta Falcons . Either way, regardless of what Manning decides to do, this report from Patrick indicates the Colts still very much place a lot of value on Manning's thoughts, enough to potentially hire him as their new GM after nearly a decade with Ballard in control. item.title: Lord of the Rings Director Says He’s Finally Making His Tintin Sequel
item.description: Tintin fans have been in the wilderness for quite some time. After the Steven Spielberg-directed The Adventures of Tintin hit theaters in 2011, Spielberg and producer Peter Jackson confirmed that a sequel was on the way. This follow-up was originally promised for sometime in 2014 or 2015, with Jackson directing. Needless to say, that didn’t happen.
item.dc:creator: Elijah Gonzalez

item.title: Vote for Seacoast boys, girls Athletes of the Week for Oct. 12-17
item.description: Welcome to the seventh installment of Seacoast high school Athletes of the Week for the 2026 fall sports season. This week, and in weeks to come, you can vote for a girls athlete and a boys athlete of the week. This week's polls are for outstanding athletic accomplishments from Oct. 12-17. How do I cast my vote? Voting can be completed through the two ballots listed below. Voting closes at midnight Thursday, Oct. 22. How do we learn who wins? Winners will be announced in a story published Friday, Oct. 23 at seacoastonline.com/sports and fosters.com/sports . May I nominate for future ballots? Yes. Nominate a Seacoast high school athlete by sending an email to sports@seacoastonline.com. Feel free to send us a photo of the athlete, too. BOYS ATHLETE OF THE WEEK NOMINEES Nils Anderson, Dover, cross country Anderson placed second with a time of 17 minutes 45 seconds to help lead Dover to a three-team meet win over Portsmouth and Newmarket on Friday, Oct. 16. Nick Costa, Exeter, soccer Costa scored two goals in Exeter's 5-1 Division I win over Keene on Monday, Oct. 12. Costa also scored a goal in Exeter's 3-0 win over Windham on Wednesday, Oct. 14. Johnny Granger, Winnacunnet, soccer Granger scored three goals and had two assists in Winnacunnet's 10-1 Division I win over Spaulding on Wednesday, Oct. 16. Noah Moore, Portsmouth/Oyster River, football Moore had two touchdowns catches in Portsmouth/Oyster River's 49-0 Division I win over Dover on Friday, Oct. 15. Brendan Taylor, Marshwood, soccer Taylor scored the game's lone goal in Marshwood's 1-0 win over Windham on Saturday, Oct. 17. GIRLS ATHLETE OF THE WEEK NOMINEES Natalie McCormack, Portsmouth, cross country McCormack place second with a time of 22:10.6 to help Portsmouth to a three-team meet win over Dover and Newmarket on Friday, Oct. 16. Ari Moulton, Newmarket, soccer Moulton scored two goals in Newmarket's 4-0 Division IV win over Holy Family on Thursday, Oct. 15. Emma Roeder, Exeter, soccer Roeder scored two goals in Exeter's 6-0 Division I win over Nashua South on Thursday, Oct. 15. Roeder also recorded an assist in Exeter's 3-0 win over Windham on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Nora Simmons, Winnacunnet, volleyball Simmons recorded 19 kills and had four aces in Winnacunnet's 3-1 Division I win over Nashua North on Thursday, Oct. 15. She had 11 kills and four digs in Winnacunnet's 3-0 win over Spaulding on Tuesday, Oct. 13. Sylvie Wamberg, Portsmouth Christian Academy, soccer Wamberg scored three goals in Portsmouth Christian Academy's 5-0 Division IV win over Sunapee on Wednesday, Oct. 14. She scored one goal and had two assists in PCA's 7-0 Division IV win over Mount Royal on Friday, Oct. 16. This article originally appeared on Portsmouth Herald: Vote for Seacoast boys, girls Athletes of the Week for Oct. 12-17

item.title: So was LeBron James overrated? We asked that question on our cover in 2003, and we have our answer
item.description: So was LeBron James overrated? We asked that question on our cover in 2003, and we have our answer originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Twenty-three years ago, before he had ever suited up for an NBA game, Sporting News posed a question on its cover that has lived on in infamy —Is LeBron James overrated? Our 2003 cover pops up on social media every so often and is sure to trigger a viral response every time. Over the course of his career, LeBron has gone 23-0 against us. Entering Year 24 and his first with the Sixers , it is looking like he will only add to the longest active winning streak in the league. King James has more than lived up to his draft hype coming out of high school, breaking a plethora of records and putting forth a compelling argument as the greatest of all time. And he's still pretty good at the age of 41. While he's no longer the best player in the league, we still have him firmly in the top 25 in our top 150 starter rankings . We've written hundreds of positive things about LeBron over the ensuing years, but that spicy headline is the one that probably gets remembered the most. With his career winding down, now is as good a time as ever to look back at how much crow we deserve to eat, along with what exactly LeBron did to make all of his doubters look bad. MORE: SN's expert predictions on 2027 NBA champs, MVP, and more The headline that oversold the story Here are two inside baseball tidbits about how headlines work across news. Betteridge's law of headlines is an adage that was created in 2009 by Ian Betteridge, a British technology journalist. His observation noted that any headline which ends in a question mark can be answered by the word no. That certainly applied to our LeBron headline, "Is LeBron James overrated?" The second thing to know about headlines is that oftentimes it's an editor rather than the writer who came up with it. Bob Hille, who is still with Sporting News as a Senior Editorial Consultant, was a part of the headline-writing process for the story back in 2003. "I feel bad for [writer Sean Deveney] because the cover oversold what the story was about," Hille said. "We brainstormed cover lines to be both honest and provocative to stand out on newsstands. In GOAT hindsight, we probably leaned too hard into provocative. Or put another way: Is LeBron overrated? Um, no." MORE: Best NBA power forwards for 2026-27: Ranking all 30 starters When our story came out, the LeBron hype machine had been in full force for over a year. Sports Illustrated had called him "The Chosen One" on their cover 15 months earlier, when he was still a junior at St. Vincent–St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio. item.content:encoded: So was LeBron James overrated? We asked that question on our cover in 2003, and we have our answer originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Twenty-three years ago, before he had ever suited up for an NBA game, Sporting News posed a question on its cover that has lived on in infamy —Is LeBron James overrated? Our 2003 cover pops up on social media every so often and is sure to trigger a viral response every time. Over the course of his career, LeBron has gone 23-0 against us. Entering Year 24 and his first with the Sixers , it is looking like he will only add to the longest active winning streak in the league. King James has more than lived up to his draft hype coming out of high school, breaking a plethora of records and putting forth a compelling argument as the greatest of all time. And he's still pretty good at the age of 41. While he's no longer the best player in the league, we still have him firmly in the top 25 in our top 150 starter rankings . We've written hundreds of positive things about LeBron over the ensuing years, but that spicy headline is the one that probably gets remembered the most. With his career winding down, now is as good a time as ever to look back at how much crow we deserve to eat, along with what exactly LeBron did to make all of his doubters look bad. MORE: SN's expert predictions on 2027 NBA champs, MVP, and more The headline that oversold the story Here are two inside baseball tidbits about how headlines work across news. Betteridge's law of headlines is an adage that was created in 2009 by Ian Betteridge, a British technology journalist. His observation noted that any headline which ends in a question mark can be answered by the word no. That certainly applied to our LeBron headline, "Is LeBron James overrated?" The second thing to know about headlines is that oftentimes it's an editor rather than the writer who came up with it. Bob Hille, who is still with Sporting News as a Senior Editorial Consultant, was a part of the headline-writing process for the story back in 2003. "I feel bad for [writer Sean Deveney] because the cover oversold what the story was about," Hille said. "We brainstormed cover lines to be both honest and provocative to stand out on newsstands. In GOAT hindsight, we probably leaned too hard into provocative. Or put another way: Is LeBron overrated? Um, no." MORE: Best NBA power forwards for 2026-27: Ranking all 30 starters When our story came out, the LeBron hype machine had been in full force for over a year. Sports Illustrated had called him "The Chosen One" on their cover 15 months earlier, when he was still a junior at St. Vincent–St. Mary High School in Akron, Ohio. Instead of focusing on LeBron, Deveney, a long-time Sporting News NBA expert who now writes for Heavy.com, wanted to shed some light on the other top prospects in that draft. "There was never any doubt that LeBron was going to be the No. 1 pick, but there were legitimate people (as I recall, Chad Ford of ESPN was among them, as well as a scout, Tony Ronzone) who were saying that Carmelo Anthony and/or Darko Milicic could be just as good if not better," Deveney told me via email. "And that was my focus was comparing those two to the hype and circumstances that surrounded LeBron." "Obviously, Darko was a bust, there's no other way to say it. But Anthony was at least close to equal with James by most measures in his first season." Before you kill Deveney for thinking that Milicic was a top prospect, keep in mind that Pistons ' GM Joe Dumars validated his intel by taking Milicic No. 2 in the draft a month later. MORE: Can 76ers win title with LeBron James? What needs to go right, what could go wrong in Philadelphia Imagn Images What we (and others) got wrong about LeBron James in 2003 How could anyone have doubted LeBron's future success? He was a legendary high school player that sold out arenas and consistently dominated under the brightest lights. It didn't take a professional scout to see that he was a man among boys. But he did have some legitimate weaknesses in his game. "Two aspects of James's game the most often questioned are his shooting and defense," Deveney wrote back in 2003. "His shot is subpar, and because of that, he probably will struggle early in his career. He must work on it." That shooting critique turned out to be somewhat right, until it wasn't. LeBron was a good-not-great 3-point shooter in high school, connecting on 36.0 percent of his attempts. As a rookie in the NBA, he shot just 29.0 percent from 3. He was so transcendent at everything else that his lack of shooting didn't hold him back, with the exception of some key moments. MORE: LeBron James high school stats, records foreshadowed NBA GOAT career During the 2007 Finals, Gregg Popovich's Spurs team swept LeBron's Cavs by taking advantage of that shooting weakness. Pop told his players to sag off LeBron, resulting in him shooting just 4-of-20 from 3. LeBron's shaky outside shooting showed up again in 2013, when Popovich used that same strategy against the Heat . Again, LeBron's team lost the series. LeBron was able to prolong his career and win several rings in part by becoming much better as a perimeter shooter. Through his first eight seasons, LeBron hit just 32.9 percent from deep. He hit 35.9 percent of his 3's from Year Nine onward, and topped over 40 percent from deep twice. Sagging off from LeBron is no longer a viable strategy. In particular, the pull-up 3 has become a real weapon for him. He deserves a ton of credit for working hard at that aspect of his game to transform a weakness into a strength. MORE: 'He is insane at Madden': LeBron James opponent explains NBA legend's world-class skill in NFL video game The other question mark about LeBron surrounded his defense. As Deveney wrote, "He never had to play the defensive stopper's role against someone with comparable skills, so his defense is an unknown, not a negative. He has the tools to become a very good defender, just as Garnett, Bryant, and McGrady have." Deveney's assessment doesn't look bad, even with the advantage of over two decades of hindsight. It is extremely difficult to project defense from a 17-year-old. But Deveney saw a Kevin Garnett-level of potential, and LeBron delivered. LeBron hasn't been a plus defender over the last several seasons. For most of his career though, he was elite, making six All-Defensive teams. Defensive Player of the Year is the one major award that has eluded him, but he has finished runner-up twice and has seven top-10 finishes in his career. He will go down as a remarkable two-way force. Perhaps the most iconic play of LeBron's career was his chase-down block in Game 7 of the 2015 NBA Finals, helping to win the game and title in dramatic fashion for the Cavs. MORE: SN 140 Moments: No. 10 - LeBron James blocks shot to propel Cleveland to first NBA title Our misses on LeBron do not look nearly as bad as our headline suggests. There were some admittedly tougher looks though when it came to Milicic, who averaged 6.0 points per game over a 10-year journeyman's career. "You'd have to work out all three, at least, to compare them," one college scout told Deveney. "And my best guess is that it would be close, but James might not come out on top." Scouts weren't the only ones to get it wrong. Scootie Penn, a former Ohio State point guard and European pro who was quoted in Deveney's story, was about as far off as possible. "He's the real deal," Penn said of Milicic. "I have seen LeBron, and I have played against Darko. It's a tough call, but Darko is a legit 7-footer who can shoot the ball. He is tough and he is only 17. It's hard to describe the kid unless you see him." While LeBron's maturity and future work ethic were questioned at the time, it was actually Milicic who fell victim to those pitfalls. He later admitted that he lacked the discipline and emotion

item.title: Masai Ujiri tells an outrageous story about LeBron James' unique work ethic
item.description: Masai Ujiri tells an outrageous story about LeBron James' unique work ethic originally appeared on The Sporting News . Add The Sporting News as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Masai Ujiri might be with the Denver Nuggets now, but he still has memories of what LeBron James did to his Toronto Raptors team in the 2010s. It was a decade when the Eastern Conference was dominated by James, as he made the NBA Finals from 2011 all the way to 2018 with two teams. However, it was during his second stint with the Cleveland Cavaliers that he dominated against Ujiri's team. It got so bad that Toronto became known as LeBronto by people in NBA circles. Masai Ujiri recalls his experience seeing LeBron James work out As the architect of the Raptors teams in the 2010s, it was tough to have awesome regular season campaigns be shot down by James in the postseason. It became so bad that people have forgotten all of those impressive Raptors seasons. LeBron was truly the dominant force in the Eastern Conference back then. That notion was further strengthened when he left the East to play for the Los Angeles Lakers . In the first year he was not in the East, the Raptors won the championship in 2019. MORE: Kevin Love goes viral for taking a shot at Kyle Lowry's Raptors getting dominated by LeBron James Since then, Ujiri has had many memories involving James. However, he has told a story about how he was impressed by seeing James work out early in the morning, which was a glimpse into what makes him such a good player. "LeBron was in the gym, running on a treadmill backwards, and his trainers were not even there yet. It's 5:30 in the morning; what is happening here? His guys come, and he does this incredible workout for an hour and a half, and that's not in front of anybody," Ujiri said about James' work ethic while on One 4 Africa . "What he does with himself in preparation, his mindset, and how much he loves this game. I got my ass kicked by that guy, I hated that guy with a passion." That early morning was proof that Ujiri needed to know that he was facing off against one of the greatest players in NBA history. Even if he's 41 now with the Philadelphia 76ers , he is likely working out like that, which should still spell trouble for the rest of the league. item.title: NEWS ALERT: Jalen Hurts to Miss the Rest of the Season; Fantasy Football Shockwaves Felt Across the Eagles' Offense
item.description: Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) before kick off against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Philadelphia Eagles Fantasy Fallout: What Jalen Hurts' Absence Means for McKee, Smith, Barkley, Goedert, Lemon, and Wicks The latest news on Jalen Hurts out of Philadelphia has immediately changed the fantasy landscape. With Hurts expected to miss the remainder of the season due to multiple blood clots in his lungs, the Eagles' offense enters an entirely new era. While reports indicate Hurts is clinically stable, fantasy implications pale in comparison to a full, healthy recovery. Our thoughts are entirely with Hurts, wishing him the absolute best and a safe return to health. Jalen Hurts will be out for the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. pic.twitter.com/PYfJpO16FS - Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 19, 2026 With Hurts' health as the main priority, we are here to talk about fantasy sports, so let's take a look at how the Eagles' offense will undergo a massive shift with this news . Here's what the data and recent sample sizes tell us about how the offense will function moving forward without Jalen Hurts, and what it means for fantasy football managers. Fantasy Football Implications on Eagles Offense Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee (16) under center against the Carolina Panthers during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tanner McKee: The New Signal-Caller With Hurts sidelined, the keys to the offense belong to Tanner McKee. With Hurts out against the Panthers this past week, McKee stepped in and completed 26-of-45 passes for 215 yards and a touchdown. From a fantasy perspective, McKee slots in best as a low-end QB2 or a matchup-based streaming option in Superflex leagues, and is available on the waiver wire in most leagues. He operates primarily as a traditional pocket passer rather than the high-impact dual-threat weapon Hurts is. item.content:encoded: Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) before kick off against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Philadelphia Eagles Fantasy Fallout: What Jalen Hurts' Absence Means for McKee, Smith, Barkley, Goedert, Lemon, and Wicks The latest news on Jalen Hurts out of Philadelphia has immediately changed the fantasy landscape. With Hurts expected to miss the remainder of the season due to multiple blood clots in his lungs, the Eagles' offense enters an entirely new era. While reports indicate Hurts is clinically stable, fantasy implications pale in comparison to a full, healthy recovery. Our thoughts are entirely with Hurts, wishing him the absolute best and a safe return to health. Jalen Hurts will be out for the season after doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs. pic.twitter.com/PYfJpO16FS - Adam Schefter (@AdamSchefter) October 19, 2026 With Hurts' health as the main priority, we are here to talk about fantasy sports, so let's take a look at how the Eagles' offense will undergo a massive shift with this news . Here's what the data and recent sample sizes tell us about how the offense will function moving forward without Jalen Hurts, and what it means for fantasy football managers. Fantasy Football Implications on Eagles Offense Oct 18, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee (16) under center against the Carolina Panthers during the second quarter at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Tanner McKee: The New Signal-Caller With Hurts sidelined, the keys to the offense belong to Tanner McKee. With Hurts out against the Panthers this past week, McKee stepped in and completed 26-of-45 passes for 215 yards and a touchdown. From a fantasy perspective, McKee slots in best as a low-end QB2 or a matchup-based streaming option in Superflex leagues, and is available on the waiver wire in most leagues. He operates primarily as a traditional pocket passer rather than the high-impact dual-threat weapon Hurts is. While McKee isn't the caliber of fantasy player that Hurts is, his willingness to distribute the ball keeps the chains moving enough to sustain key pass-catchers, and may actually boost their fantasy value. DeVonta Smith: A Silver Lining If there is a clear winner from McKee taking over under center, it is wide receiver DeVonta Smith. McKee heavily locked onto Smith in the loss to the Panthers, peppering him with a team-high 14 targets. Smith capitalized on the volume, turning those looks into 7 receptions for 75 yards and a touchdown. While a 14-target sample size is small and bound to show some regression, it suggests immediate, tangible chemistry between the two. Unlike many backup quarterback situations where receiver values plummet, Smith's floor feels remarkably secure. McKee's clear trust in his premier weapon keeps Smith firmly locked in as a reliable fantasy WR2 with potential WR1 upside. Saquon Barkley: A Stacked-Box Downgrade For star running back Saquon Barkley, the loss of Hurts changes the defensive math entirely. Opponents no longer have to respect the threat of the Tush Push or account for Hurts keeping the ball on read-options. Without that dynamic element, defenses can afford to cheat closer to the line of scrimmage and load the box against Barkley. When healthy, Barkley remains an elite, game-breaking talent. However, his efficiency could face heavy resistance if McKee and the passing game cannot consistently keep secondaries honest. Fantasy managers should anticipate a slight dip in yards-per-carry efficiency, though Barkley's high-volume workload ensures he remains an absolute mandatory weekly starter (though he's probably more of an RB2 when he's back from his hamstring injury). Dallas Goedert: Stability in the Intermediate Game With a traditional pocket passer like McKee orchestrating the offense, tight end Dallas Goedert stands to benefit from a steady diet of short-to-intermediate routes. Goedert has been a reliable safety valve throughout his career, and backup-to-starter transitions usually correlate with an uptick in quick, underneath throws to mitigate pass-rush pressure. He was solid with McKee under center and is coming off one of his best games of the season with six catches for 61 yards. With eight targets in Week 6, Goedert's baseline target volume should keep him safely inside the TE1/TE2 fringe conversation. Makai Lemon & Dontayvion Wicks: Expanding the Supporting Cast The shifting target distribution also brings rookie first-rounder Makai Lemon and trade addition Dontayvion Wicks into sharper fantasy focus. As an explosive weapon with immense upside, Makai Lemon's fantasy utility depends on how quickly McKee can build a rapport with the young wideout. While a run-heavy or conservative game plan could limit vertical opportunities, any expansion of three-receiver sets under McKee elevates Lemon to a high-upside stash in deeper leagues. Dontayvion Wicks has shown flashes of efficiency and route-running savvy, making him a fascinating piece in this evolving receiver room. In deeper formats or standard leagues tracking secondary targets, Wicks becomes a speculative waiver wire monitor to see if McKee's distribution patterns extend past the primary read. item.title: ‘Going to be difficult’ – Andoni Iraola suggests Liverpool ace could miss at least six games
item.description: ‘Going to be difficult’ – Andoni Iraola suggests Liverpool ace could miss at least six games Andoni Iraola has indicated that one Liverpool player could now miss at least the Reds’ next six matches after being struck down by injury. The glee at coming from behind to win 2-1 at Brentford on Saturday was tempered by injuries to Dominik Szoboszlai (who’d just returned after missing the previous two games with a hamstring problem) and Jeremie Frimpong (forced off just seven minutes after coming on at half-time). Recovery time for the pair is minimal, with the Merseysiders back in action once more against Villarreal in the Champions League tomorrow night, and the head coach has now shared updates on both players ahead of that fixture. Iraola gives injury updates on Frimpong and Szoboszlai Iraola is expecting the Dutch right-back to miss Liverpool’s upcoming fixtures this side of the November international window, saying (via liverpoolfc.com ): “Jeremie Frimpong is obviously a new muscle injury and it happened, I think, in the second or third minute he was playing. “It’s difficult to predict and we will have to wait until he recovers, but it’s going to be difficult, I think, before the [November international] break. We will try but it’s going to be difficult to have him.” (Photo by Alexander Hassenstein/Getty Images) There was better news on the Hungarian midfielder at least as the head coach said: “Dom Szoboszlai is different. It’s not a new injury, I think it’s in the same place it was probably last week. He hasn’t worsened the injury but probably we have to be a little bit more patient until he recovers fully. “It’s not like something now where he has to wait a lot of time to come back. He is more or less in the same situation he was last week, but we need more patience with him.” Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Frimpong can’t seem to catch a break It’s easy to say in hindsight, of course, but there’s a sense that Szoboszlai was rushed back for the Brentford game on Saturday after missing the two previous matches, and it seems from Iraola’s update that Liverpool’s number 8 won’t be available to face Villarreal tomorrow night. At least the subsequent fixture against Brighton isn’t until next Sunday, so that might hopefully give the midfielder enough time to recover and see if he’s fit enough to feature against the in-form Seagulls. (Photo by Julian Finney/Getty Images) Unfortunately, Frimpong is set to miss all six of the Reds’ matches before the November international window , with the earliest we can expect to see him back in action being the visit of Manchester United to Anfield in five weeks’ time. The Dutchman endured an injury-plagued first season on Merseyside and then lost his place to Ronald Araujo in the early weeks of this campaign, and his abortive outing against Brentford summed up his luckless time with Liverpool thus far. It’s far from ideal that the Reds’ casualty list is increasing in tandem with the fixture workload, and the latter isn’t going to ease up any time soon.

item.title: Seahawks host Chiefs on Sunday Night Football, tickets start at $350
item.description: Sunday Night Football this weekend is set to be a battle between two of the last three Super Bowl champions when the Seattle Seahawks host the Kansas City Chiefs . The Seahawks are looking to erase their loss from last Thursday after quarterback Sam Darnold tossed two interceptions against the Denver Broncos, which dropped them to 3-3. SHOP: Seattle Seahawks vs. Kansas City Chiefs Sunday Night Football tickets Kansas City remains undefeated through five weeks following a 22-6 win over the LA Chargers last Sunday as former Seahawks Super Bowl MVP Kenneth Walker III rushed for over 120 yards and two touchdowns. Seattle looks to remain above .500 while Walker eyes a revenge game against his former team, making it a must-see matchup in prime time. Tickets are still available , and below you'll learn more about how to buy them.
