item.title: Should NFL reconsider its European, worldwide game scheduling in light of recent issues?
item.description: The NFL ‘s worldwide game scheduling could come under additional scrutiny as two situations are in the news. One involves Jalen Hurts’ health which seemingly worsened around the time he flew to and from London for the Eagles game in Week 5. The other is surrounding the civil unrest in Paris, France, site of a Week 7 game. The 2026 season is the first time the NFL has hosted nine games outside of the United States spanning four continents and seven countries. American football has been well received in these stadiums around the world,. However, the inherent risks may not make it worth the rewards. MORE: Eagles’ gross Jalen Hurts blood clot negligence highlighted by NFL insider Jalen Hurts Sep 11, 2026; Melbourne, Victoria, Australia; San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy (13) throws the ball against the Los Angeles Rams during the 2026 NFL Melbourne Game at Melbourne Cricket Ground. Mandatory Credit: Kirby Lee-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts flew to and from London and played a game within a 50 hour time span. At the time, fans did not know he was hospitalized prior to the flight and sleep-deprived. Flying 14 hours round trip with a blood clot is not conducive to anyone’s health, especially a professional athlete playing a contact sport. Perhaps some will say Hurts’ situation is a fluke and should not be enough to derail the NFL’s expansion plans. MORE: Rams’ Sean McVay makes feelings on Australia clear after 49ers loss Unrest in Paris, France The league has a Week 7 game betwen the Pittsburgh Steelers and New Orleans Saints scheduled for October 26 in Paris, France. Boomer Esiason is among those concerned about the health and safety of the players in France where civil unrest has been a significant problem. Rioting and looting are occurring on a daily basis. Over the weekend, Paris’ Louvre Museum was forced to close as protesters created a blockade around it. As Esiason put it, the best way to trigger more unrest is to host an NFL game in the area. "If you want to amplify your unrest, the best way to do it would be around an NFL football game in France." – Boomer Esiason pic.twitter.com/9MT3ZYWFRz — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 19, 2026 Given the circumstances, it would not be surprising to hear from the NFL Players’ Association on this issue in the near future. — Enjoy free coverage of the top news & trending stories with The Big Lead Newsletter —

item.title: ‘Can have a similar effect to being drunk’: Sports doctor questions how Jalen Hurts was allowed to play after being hospitalized
item.description: Oct 4, 2026; Philadelphia, Pennsylvania, USA; Philadelphia Eagles quarterback Jalen Hurts (1) before kick off against the Los Angeles Rams at Lincoln Financial Field. Mandatory Credit: Bill Streicher-Imagn Images The Philadelphia Eagles turned to Tanner McKee in place of star quarterback Jalen Hurts for Sunday’s game against the Carolina Panthers after the team revealed that he has been dealing with a blood clot in his calf. Although there was initially optimism that Hurts could return sooner rather than later, he was ultimately placed on IR, forcing him to miss at least the next four games, including Sunday’s loss to the Carolina Panthers. However, on Monday, the Eagles took things a step further, announcing that Hurts would miss the remainder of the season as he undergoes treatment via blood thinners. “Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition,” the Eagles said via statement. “Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e., blood thinners’). ESPN’s Ian Rapoport followed up the statement wth more details surrounding the timeline of events. “ Eagles QB Jalen Hurts, who is out for the season after several blood clots were revealed in his lungs, has been undergoing tests for days,” he reported on Monday. “Before the London game, Hurts was in the hospital until 4 am and did not sleep because sleep was a risk. He played without having slept.” Brian Sutterer, a sports doctor, couldn’t believe the Eagles’ decision to still play Hurts despite him not having slept on doctors’ orders, something he said “makes zero sense.” “Ok this part makes zero sense and now I do question why he played after seeing this part of the report. That much sleep deprivation can have a similar effect to being drunk in terms of awareness and neuromuscular control,” Sutterer posted on X. Ok this part makes zero sense and now I do question why he played after seeing this part of the report. That much sleep deprivation can have a similar effect to being drunk in terms of awareness and neuromuscular control. There’s nothing inherently dangerous about sleeping while having a superficial clot. Immobility (venous stasis) can cause clots to get worse, but that’s why you are often advised to just sleep with the leg elevated. I’ve NEVER heard of someone being told to avoid sleep after a superficial blood clot diagnosis and the short term effect of that sleep deprivation is a terrible thing to play football with. — Brian Sutterer MD (@BrianSuttererMD) October 19, 2026 “There’s nothing inherently

item.title: Stafford Rangers awaiting another bumper Cup crowd
item.description: Stafford Rangers chief executive Dave Smith smiles at the prospect of another 3,000 crowd at Marston Road [Stafford Rangers FC] Stafford Rangers are awaiting another "bumper crowd" at their Marston Road home for Tuesday's home FA Cup fourth qualifying round replay with National League strugglers Gateshead. The Staffordshire side, a powerhouse of non-league football in the 1970s when they twice won the FA Trophy, were founder members when the English football authorities introduced the Alliance Premier as their first fifth tier in 1979. Rangers, where Stan Collymore began his career and both Steve Bull and Andy Mutch managed, have fallen on hard times since those days and are now in the eighth tier and fifth in the Northern Premier League Division One West. But, having held Gateshead 1-1 up in the north-east on Saturday, they will be into the first round of the Cup for the first time in 20 years if they can complete the job and win the replay on Tuesday night. They have already attracted 3,000 crowds twice in this Cup run - and would like to go even higher. "The limit is currently 3,130," Stafford Rangers chief executive David Smith told BBC Radio Stoke. "That is the maximum we could get in. But we have got a meeting with the local council to see if we can increase that number. "Whatever happens, it will be 3,000 crowds three games running - and that's massive. For the club, financially, it's superb. But the big thing is what it's doing for the town. "There is a real buzz about Stafford. Tickets are selling so quick it's unbelievable." Four sides reach round one of FA Cup for first time "We've now hit a problem that, with Gateshead being a Step One side, we're not allowed to sell beer on the pitchside. "But we'll be organised. We'll find a solution. We'll make sure everybody is fed and watered properly." The last time Stafford Rangers got to this stage was 2020 when they lost 4-1 at home to Skelmersdale United. But manager Graham Deakin is convinced that his side can go one better. "I'm proud that we've gone up there and competed with a Step One side, but I'm just disappointed that we didn't win. We were told by so many that we should have done. That's testimony to the confidence we have created, that we could go up there to Gateshead, get a result and still be disappointed. But, back at Marston Road in front of a bumper crowd, let's see what happens." Tuesday's replay comes after Monday evening's televised draw so Rangers will know the identity of their opponents. When asked who he would like to face, Deakin reluctantly said: "Sheffield Wednesday or Leicester away probably, but really my attention is devoted only to making sure my team are up for it again on Tuesday night."
item.content:encoded: Stafford Rangers chief executive Dave Smith smiles at the prospect of another 3,000 crowd at Marston Road [Stafford Rangers FC] Stafford Rangers are awaiting another "bumper crowd" at their Marston Road home for Tuesday's home FA Cup fourth qualifying round replay with National League strugglers Gateshead. The Staffordshire side, a powerhouse of non-league football in the 1970s when they twice won the FA Trophy, were founder members when the English football authorities introduced the Alliance Premier as their first fifth tier in 1979. Rangers, where Stan Collymore began his career and both Steve Bull and Andy Mutch managed, have fallen on hard times since those days and are now in the eighth tier and fifth in the Northern Premier League Division One West. But, having held Gateshead 1-1 up in the north-east on Saturday, they will be into the first round of the Cup for the first time in 20 years if they can complete the job and win the replay on Tuesday night. They have already attracted 3,000 crowds twice in this Cup run - and would like to go even higher. "The limit is currently 3,130," Stafford Rangers chief executive David Smith told BBC Radio Stoke. "That is the maximum we could get in. But we have got a meeting with the local council to see if we can increase that number. "Whatever happens, it will be 3,000 crowds three games running - and that's massive. For the club, financially, it's superb. But the big thing is what it's doing for the town. "There is a real buzz about Stafford. Tickets are selling so quick it's unbelievable." Four sides reach round one of FA Cup for first time "We've now hit a problem that, with Gateshead being a Step One side, we're not allowed to sell beer on the pitchside. "But we'll be organised. We'll find a solution. We'll make sure everybody is fed and watered properly." The last time Stafford Rangers got to this stage was 2020 when they lost 4-1 at home to Skelmersdale United. But manager Graham Deakin is convinced that his side can go one better. "I'm proud that we've gone up there and competed with a Step One side, but I'm just disappointed that we didn't win. We were told by so many that we should have done. That's testimony to the confidence we have created, that we could go up there to Gateshead, get a result and still be disappointed. But, back at Marston Road in front of a bumper crowd, let's see what happens." Tuesday's replay comes after Monday evening's televised draw so Rangers will know the identity of their opponents. When asked who he would like to face, Deakin reluctantly said: "Sheffield Wednesday or Leicester away probably, but really my attention is devoted only to making sure my team are up for it again on Tuesday night."

item.title: Larson’s Phoenix Tire Failure Cut a 49-Point Chase Lead to 5
item.description: Kyle Larson arrived at Phoenix with a 49-point cushion. He left with five. A slow car was part of it, but the decisive piece was a right-front tire, and his crew chief has said the team ran the air pressure too low. Tyler Reddick won the Freeway Insurance 500, but the result that rewrote the Chase is a 34th-place finish worth three points. Confirmed vs. analysis: everything in the first sections below comes from NASCAR’s own race reporting and series rules. Anything that is my reading of those facts is labeled Analysis . What happened at Phoenix (confirmed) Reddick, in the No. 45 23XI Racing Toyota, beat Ryan Blaney by 0.801 seconds on Oct. 18. It was his sixth win of 2026, his first at Phoenix and his 14th in Cup, ending a 23-race winless run. He took the lead after a restart on Lap 294 and led the final 18 laps. Chase Elliott, Christopher Bell and Corey Heim completed the top five, with Joey Logano sixth. Larson started 22nd in a car that lacked speed, scored no stage points, and lost his right-front tire about 30 laps from the finish, hitting the Turn 1 wall. He was classified 34th and scored three points. Reddick scored 61. Denny Hamlin, running in the top five with under 100 laps to go, had a right-rear tire go down, then was caught speeding on pit entry, which cost him the free pass back onto the lead lap. He finished 28th. The swing in numbers (confirmed) Before the race Larson led Hamlin by 49 points. After it, Bell is five back and every one of Larson’s 15 Chase rivals gained at least 12 points on him. Reddick gained 58. NASCAR’s own count has seven drivers in contention with three races left. Driver Points behind Kyle Larson after Phoenix Christopher Bell 5 Chase Briscoe 24 Denny Hamlin 31 Ryan Blaney 40 Joey Logano 44 Tyler Reddick 56 Chase Elliott 149 Even Hamlin, who finished 28th after his own tire problem, gained 18 points on Larson, because Larson’s day was so much worse. Why Larson’s tire failed (confirmed, then analysis) Crew chief Cliff Daniels said the team ran its tire pressure too low, roughly a pound less air than it used in last year’s Championship 4 race at Phoenix, where Larson also had a tire failure late. Daniels said the team believed it had margin and did not. The NASCAR report does not carry any statement from Goodyear. Stock photo via Pexels (free license); not from the Phoenix race. Analysis: lower starting pressure generally buys grip early in a run and spends safety margin to pay for it. The team does not publish its pressure numbers, so the size of that trade is unknown. What is known is that this was a repeat of a failure from a year earlier, at the same track, and the explanation came from inside the team. It is fair to ask whether a car that qualified 22nd and was short on speed pushed the pressure window harder than a comfortable one would have. NASCAR’s reporting does not say that, so treat it as a question, not a finding. Because the explanation is about the team’s own pressure choice, not a reported defe
item.content:encoded: Kyle Larson arrived at Phoenix with a 49-point cushion. He left with five. A slow car was part of it, but the decisive piece was a right-front tire, and his crew chief has said the team ran the air pressure too low. Tyler Reddick won the Freeway Insurance 500, but the result that rewrote the Chase is a 34th-place finish worth three points. Confirmed vs. analysis: everything in the first sections below comes from NASCAR’s own race reporting and series rules. Anything that is my reading of those facts is labeled Analysis . What happened at Phoenix (confirmed) Reddick, in the No. 45 23XI Racing Toyota, beat Ryan Blaney by 0.801 seconds on Oct. 18. It was his sixth win of 2026, his first at Phoenix and his 14th in Cup, ending a 23-race winless run. He took the lead after a restart on Lap 294 and led the final 18 laps. Chase Elliott, Christopher Bell and Corey Heim completed the top five, with Joey Logano sixth. Larson started 22nd in a car that lacked speed, scored no stage points, and lost his right-front tire about 30 laps from the finish, hitting the Turn 1 wall. He was classified 34th and scored three points. Reddick scored 61. Denny Hamlin, running in the top five with under 100 laps to go, had a right-rear tire go down, then was caught speeding on pit entry, which cost him the free pass back onto the lead lap. He finished 28th. The swing in numbers (confirmed) Before the race Larson led Hamlin by 49 points. After it, Bell is five back and every one of Larson’s 15 Chase rivals gained at least 12 points on him. Reddick gained 58. NASCAR’s own count has seven drivers in contention with three races left. Driver Points behind Kyle Larson after Phoenix Christopher Bell 5 Chase Briscoe 24 Denny Hamlin 31 Ryan Blaney 40 Joey Logano 44 Tyler Reddick 56 Chase Elliott 149 Even Hamlin, who finished 28th after his own tire problem, gained 18 points on Larson, because Larson’s day was so much worse. Why Larson’s tire failed (confirmed, then analysis) Crew chief Cliff Daniels said the team ran its tire pressure too low, roughly a pound less air than it used in last year’s Championship 4 race at Phoenix, where Larson also had a tire failure late. Daniels said the team believed it had margin and did not. The NASCAR report does not carry any statement from Goodyear. Stock photo via Pexels (free license); not from the Phoenix race. Analysis: lower starting pressure generally buys grip early in a run and spends safety margin to pay for it. The team does not publish its pressure numbers, so the size of that trade is unknown. What is known is that this was a repeat of a failure from a year earlier, at the same track, and the explanation came from inside the team. It is fair to ask whether a car that qualified 22nd and was short on speed pushed the pressure window harder than a comfortable one would have. NASCAR’s reporting does not say that, so treat it as a question, not a finding. Because the explanation is about the team’s own pressure choice, not a reported defect, it is a process question for Larson’s team. How Reddick won it (confirmed, then analysis) Reddick took a two-tire call on a late caution. On the Lap 294 restart he cleared the leaders, then passed Chase Briscoe for the lead a lap later, setting Briscoe loose into Turn 3. Briscoe slid back to eighth on older tires. Bell had led a race-high 85 laps and finished fourth. Logano swept both stages, led 84 laps and lost track position on pit road before finishing sixth. Blaney started from the pole, dropped to eighth after a four-tire stop in the first stage break, and recovered to second. Stock photo via Pexels (free license); not from the Phoenix race. Analysis: the late caution was the whole race. Tire age mattered less than being at the front of the restart order when it counted, and the two-tire call put Reddick at the front of the restart order. Bell and Logano led 169 laps between them and finished fourth and sixth. Reddick led 18 and took 55 points for the win. That is the Chase math in one sentence: leading laps does not pay by itself, and the win is the prize. Why the format kept Larson alive (analysis) This is the first year of the revived Chase. There are no eliminations, points are reset once, and the champion is whoever has the most points after the finale. A win pays 55 points and second pays 35, according to NASCAR’s published breakdown, with stage points of 10 for first, 9 for second and so on down. By my reading of those values, a perfect race pays 75 points: 55 for the win plus 10 for each of the two stage wins. Larson’s 49-point cushion at the start of Phoenix was smaller than one perfect race, and so is the 56-point gap between Larson and Reddick. Under an elimination format, a 34th-place finish at a race this late could have ended a season. Under this one, it ended a lead. That is the argument for the format, and Phoenix is the case study. For more on how the points work with no eliminations, see our look at the Chase standings after Las Vegas ; Briscoe’s Las Vegas win already showed that a driver can take a full race’s worth of points and still lose ground to the leader. Our Phoenix preview pointed at the same 49-point cushion and the three Gibbs cars behind it. It lasted one race. What to watch next Talladega, Sunday, Oct. 25. A superspeedway can erase a five-point lead in one pack-wreck, so Larson cannot control his own margin. The stage breaks and rules package are different here; our look at Talladega’s spoiler trim and stage-break changes covers what the cars will do. Martinsville, Sunday, Nov. 1. A short track where pit-road discipline and track position decide the race. Hamlin and Wallace each lost ground to speeding penalties at Phoenix, so pit-road speed lines are worth watching. Homestead-Miami, Sunday, Nov. 8. The finale. The driver with the most Chase points after this race is champion. Reddick’s math. At 56 back, he is inside the 75 points a perfect race pays, so one more big day from him and one more bad one for the leader would flip the standings. Analysis: the question for Larson is not speed; it is whether his team trusts its own tire margin again, because the same failure has now shown up twice. If that margin changes at Talladega, we will know soon. Sources and method Race facts, standings gaps and quotes from the team come from NASCAR’s own reporting: the Phoenix race recap , Larson’s tire-failure report , Hamlin’s report , and NASCAR’s explainer on how the Chase works . The 2026 schedule dates come from NASCAR’s schedule release . Lap numbers differ slightly between NASCAR’s reports (the recap puts Larson’s tire failure at Lap 283, his own report at Lap 281), so this article says “about 30 laps from the finish.” The 75-point maximum is my own arithmetic from NASCAR’s published values, not an official figure. The post Larson’s Phoenix Tire Failure Cut a 49-Point Chase Lead to 5 appeared first on Backfire Racing .

item.title: Helmut Marko delivers sharp response to Horner: 'That's a collection of falsehoods'
item.description: Helmut Marko has hit back at Christian Horner following a series of accusations made by the former Red Bull team principal, dismissing his claims as false in a brief response to F1-Insider. Horner has recently spoken about his deteriorating relationship with Marko, with whom he worked for more than two decades at Red Bull. The Briton, who was dismissed as team principal in July 2025, has criticised the Austrian's behaviour behind the scenes, particularly following the death of Red Bull co-founder Dietrich Mateschitz in 2022. Horner criticises Marko over Red Bull's internal tensions Speaking to BILD, Horner accused Marko of working towards his dismissal and criticised his handling of internal information. He also claimed that Marko had failed to offer his condolences following the death of Horner's former partner and mother of his daughter. Horner revealed that the two no longer have a relationship, explaining that they have not spoken since his departure from Red Bull. The former team principal expanded on his frustrations during an appearance on Up to Speed. Asked whether he sometimes felt responsible for cleaning up situations created by Marko, Horner replied: "Sometimes, yes. And there there periods where it was was fine, it was great, and everybody knew what their roles were. I think where it started to get a little bit messy was, as I say, after Dietrich passed." Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Horner suggested that the internal dynamics changed following Mateschitz's death, with information becoming a source of influence within the organisation: "In the desire to become relevant, knowledge was that currency. And so, I would have engineers coming in, Adrian would go bananas at something that was in the media about an upgrade and he's so secretive about that kind of thing, that suddenly we were doing all our talking through the media, and then inevitably you end up having to mop elements of it up." The Briton explained that he believed these situations created an inaccurate public impression of Red Bull and caused frustration among employees at the team's Milton Keynes headquarters: "I felt it portrayed the team in a way that wasn't true to our character of who we were as an organisation. Certainly the people within Milton Keynes didn't recognise that. So you're having to balance all those dynamics." Marko dismisses Horner's allegations Following the latest comments from his former colleague, Marko was approached by F1-Insider for his reaction. The Austrian declined to engage with Horner's individual allegations, instead rejecting his account altogether: "That's a collection of falsehoods, I don't even want to go into that." Horner's departure in July 2025 brought an end to his 20-year tenure as team principal, while Marko also left the organisation at the end of that season. Both played central roles in the team's championship successes with Sebastian Vettel and Max Verstappen, but their accounts of the final years of their working

item.title: Japan to launch world-first mission to moon of Mars
item.description: Japanese scientists will launch a spacecraft on Tuesday that aims to be the first to retrieve samples from one of Mars’s moons, potentially helping unlock the origins of the Solar System and life on Earth. The flagship H3 rocket carrying the unmanned Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) probe is set to blast off from the Tanegashima Space Center at 4:41 am (1941 GMT Monday), according to the Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA). If successful, the spacecraft will arrive near Mars around August next year, where it will orbit one of its moons, Phobos. It will later land on Phobos and collect at least 10 grams (0.35 ounces) of material from the surface during its planned three years in the Red Planet’s vicinity. The mission — which aims to be the first round trip to the Martian region — is a collaboration with US and European space agencies, as well as numerous universities and tech companies. Those involved hope that it will help lay the groundwork for eventual human exploration. JAXA hopes the mission will reveal how Mars and its two moons formed, a key piece of knowledge in working out how the Solar System was born. One theory for the origin of the moons — the “giant impact” hypothesis — is that they formed after a celestial body collided with Mars. The “capture” hypothesis, meanwhile, postulates that the moons are asteroids pulled in by Mars’s gravity. Determining which theory is correct will help reveal “how a habitable environment for life might have arisen on the terrestrial planets”, JAXA said, referring to the four rocky worlds closest to the Sun — Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars. – ‘Natural space station’ – JAXA said the mission will also explore the possibility of using Phobos as a “natural space station” by establishing the requirements for a round trip — something “essential for crewed Mars exploration”. It will also observe the planet’s other moon, Deimos, although it will not land on it. US and Chinese space agencies have also been vying to be the first to return rock samples from Mars’s surface back to Earth. NASA’s Perseverance rover, which has been roaming across Mars since 2021, has already collected samples. The return mission, however, was effectively cancelled by the administration of President Donald Trump following a vote by Congress in January. China’s Tianwen-3 spacecraft is scheduled for launch around 2028 and hopes to return Mars samples to Earth as early as 2031 — potentially before the Japanese mission’s return. The post Japan to launch world-first mission to moon of Mars appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Jon Gruden torches NFL referees after controversial personal foul call against Rams
item.description: Credit: FS1 The vaunted Los Angeles Rams superteam have reason to complain about NFL officials, but Jon Gruden is already doing it for them. After entering the season as heavy Super Bowl favorites, with some pundits even wondering whether they could go undefeated, the Rams now find themselves in last place in the NFC West following a bad loss at home to the Arizona Cardinals Sunday afternoon. And while the Rams deserve plenty of blame for starting the season 2-4, they were briefly in position to win Sunday until a brutal personal-foul call against them helped set up a game-winning field goal for the Cardinals. The Rams scored a late touchdown to take a 16-15 lead with less than a minute to go in the game. But the Cardinals would go on to complete a 21-yard pass to Jalen Brooks on their final drive, and as he came down with the ball, his helmet collided with Rams cornerback Josh Wallace, who was flagged for unnecessary roughness. WOW… Rams get called for a personal foul for hitting a defenseless receiver… he barely touched him but the refs added 15 yards to the end of this play for that https://t.co/6xuLynSAiw — Rate the Refs (@Rate_the_Refs) October 18, 2026 Gruden joined Wake Up Barstool Monday morning to react to the controversial personal foul call. And while it’s one thing for an official to make that call in real time, Gruden wants to know why the replay official didn’t quickly correct it. And if the replay official isn’t going to correct it, then why does the NFL have replay? “Whats the point in having [a ref] up there communicating with the [refs] down there [on the field] that can pick up some of these flags?” -@BarstoolGruden is disgusted with the NFL’s inability to use the replay official to correct on the field refereeing mistakes https://t.co/oaIjfq1Z5p — Wake Up Barstool (@wakeupbarstool) October 19, 2026 “We have a guy in the booth; he’s called the replay official,” Gruden began. “And his job is to look at the game and see calls that are screwed up. He has communication with the white hat. And I should just say, ‘Hey, Dave, you really screwed up that call, pick up the flag.’ “Now, for that not to happen, it makes me sick. I don’t understand what the hell we’re doing! We have all this technology; look at this super high-speed, Emmy Award-winning shots you’re showing. What’s the point in having a guy up there communicating?” Gruden might not want to be overly critical of players or teams as he continues to seek a path back to being an NFL head coach . But his desire to return to the sideline hasn’t stopped Gruden from criticizing the refs. NFL on Fox analyst Greg Olsen questioned the call during the broadcast. And Fox rules analyst Mike Pereira similarly questioned the flag being thrown, agreeing the personal foul shouldn’t have been called. item.title: Stripes of the Week: Week 7 LSU vs. Mississippi State
item.description: Like the NHL’s “Three Stars of the Week,” David Billiot Jr. and I snake-draft Stripes of the Week for our podcast, Geaux Deep Dive. With David a bit under the weather, Matt Miguez stepped in for him. Here are Week 7’s Stripes of the Week: Three Stripes: Jordan Ross (Matt), Sam Leavitt (Zach) After earning two stripes for his Week One performance against Clemson, Jordan Ross returns to the list, earning three in the absence of Princewill Umanmielen, who went down with an injury early against Mississippi State. Ross stepped up in a big way, recording six tackles, 1.5 sacks, 2.5 tackles for a loss, one forced fumble, two passes broken up and one additional QB hurry. That laundry list of stats was enough for Ross to be the highest-rated player for LSU from Pro Football Focus on Saturday with a 92.8 overall grade. He will need to keep up this type of impact, especially with question marks about Umanmielen’s injury. Sam Leavitt, despite the high volume of turnovers this season, has been very good. He is 14th in the country in passing yards; of the top 15 quarterbacks in passing yards, he is 3rd in completion percentage; he is tied for 20th in the country in passing touchdowns, all while adding 270 yards rushing for seven touchdowns. There have been two glaring weaknesses for Leavitt this season: patience and turnovers. The two go hand in hand, particularly when it comes to Leavitt. He made strides to fix both of those on Saturday. He had zero turnovers on the day for the first time this season. A large part of that was taking his time in the pocket, making his reads and hitting the checkdown more often to the tune of 31 of 38 passes completed for 289 yards and four touchdowns. Those marks made him the highest-rated PFF player on offense with an 81.4. Two Stripes: DJ Pickett (Zach), Jackson Harris (Matt) Similar to the thought process from PJ Woodland last week, it is great when you do not have to hear a cornerback’s name called, but when it is called, you hope it is for all of the right reasons. Pickett’s name was called for a lot of the right reasons on Saturday: he recorded six tackles and broke up two passes, and he was a toenail away from an interception as well. For weeks, I have said Winston Watkins Jr. was the clear-cut WR 1. That conversation has quickly muddied itself. Not because Watkins has been bad. Far from it. item.content:encoded: Like the NHL’s “Three Stars of the Week,” David Billiot Jr. and I snake-draft Stripes of the Week for our podcast, Geaux Deep Dive. With David a bit under the weather, Matt Miguez stepped in for him. Here are Week 7’s Stripes of the Week: Three Stripes: Jordan Ross (Matt), Sam Leavitt (Zach) After earning two stripes for his Week One performance against Clemson, Jordan Ross returns to the list, earning three in the absence of Princewill Umanmielen, who went down with an injury early against Mississippi State. Ross stepped up in a big way, recording six tackles, 1.5 sacks, 2.5 tackles for a loss, one forced fumble, two passes broken up and one additional QB hurry. That laundry list of stats was enough for Ross to be the highest-rated player for LSU from Pro Football Focus on Saturday with a 92.8 overall grade. He will need to keep up this type of impact, especially with question marks about Umanmielen’s injury. Sam Leavitt, despite the high volume of turnovers this season, has been very good. He is 14th in the country in passing yards; of the top 15 quarterbacks in passing yards, he is 3rd in completion percentage; he is tied for 20th in the country in passing touchdowns, all while adding 270 yards rushing for seven touchdowns. There have been two glaring weaknesses for Leavitt this season: patience and turnovers. The two go hand in hand, particularly when it comes to Leavitt. He made strides to fix both of those on Saturday. He had zero turnovers on the day for the first time this season. A large part of that was taking his time in the pocket, making his reads and hitting the checkdown more often to the tune of 31 of 38 passes completed for 289 yards and four touchdowns. Those marks made him the highest-rated PFF player on offense with an 81.4. Two Stripes: DJ Pickett (Zach), Jackson Harris (Matt) Similar to the thought process from PJ Woodland last week, it is great when you do not have to hear a cornerback’s name called, but when it is called, you hope it is for all of the right reasons. Pickett’s name was called for a lot of the right reasons on Saturday: he recorded six tackles and broke up two passes, and he was a toenail away from an interception as well. For weeks, I have said Winston Watkins Jr. was the clear-cut WR 1. That conversation has quickly muddied itself. Not because Watkins has been bad. Far from it. Jackson Harris has just been that good over the past few weeks. Six catches for 85 yards and two touchdowns land Harris on the stripes list for the third time in the last four weeks and good enough for the second-highest-rated player by PFF with a 77.4 overall grade. Harris, like Umanmielen, did go down with an injury later in the game and was seen in a boot, so time will tell as to what his availability will be for Auburn and beyond. One Stripe: TJ Dottery (Matt), Dilin Jones (Zach) Death, taxes and TJ Dottery leading the team in tackles (especially while Whit Weeks is out) feel like the three certainties in life right now. 12 tackles for Dottery on Saturday do not even tell the full story. Since Weeks has been injured, Dottery has taken on the green dot role for LSU, which, as you may know, is the leader of the defense and the de facto on-field coach. Dottery led the Tigers to their first shutout win of the season against a very good offensive coach in Jeff Lebby. Dilin Jones’ 18 carries for 85 yards are not the reason he is cracking back into the Stripes of the Week this week. In fact, the reason stems back to last week’s loss to Kentucky. Over the past two weeks, Dilin Jones has blossomed into a weapon in the passing attack alongside his production in the run game. In that span, Jones has caught 15 passes for 142 yards, surpassing his combined totals from the five games prior in which he had just 11 catches for 48 yards. It is only fitting Jones makes the list the same week Sam Leavitt returns as the aforementioned checkdowns Leavitt has been relying on more have been going to Jones, and whenever he gets the ball, he has a great chance to make some defenders miss and break some tackles. Honorable Mentions: Eugene Wilson III – 3 catches, 32 yards, 1 TD (his first as a Tiger) Malik Elzy – 2 catches, 20 yards, 1 TD (his first as a Tiger) Ty Benefield – 4 tackles, 1 INT (his first as a Tiger) Dominick McKinley – 3 tackles, 1 sack Stephiylan Green – 3 tackles, 1.5 for a loss, .5 sacks Deuce Geralds – 6 tackles, 1 QB hurry PJ Woodland – 4 tackles, 2 passes broken up

item.title: ‘Just trying’ – What A.J. Brown thinks of his performance during Patriots vs. Jets clash
item.description: Photo by Kathryn Riley/Getty Images A.J. Brown’s return should have energized the New England Patriots fans, and it certainly did, but the excitement stayed only until the start of the game, as after that, there was nothing in the wide receiver’s performance against the New York Jets that could make anyone happy. He recorded 3 receptions in his return from injury, which would anger fans who did not watch the game, as Brown is a player who needs more than three receptions to make himself known in a game. However, the real reason behind the three receptions was his inability to catch the ball on the day. He only managed to record three receptions out of the 10 attempts thrown at him against the New York Jets. The Super Bowl LIX MVP dropped three catches in the game, including one that could have been a touchdown pass. There was another crucial moment where Brown’s poor display could have cost the Patriots the game. With 32 seconds remaining, the Jets attempted an onside kick, the ball slipped through Brown’s hands again but his teammate Eli Raridon was able to recover the ball safely. After the game, Brown made no excuses for his performance against the Jets. A.J. Brown wants to ‘get going’ soon This was Brown’s first game since the high ankle sprain in Week 1 against the Seattle Seahawks. It was expected that he would take time to settle in, but Brown was not ready to use his return as an excuse for the poor performance. “No matter whatever question you guys ask, I’ll tell you guys there’s no excuses… Ankle or not, I’ll make all those plays,” said Brown in the locker room. “Short week, just trying to get going again and put my best foot forward, put this to bed really fast, I’m going to watch the tape and it’s over, I’m going to flush it.” Brown was the Patriots’ biggest addition in the offseason. He was the player expected to take them over the hump. So far, he has not been able to prove that bringing him in was the right move, but with more than half of the season remaining, Brown has the chance to silence the doubters. Drake Maye, who started the season with a string of poor performances, was called out by many analysts. However, he has stepped up for the Patriots; all they now need is their star WR Brown to get back to his usual self. Having won three games in a row, Mike Vrabel’s men are finally showing the world why they deserved their place in the Super Bowl last season. Once Brown gets firing, they definitely look like a team that could make a push to win the AFC East division title. item.title: Bayern Munich fear Vincent Kompany will miss the Arsenal game
item.description: (Photo by Sebastian Widmann/Bundesliga via Getty Images) | Bundesliga via Getty Images According to reports in the German media, Bayern Munich coach Vincent Kompany is suffering from a bout of illness, which jeopardizes his participation against Arsenal FC in the Champions League this week. Assistant coach Aaron Danks may be called to take over in case the Belgian cannot make the touchline. According to Tz, the situation looks grim (via @iMiaSanMia ): It’s still unclear whether Vincent Kompany will actively coach the team on the sideline against Arsenal on Wednesday, or take his seat on the bench as he did against Leipzig. The coach is currently struggling with the flu, which is having a slight impact on his old scar tissue. Kompany is currently having problems climbing stairs and standing for extended periods. If the coach is not fit in time, assistant Aaron Danks will primarily take charge in the coaching zone on Wednesday. Bild confirmed that Kompany missed training, but the club expects him to be fit in time (via @iMiaSanMia ): Assistant coach Aaron Danks was in charge of today’s closed training session. Vincent Kompany was not there, but Bayern expect him to be available against Arsenal. The Belgian coach is also determined to be with his team on Wednesday. This comes after reports that the coach was battling a hip issue during the 6-1 win over RB Leipzig in the weekend. The situation compounds the misery for FC Bayern, who already have to deal with losing Michael Olise for one of the biggest games of the Champions League league phase. Last year, Kompany was forced to sit out the opening leg against PSG in the semi-final due to yellow card accumulation. Bayern Munich eventually lost that game 4-5. With all these factors working against the team right now, defeating the Gunners seems like a Herculean task at the moment. Join the conversation! item.title: Brock Purdy and the 49ers can expect plenty of blitzing from the Commanders
item.description: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers gestures after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a huge Week 5 divisional win against the Seattle Seahawks, the San Francisco 49ers begin their longest stretch of games without an NFC West opponent with a Monday night date against the Washington Commanders. Washington has already aided the 49ers this season, handing Seattle its first loss of the season with a Week 3 win over San Francisco’s division rival. A Commanders loss to the 49ers on Monday night would also be a huge boost for San Francisco, with a win putting the 49ers up three games in the NFC West. The 49ers will look to avoid a letdown spot against a lesser Washington team. Here are the numbers to know heading into the Monday night clash: 37.7 Percent. The Commanders blitz on 37.7 of opponents’ dropbacks, the second-highest rate in the league. The dam finally broke for the 49ers offense when Seattle’s defense got to Brock Purdy for the first three sacks San Francisco has allowed this season. The 49ers offense will now have to face the team that sends an extra man or two at the second-highest clip in the league on Monday night. Unfortunately, that high blitz rate hasn’t done much for the lacking Washington pass defense. Because of the blitz, Washington’s defense ranks well in pressure rate (9th) and hurry percentage (6th), but that hasn’t resulted in sacks. Washington ranks 24th with nine sacks, and since the pass rush can’t bring down the opposing quarterback, the Commanders’ poor secondary has been exposed to the tune of: 255 passing yards per game (4th-highest) 14 passing touchdowns (tied for most) 67 passing first downs (third-most) Purdy’s been in incredible form to start the season, and that form should continue against the lacking Washington secondary, so long as the San Francisco offense can handle the blitzes that Dan Quinn and his Washington defense will present. 67.7 Rushing yards per game. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels averages 67.7 rushing yards per game. With Washington’s leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) out on Monday night, the onus will be on Daniels to pick up the slack in the run game, something he’ll have no issue in taking on. Entering Week 6, Daniels ranked eighth among quarterbacks with 21 rush attempts. The only reason he doesn’t have more is the two games he missed, but despite the missed games, Daniels 203 rushing yards are second-most for quarterbacks behind only Josh Allen, who has 239 rushing yards on twice as many rush attempts in his five games. Simply put, the 49ers will not face a more prolific mobile quarterback this season than Daniels. Raheem Morris and the 49ers defense have faced one quarterback with more rush attempts so far this season than Daniels, and that was Malik Willis in Week 2 when the 49ers beat the Miami Dolphins. item.content:encoded: SEATTLE, WASHINGTON - OCTOBER 11: Brock Purdy #13 of the San Francisco 49ers gestures after the game against the Seattle Seahawks at Lumen Field on October 11, 2026 in Seattle, Washington. (Photo by Alika Jenner/Getty Images) | Getty Images Fresh off a huge Week 5 divisional win against the Seattle Seahawks, the San Francisco 49ers begin their longest stretch of games without an NFC West opponent with a Monday night date against the Washington Commanders. Washington has already aided the 49ers this season, handing Seattle its first loss of the season with a Week 3 win over San Francisco’s division rival. A Commanders loss to the 49ers on Monday night would also be a huge boost for San Francisco, with a win putting the 49ers up three games in the NFC West. The 49ers will look to avoid a letdown spot against a lesser Washington team. Here are the numbers to know heading into the Monday night clash: 37.7 Percent. The Commanders blitz on 37.7 of opponents’ dropbacks, the second-highest rate in the league. The dam finally broke for the 49ers offense when Seattle’s defense got to Brock Purdy for the first three sacks San Francisco has allowed this season. The 49ers offense will now have to face the team that sends an extra man or two at the second-highest clip in the league on Monday night. Unfortunately, that high blitz rate hasn’t done much for the lacking Washington pass defense. Because of the blitz, Washington’s defense ranks well in pressure rate (9th) and hurry percentage (6th), but that hasn’t resulted in sacks. Washington ranks 24th with nine sacks, and since the pass rush can’t bring down the opposing quarterback, the Commanders’ poor secondary has been exposed to the tune of: 255 passing yards per game (4th-highest) 14 passing touchdowns (tied for most) 67 passing first downs (third-most) Purdy’s been in incredible form to start the season, and that form should continue against the lacking Washington secondary, so long as the San Francisco offense can handle the blitzes that Dan Quinn and his Washington defense will present. 67.7 Rushing yards per game. Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels averages 67.7 rushing yards per game. With Washington’s leading rusher Jacory Croskey-Merritt (groin) out on Monday night, the onus will be on Daniels to pick up the slack in the run game, something he’ll have no issue in taking on. Entering Week 6, Daniels ranked eighth among quarterbacks with 21 rush attempts. The only reason he doesn’t have more is the two games he missed, but despite the missed games, Daniels 203 rushing yards are second-most for quarterbacks behind only Josh Allen, who has 239 rushing yards on twice as many rush attempts in his five games. Simply put, the 49ers will not face a more prolific mobile quarterback this season than Daniels. Raheem Morris and the 49ers defense have faced one quarterback with more rush attempts so far this season than Daniels, and that was Malik Willis in Week 2 when the 49ers beat the Miami Dolphins. Willis is a quality rusher in his own right, with the third-most at the position, 186 rushing yards on his 27 rush attempts. His 6.9 yards per attempt rank fourth among quarterbacks with 15 or more rushing attempts this season. But when the 49ers faced him, Willis couldn’t get his legs going, holding the quarterback to a season-low six rushing yards on two carries. Commanders offensive coordinator David Blough will draw up at least two designed runs for Daniels, so don’t expect a Willis-like ground usage for Washington’s quarterback on Monday night. 4 Times. The 49ers have started 6-0 four times in franchise history (1948, 1984, 1990, and 2019). A win on Monday night would mark the fifth time the 49ers have started the first third of the season without a loss. Each of the last three 6-0 starts have meant at least an NFC Championship Game appearance (in the Super Bowl era). 1948 was the only 6-0 start in 49ers history that didn’t result in a playoff game appearance (the 14-0 Cleveland Browns claimed the 1948 AAFC Championship defeating the Buffalo Bills), but the 49ers would finish 12-2. Those 12 wins came against teams like the New York Yankees, Brooklyn Dodgers, Los Angeles Dons, and Chicago Rockets. But since the invention of the Super Bowl, a 6-0 start has meant at least an NFC Championship Game appearance for the 49ers. The 2026 49ers have the chance to do something the 1984 team did: go 6-0 with a Monday night win against an NFC East foe. 1984 saw the 49ers defeat the New York Giants to move to 6-0 with a 31-10 Monday Night Football win. San Francisco’s quest for perfection in 1984 would end the next week with a loss against Pittsburgh, but the 49ers would go on to win the franchise’s second Super Bowl. The 1990 49ers would use a Week 6 win against the Steelers to move to 6-0. The streak would continue into the middle of November when a Week 12 loss to the Rams would drop San Francisco to 10-1. San Francisco would finish 1990 with a 14-2 record but fall short in the NFC Championship Game to a 13-3 Giants team that would go on to win Super Bowl XXV. The most recent 6-0 team was Kyle Shanahan’s third season with the 49ers in 2019, when San Francisco moved to 6-0 with a sloppy 9-0 win in a rainy Washington, D.C. The 49ers would stay undefeated a few more weeks before losing to Seattle to end the start-of-the-season winning streak at eight games. The 49ers would again make the Super Bowl, but fell to the Chiefs in Miami. Now, 6-0 doesn’t guarantee postseason success, but the history shines brightly on the 2026 49ers’ Monday night win.

item.title: BJ Upton to throw out ALCS Game Six first pitch
item.description: ST. PETERSBURG, FL - SEPTEMBER 09: BJ Upton #2 of the Tampa Bay Rays salutes the fans after hitting his third home run during the game against the Texas Rangers on September 9, 2012 at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Florida. (Photo by Charles Sonnenblick/Getty Images) | Getty Images The American League Championship Series is returning to Tropicana Field and with it, the Rays will bring back another of the franchise’s greatest players to toss out the ceremonial first pitch prior to the game. Earlier this postseason, the Rays have already called upon Kevin Kiermaier, Carlos Pena, and Carl Crawford to throw out the first pitch and now they’re bestowing the honor upon BJ Upton. The Rays drafted BJ Upton with the 2nd overall selection of the 2002 draft. The franchise accelerated Upton through the system and had him make his big league debut just over two years later at just 19-years old. Despite his young age, Upton displayed offensive potential but his defense needed serious improvement. Upton spent the entirety of the 2005 season and most of the 2006 campaign in Triple-A before making his way to the big league roster for good starting in 2007. With this advancement, Upton found a new home in center field where he showcased plus defense due to his elite speed and arm strength. Over the next six seasons, Upton would be an above average offensive player and stellar defender. From 2007 through 2012, Upton hit .255/.338/.430 with 113 HR and 217 stolen bases, registering a 110 wRC+ and accruing 22.7 fWAR (3.8 fWAR per season). Upton was an integral part of the Rays 2008 American League pennant run, providing the team with a historic offensive performance in the postseason as tied the record for most RBI in the ALCS and launched 7 HR during the playoffs. During game two of the 2008 ALCS, it was BJ Upton who lifted the walkoff sacrifice fly that tied the series for the Rays. At the end of the 2012 season, Upton became the first player in franchise history to hit for the cycle. Following his departure from the Rays as a free agent following the 2012 season, Upton signed with the Atlanta Braves and eventually played for the San Diego Padres and Toronto Blue Jays, last playing in 2017 in the San Francisco Giants minor league system; Upton officially retired in 2019. At the end of play in 2026, Upton currently ranks 5th among Rays position players all-time in fWAR, 6th in homeruns, and 2nd in stolen bases.

item.title: CAN mourns Uduaghan, hails commitment to national unity
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike The Christian Association of Nigeria (CAN) has mourned former Delta State Governor, Dr Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, praising his commitment to dialogue and confidence-building during a period of heightened political tension in Nigeria. The association said Uduaghan’s efforts to promote understanding and preserve national unity remained an important part of his contributions to public service and nation-building. In a statement on Monday, CAN President, Archbishop Daniel Okoh, expressed sadness over the former governor’s death and extended the association’s sympathies to his family, the Delta State Government and the people of Delta State, as well as all those mourning him. “His commitment to dialogue, confidence-building and the preservation of national unity remains worthy of commendation,” Archbishop Okoh said. He described Uduaghan’s passing as a loss to his family and all who valued his contributions to public service and nation-building. Archbishop Okoh prayed for God’s comfort for the bereaved family and others affected by the loss, asking God to grant the former governor eternal rest. The post CAN mourns Uduaghan, hails commitment to national unity appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Man City’s Guehi questions impact of taking the knee in fight against racism
item.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester City defender Marc Guehi believes taking the knee before football matches may have lost some of its impact saying more can be done to tackle racism. According to the Associated Press, Guehi, who is Black, did not take the knee before City’s Premier League match against Ipswich on Saturday, the first of two rounds of games dedicated to the league’s “No Room For Racism” campaign. It isn’t the first time Guehi refused to perform the gesture. The gesture was introduced in June 2020 in support of the Black Lives Matter movement. The Premier League stopped asking players to take the knee before every match from the 2022-23 season, instead inviting them to do so on selected occasions. Speaking on Monday, ahead of City’s Champions League match against AEK Athens, Guehi welcomed the continuation of the anti-racism campaign and called for further action. “It’s great,” he said. “Whether more can be done — more can always be done. We have to see how we can move the campaign along. “I don’t think it’s necessarily a football issue. I think it’s a wider societal issue and football is that beacon of hope to try to get the message out. But whether more can be done, we will try, hopefully with the PFA (English soccer’s players union), with the league.” Asked whether taking the knee had lost its meaning, Guehi replied: “Maybe. I haven’t been taking the knee for a while now, to be honest. I’d always clap, just because of what that actually signifies.” He did not elaborate on his reasons for no longer taking the knee. Leeds striker Dominic Calvert-Lewin also remained standing during the weekend’s anti-racism gesture, while his teammates and Manchester United players knelt. Calvert-Lewin scored in the 1-1 draw. Leeds manager Daniel Farke said: “Dom is more or less like, ‘No, I don’t go down. I show my respect by standing up, more or less.’ “I think each individual is different and shows respect for this campaign in a different way.” Former Crystal Palace forward Wilfried Zaha, who is Black, said in 2021 that he would no longer take the knee, describing the gesture as “degrading”. “I feel like taking a knee is degrading,” Zaha was quoted by The Guardian as telling the FT Business of Football conference. “Growing up, my parents just let me know that I should just be proud to be black, no matter what, and I just think we should stand tall. “I think the meaning behind the whole thing is becoming something that we just do now. That’s not enough.” The Premier League’s “No Room For Racism” initiative takes place during the UK’s Black History Month. League chief executive Richard Masters said it aims to use “the reach of our players to send an important message: we are united in the fight against racism.” The post Man City’s Guehi questions impact of taking the knee in fight against racism appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Avengers Star Officially Clarifies His Huge Doomsday Spoiler
item.description: Ever since Robert Downey Jr. was announced to be playing Doctor Doom in December's Avengers: Doomsday , Marvel fans have wondered how the film would handle this in the context of the multiverse. Would Victor von Doom be a variant of Tony Stark, the character Downey played for over a decade? Would he never take off his mask, meaning Avengers like Steve Rogers and Thor wouldn't have to address how their new enemy suspiciously looks a lot like their old friend?

item.title: Rivers assembly set to recall three suspended Pro-Fubara lawmakers
item.description: By Davies Iheamnachor, Port Harcourt The Rivers State House of Assembly has reversed its earlier decision to declare the seats of three lawmakers supporting the state governor, Siminalayi Fubara, vacant. The state’s legislative arm reached this resolution to reinstate the three lawmakers during its plenary on Monday. The pro-Fubara lawmakers, whose seats were earlier marked to be declared vacant, included Hon. Victor Oko-Jumbo, representing Bonny Constituency. Hon. Sokari Goodboy Sokari, Ahoada West and Hon. Orubienimigha Timothy, Opobo/Nkoro Constituency. The assembly decision followed letters dated 16th of October 2026 from the three lawmakers, which were read on the floor of the House during plenary. The lawmakers in the letter requested that they be called back into the House to continue the representation of the constituency with the emergence of peace. It would be recalled that the House of Assembly had, on the 30th October 2023, in the heat of the political crisis, suspended the three lawmakers alongside Hon. Edison Ehie for alleged misconduct. Ehie, who later became the Chief of Staff to the Governor, had resigned his membership of the assembly in the heat of the crisis, allowing for a by-election in his constituency. The trio’s suspension was, however, lifted on the 20th of December 2023 after the first peace meeting initiated by President Tinubu between the Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Nyesom Wike and Governor Fubara. But following the failure of the three lawmakers to attend sittings after their suspension was lifted, their seats were then declared vacant on the 15th of October 2025 by the Amaewhule-led House in line with section 109 sub 1 (e) of the Constitution. The House had consequently written the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to conduct a by-election to fill the vacant seats. But during Monday’s plenary, the Speaker, Rt. Hon. Martin Amaewhule read the letters from each of the three lawmakers explaining that they never saw the letter lifting their suspension earlier, which was the reason they didn’t attend the sitting and appealed for the House to rescind its decision. After debates on the letter by the lawmakers, the House decided to rescind its decision to declare their seats vacant The assembly’s decision might not be unconnected with Sunday’s meeting between the Leader of Rainbow Coalition and Minister of the Federal Capital Territory, Chief Nyesom Wike, the lawmakers, Chairmen of Local Government Areas and other leaders of the coalition with the Governor, Fubara and members of his team. It was gathered that the letters that preceded and the decision of the Assembly were issues resolved at the strategic closed-door meeting. It was further gathered the meeting which had Senator Magnus Abe was aimed at resolving outstanding areas of differences between the two political camps of Wike and Fubara ahead of the 2027 general elections. The post Rivers assembly set to recall three suspended Pro-Fubara

item.title: 'They're kind of goth': NASA spacecraft gives mysterious brown dwarfs a close-up
item.description: null Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?). And that's apt, according to the leader of the new study, which reveals that, chemically speaking, the atmospheres of these dark and cloudy worlds are not unlike those of our solar system's gas giant planets. "They’re kind of goth," Zafar Rustamkulov, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement . "Unlike exoplanets , free-floating brown dwarfs are completely independent celestial objects that will fade into eternity alone. We’re still learning how complex they are." Rustamkulov added that, from Earth orbit, SPHEREx — short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer — sees wavelengths of light that are nigh-impossible to see with telescopes on the ground because water in Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. That is important for bringing brown dwarfs into the light. "We are picking up light from the deep, red clouds of brown dwarfs all over the sky," he said. A forest (of brown dwarfs) Brown dwarfs have been somewhat mysterious since their discovery in the 1990s, due to the fact that the small amount of nuclear fusion that occurs within them causes them to emit no more than a faint glow. That means that our understanding of their makeup, their storms, and their evolution really only comes from theory. To help lift this observational darkness, the team turned to data from SPHEREx. They studied 37 nearby brown dwarfs in a spectrum of light including 102 wavelengths, from the deepest red our eyes can see to the invisible infrared light. These local failed stars spanned the full temperature range for brown dwarfs — from 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius). Considering that the temperature of the sun is about 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit (5,500 degrees Celsius), you could definitely say brown dwarfs run cold. Brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/NASA/JPL-Caltech) The spectra of brown dwarfs seen by SPHEREx allowed the team to determine that their atmospheres are chemically rich in water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane. item.dc:creator: Robert Lea
item.content:encoded: null Using NASA’s SPHEREx spacecraft, astronomers have studied a host of "failed stars," also known as brown dwarfs. These strange cosmic bodies straddle the line between planets and stars, possessing a mass between 13 and 80 times that of Jupiter (0.013 to 0.08 times the mass of the sun ). They get the nickname failed stars because they form like stars from collapsing clouds of gas and dust but fail to gather enough mass to trigger the fusion of hydrogen to helium in their cores, the process that powers actual stars . This formation process also means that brown dwarfs are cosmic loners, wandering the darkness of space alone, bereft of the light of a parent star. That description might sound like lyrics from a Type O Negative song ("Black No. 1," anybody?). And that's apt, according to the leader of the new study, which reveals that, chemically speaking, the atmospheres of these dark and cloudy worlds are not unlike those of our solar system's gas giant planets. "They’re kind of goth," Zafar Rustamkulov, of the California Institute of Technology (Caltech), said in a statement . "Unlike exoplanets , free-floating brown dwarfs are completely independent celestial objects that will fade into eternity alone. We’re still learning how complex they are." Rustamkulov added that, from Earth orbit, SPHEREx — short for Spectro-Photometer for the History of the Universe, Epoch of Reionization, and Ices Explorer — sees wavelengths of light that are nigh-impossible to see with telescopes on the ground because water in Earth’s atmosphere absorbs them. That is important for bringing brown dwarfs into the light. "We are picking up light from the deep, red clouds of brown dwarfs all over the sky," he said. A forest (of brown dwarfs) Brown dwarfs have been somewhat mysterious since their discovery in the 1990s, due to the fact that the small amount of nuclear fusion that occurs within them causes them to emit no more than a faint glow. That means that our understanding of their makeup, their storms, and their evolution really only comes from theory. To help lift this observational darkness, the team turned to data from SPHEREx. They studied 37 nearby brown dwarfs in a spectrum of light including 102 wavelengths, from the deepest red our eyes can see to the invisible infrared light. These local failed stars spanned the full temperature range for brown dwarfs — from 4,000 degrees Fahrenheit to minus 10 degrees Fahrenheit (2,200 to minus 20 degrees Celsius). Considering that the temperature of the sun is about 10,000 degrees Fahrenheit (5,500 degrees Celsius), you could definitely say brown dwarfs run cold. Brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/NASA/JPL-Caltech) The spectra of brown dwarfs seen by SPHEREx allowed the team to determine that their atmospheres are chemically rich in water, carbon dioxide, carbon monoxide and methane. "We’re seeing the signatures of these molecules and how they change from object to object across the entire temperature regime," said team member J. Davy Kirkpatrick, also of Caltech. "Our paper concentrated on just three dozen, but we have thousands more that we are in the process of analyzing. "I really want to see what bounds the universe places on the variety of brown dwarfs." All my colors Brown dwarfs have been routinely observed by other telescopes, including NASA's James Webb Space Telescope and the agency's now-retired Spitzer Space Telescope , but the wide wavelength coverage of SPHEREx has made it particularly useful in observing these failed stars. That's good news for astronomers waiting for change in the atmospheres of brown dwarfs as they age and grow cold. The researchers found that some brown dwarfs observed by SPHEREx are at a stage of extreme change in which their clouds are clearing, creating atmospheres rich in methane. The team may have discovered significant new details about brown dwarfs, but they are still on the proverbial mystery street when it comes to these strange celestial objects, "The state-of-the-art models are capturing the general chemical trend, but when it comes to these cloudy transitions, the models are struggling to match the data," said Rustamkulov. "No two brown dwarfs are alike. Even at the same temperature, their spectra look quite distinct." NASA’s SPHEREx reveals molecules like methane (CH4), carbon dioxide (CO2), and carbon monoxide (CO) in brown dwarf atmospheres. The telescope’s view of three different brown dwarfs appears on the left. (Image credit: Zafar Rustamkulov/International Gemini Observatory/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA, M.H. Wong (UC Berkeley) et al. Acknowledgments: M. Zamani) "This journey has turned many of us into accidental meteorologists. We know how hard it is to predict weather on our own planet, and we realize it's going to be just as challenging to explain the phenomena we see in these bizarre, cold objects," Kirkpatrick said. "The findings are a call to action to explore even more of these dark worlds." As astronomers resond to that call to action, I will ponder how I could have worked Bauhaus' Goth classic "Bela Lugosi is Dead" into this article. The team's research was published on Sept. 28 in The Astrophysical Journal.

item.title: Crystal Palace to give Sage more time but manager under serious scrutiny

The Frenchman’s future was in serious doubt after his side conceded three times inside the opening 10 minutes before equalling the 70-year-old record for the club’s heaviest loss against their arch-rivals. The thrashing means Palace have conceded the most goals in the Premier League: 17 from seven matches. Continue reading...

item.title: 'Police weren't overwhelmed by people protesting and marching' about education and cost of living
item.description: Oliver Farry is pleased to welcome Andrew Smith, Lecturer in Liberal Arts at Queen Mary University of London. France's escalating social unrest has exposed a troubling disconnect between legitimate popular grievances and the government's increasingly security-focused response. Smith argues that the violence accompanying otherwise largely peaceful demonstrations reveals serious failures of policing, while President Emmanuel Macron's response offers "very little of substance." Drawing parallels with France's historic protest movements, Smith identifies a "convergence of causes" rooted in economic insecurity, educational inequalities and political paralysis. He warns that a repressive response risks deepening the crisis, calling instead for a renewed commitment to "participatory social democracy."

item.title: Makinde campaign knocks Tinubu over poverty, N166.7trn debt
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The Makinde-Daura Presidential Campaign Organisation (MDPCO) has accused President Bola Tinubu’s administration of pushing Nigeria towards collapse, citing widespread poverty, mounting public debt and worsening insecurity. The organisation said the country’s economic hardship and declining public confidence demanded a change of direction, urging Nigerians to consider Oyo State Governor Seyi Makinde’s proposed RESET NIGERIA agenda. In a statement by its Director of Strategic Communications, Richard Nnanna Ihediwa, on Monday, the campaign organisation cited a World Bank estimate that about 140 million Nigerians were living in poverty, accusing the All Progressives Congress (APC) administration of failing to ease citizens’ hardship. It also faulted the Federal Government’s borrowing strategy, citing public debt of about N166.7 trillion and plans to secure another $1.5 billion in World Bank financing. “President Tinubu is burying Nigeria by instalment, saddling the nation with a debt burden her future generation won’t be able to pay,” the organisation said. The MDPCO warned that continued borrowing without a clear repayment strategy could deepen the country’s economic difficulties, arguing that mounting debt had yet to translate into meaningful improvements in citizens’ lives. It also cited poor educational outcomes and Nigeria’s infrastructure deficit as evidence of the country’s development challenges, while accusing the administration of weakening public confidence through its handling of the economy and security. Describing the 2027 presidential election as an opportunity to change the country’s direction, the organisation said Makinde’s RESET NIGERIA agenda would prioritise economic growth, transparency, social stability and reforms in education, security and productive sectors. The campaign organisation urged Nigerians to use their votes to demand accountability and determine the country’s political future. The post Makinde campaign knocks Tinubu over poverty, N166.7trn debt appeared first on Vanguard News .
