item.title: CALC faults AAC over declaration of court as campaign venue
item.description: Group warns against actions capable of disrupting judicial proceedings By Dapo Akinrefon The Centre for Advocacy for Credible Leadership (CALC) has criticised the African Action Congress (AAC) for declaring the environs of the Federal High Court and the Federal Ministry of Justice in Abuja as official campaign venues for October, warning against actions capable of undermining public order and disrupting judicial proceedings. The group, in a statement issued by its Secretary-General, Mr Samuel Kolawole, described the AAC’s announcement as an irresponsible political provocation that could turn sensitive judicial and government institutions into centres of political confrontation. CALC said political parties must exercise restraint as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections, stressing that political activities should not threaten public safety or the independence of judicial institutions. The group expressed particular concern over the AAC’s planned mobilisation of supporters to the Federal High Court on Monday, October 19, 2026, saying the move could heighten tensions around the court. “While every political party and citizen has the constitutional right to express grievances, criticise government policies and demand justice, such rights must be exercised within the limits of the law,” the statement said. It added that freedom of expression and peaceful assembly should not be used to justify disrupting court proceedings, intimidating public institutions or creating conditions for a breakdown of law and order. Addressing the party’s position on the legal proceedings involving its presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, CALC said the appropriate response to any perceived politically motivated litigation was to pursue lawful remedies through the courts. “A political party cannot unilaterally transform the premises of a court or a government ministry into campaign grounds simply because its candidate is involved in litigation,” the group said. CALC maintained that the rule of law must take precedence over political mobilisation and warned against attempts to turn public institutions into arenas for partisan confrontation. The organisation also raised concerns about the implications of heightened political tensions ahead of the 2027 elections, saying any strategy that encourages confrontational mobilisation or hostility around state institutions warranted public scrutiny. It cautioned, however, that suspicions of attempts by anti-democratic forces, within or outside Nigeria, to undermine democratic institutions must be supported by credible evidence and subjected to proper investigation. The group urged Nigerians, particularly young people and political party supporters, to avoid mobilisation that could expose them to unlawful conduct, violent confrontations or the disruption of judicial proceedings. It also called on the AAC leadership to reconsider the implications of its announcement and ensure that its activities did not obstruct access
item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: Group warns against actions capable of disrupting judicial proceedings By Dapo Akinrefon The Centre for Advocacy for Credible Leadership (CALC) has criticised the African Action Congress (AAC) for declaring the environs of the Federal High Court and the Federal Ministry of Justice in Abuja as official campaign venues for October, warning against actions capable of undermining public order and disrupting judicial proceedings. The group, in a statement issued by its Secretary-General, Mr Samuel Kolawole, described the AAC’s announcement as an irresponsible political provocation that could turn sensitive judicial and government institutions into centres of political confrontation. CALC said political parties must exercise restraint as the country prepares for the 2027 general elections, stressing that political activities should not threaten public safety or the independence of judicial institutions. The group expressed particular concern over the AAC’s planned mobilisation of supporters to the Federal High Court on Monday, October 19, 2026, saying the move could heighten tensions around the court. “While every political party and citizen has the constitutional right to express grievances, criticise government policies and demand justice, such rights must be exercised within the limits of the law,” the statement said. It added that freedom of expression and peaceful assembly should not be used to justify disrupting court proceedings, intimidating public institutions or creating conditions for a breakdown of law and order. Addressing the party’s position on the legal proceedings involving its presidential candidate, Omoyele Sowore, CALC said the appropriate response to any perceived politically motivated litigation was to pursue lawful remedies through the courts. “A political party cannot unilaterally transform the premises of a court or a government ministry into campaign grounds simply because its candidate is involved in litigation,” the group said. CALC maintained that the rule of law must take precedence over political mobilisation and warned against attempts to turn public institutions into arenas for partisan confrontation. The organisation also raised concerns about the implications of heightened political tensions ahead of the 2027 elections, saying any strategy that encourages confrontational mobilisation or hostility around state institutions warranted public scrutiny. It cautioned, however, that suspicions of attempts by anti-democratic forces, within or outside Nigeria, to undermine democratic institutions must be supported by credible evidence and subjected to proper investigation. The group urged Nigerians, particularly young people and political party supporters, to avoid mobilisation that could expose them to unlawful conduct, violent confrontations or the disruption of judicial proceedings. It also called on the AAC leadership to reconsider the implications of its announcement and ensure that its activities did not obstruct access to the courts, interfere with the administration of justice or endanger judges, court personnel, lawyers, security officers and other citizens. CALC urged the Nigeria Police Force, the Department of State Services and other relevant security agencies to take preventive measures to protect the Federal High Court, the Federal Ministry of Justice and surrounding public facilities. It further called for the investigation of credible threats of violence, intimidation or organised disruption, insisting that anyone found to have engaged in criminal conduct should be dealt with in accordance with the law, regardless of political affiliation or status. The group stressed that any security response must remain professional, impartial and proportionate, with due respect for citizens’ constitutional rights to peaceful assembly and lawful expression. “The objective must be to prevent violence and preserve public order, not to suppress legitimate political opposition,” it said. CALC reiterated that Nigeria’s democratic process should be guided by constitutional procedures, peaceful political competition and credible elections rather than intimidation or attempts to draw public institutions into political confrontations. It urged political actors to avoid rhetoric and strategies capable of inflaming tensions ahead of the 2027 elections, adding that the polls must take place in an atmosphere of peace, security and respect for the law. item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.title: Uber dodges £340M cabbie lawsuit after drivers miss legal deadline
item.description: Uber has dodged a £340 million lawsuit brought by thousands of London black cab drivers after a High Court judge ruled that they'd left it too late to sue. Monday's ruling kills off two claims involving around 13,000 cabbies and former private hire companies Kabbee and Iride, which accused Uber of misleading Transport for London (TfL) to secure its operating license. The cabbies wanted nearly £200 million in compensation for lost earnings, while Kabbee and Iride sought another £140 million. But the court never got as far as deciding whether Uber had done anything wrong. The claims were filed in May and June 2024, but Mr Justice Simon Birt ruled they were too late under the six-year time limit. The cabbies insisted that they hadn't had enough evidence to allege fraud until June 2018, but the judge wasn't buying it. According to the judgment, seen by The Register, three cabbies had already filed their own claims against Uber in September 2017. Litigation funder Harbour approached law firm Mishcon de Reya about a larger lawsuit that December, and by February 2018, the Licensed Taxi Drivers' Association was telling members about the planned action. The dispute dates back to Uber's arrival in London in 2012. The claimants alleged that the company deliberately misled TfL about how its booking system worked, allowing it to operate when it shouldn't have been permitted to do so. Uber has some history here. In a separate licensing appeal in 2018, the company admitted that it gave TfL and the High Court false information about how bookings were accepted through its app. The magistrate stopped short of finding dishonesty, however, and granted Uber a new 15-month license. The judgment also revisits Greyball, Uber's software for identifying suspected regulators, and Ripley, a tool used to remotely lock computers during regulatory visits. Uber maintained that Ripley hadn't been used that way in the UK. The cabbies insisted that they needed information from the June 2018 licensing appeal to support their fraud allegations. Justice Birt disagreed, finding that enough information had been available earlier to bring a claim. Things then went quiet. Mishcon sent Uber a letter before action in July 2019, but Harbour pulled its funding that November. The claimants didn't write to Uber again about the potential lawsuit for another four and a half years, according to the judgment, and by the time proceedings began in 2024, the deadline had passed. The ruling is a victory for Uber, but doesn't clear it of the alleged fraud. The judge dismissed the claims because they were filed too late, without deciding whether the allegations, which Uber denies, were true. Neither Uber nor RGL Management, the company representing the cabbies, responded to The Register’s questions. London's taxi wars are far from over. Minicab Drivers are now pushing back against plans to bring robotaxis to the capital, warning that driverless cars could put thousands of jobs at risk. Uber is working with British autonomous driving startup Wayve on driverless technology. Having spent years battling London's cabbies for passengers, it's now helping develop cars that won't need drivers at all. ®

item.title: Disney found a way to buy Character.AI without buying its lawsuits
item.description: This week, Character.AI declared bankruptcy. While some saw the fall of a chatbot platform as a harbinger for the industry , court filings indicate that the decision was actually a key part of a deal that has let Disney hire most of Character.AI’s staff—including its now former CEO Karandeep Anand —potentially acquire most of Character.AI’s technology , and avoid the beleaguered startup’s many legal liabilities and obligations. In the past few years, Character.AI has faced multiple private lawsuits over the safety of its chatbots, as well as investigations from regulators around the world. In a declaration filed as part of the bankruptcy, Character.AI’s newly appointed CEO explained that the goal of the bankruptcy was to reach a “consensual resolution” with personal injury claimants and a group of states investigating the company, while maximizing the value of the company’s assets for shareholders. The Disney deal seems to be structured so that whatever is left of Character.AI will retain responsibility for those legal battles, some of which are still ongoing. Read full article Comments

item.title: Inflation: Jigawa to increase NYSC members’ allowance — Namadi
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Government has announced plans to increase the ₦5,000 monthly allowance paid to National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) members serving in the state to cushion the effects of rising inflation. Governor Umar Namadi disclosed this while addressing Batch C corps members at the Yakubu Gowon NYSC Orientation Camp in Fanisau, Dutse. Namadi acknowledged the contributions of corps members to community development, saying the government would review their allowance to improve their welfare amid rising living costs. “We are aware of your contributions in our communities. Therefore, we will look into and review your monthly allowance to help you manage the effects of recent inflation,” he said. He commended President Bola Tinubu’s administration for increasing the federal monthly allowance for corps members to ₦77,000, assuring them that Jigawa would also review its payment. “On our part, we will follow the footsteps of the Federal Government to review and increase your monthly state allowance,” he added. The governor also announced a one-off settlement allowance of ₦10,000 for each corps member at the end of the three-week orientation programme to assist them in moving to their primary places of assignment. “We will also give each of you ₦10,000 so that when you are posted to your various primary places of assignment, you will have something in your pocket,” he said. Namadi urged ministries, departments and agencies to make adequate arrangements to receive corps members posted to their offices and ensure a smooth transition from the orientation camp to their places of primary assignment. He further pledged to renovate the orientation camp, construct a new hall and provide a standby generator to improve facilities and ensure a reliable power supply. Describing Jigawa as a peaceful state with hospitable residents, the governor encouraged corps members to integrate into their host communities and contribute meaningfully to local development. He congratulated them on their deployment to the state and wished them a successful service year. The post Inflation: Jigawa to increase NYSC members’ allowance — Namadi appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Apple’s last-gen Mac Mini with the M4 is $150 off
item.description: The front view of the Mac Mini. | Image: The Verge Best Buy has a great deal for the rest of the day on the M4 Mac Mini base model that has 16GB RAM and a 256GB SSD. Normally, it doesn’t make a ton of sense to buy the M4 model for its usual $799 price given that the newer, faster M6 version has been available from Amazon for $779.99 (originally $899) for the past couple of weeks. However, at $649 it’s a much more tempting price. The M4 Mac Mini launched at $599 in 2024, and was an incredible value. Given that this sale price makes it just $50 more than the original price instead of $200, it’s a good time to buy if you want to spend as little as possible on a modern Mac desktop. Mac Mini with M4 Where to Buy: $799 $649 at Best Buy (256GB) Aside from some impressive generational leaps in processing power, you aren’t missing out on a ton by skipping the M6 model and opting for the M4. Their design and ports are nearly identical, and with either model you’ll need to supply your own keyboard, mouse, display, webcam, etc. If you’re on the fence and can’t decide between the M4 and M6 models, I suggest checking out my colleague Antonio’s review of the M6 Mac Mini. The newer model might be well worth the extra $130 cost. Read our review of the M4 Mac Mini and the M6 Mac Mini More Verge-approved deals Today brought a big discount to LG’s C6 OLEDs lineup , particularly its bigger models. The 55-inch model is $999.99 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Costco (previously $1,399.99), costing a little less than the 42- and 48-inch configurations. The price hasn’t gone below $1,299.99 before, so it’s a good time to consider an upgrade. The 65-inch model is cheaper than before, too. Previously $1,699.99, but normally selling for $1,500 or so, you can grab the larger version for $1,399.99 at Amazon , Best Buy , and Costco . If you have a big room and budget, the 77-inch LG C6H that, like the 48-inch version, has a tandem OLED panel that offers more brightness and better colors, is $1,999.99 , down from $2,499.99. For $499.99, you can grab a 14-inch HP OmniBook 3 during Best Buy’s deal of the day that has a 2K OLED screen, a capable Snapdragon X ARM processor, 16GB of RAM, and a 256GB SSD. This seems like a fantastic option for anyone on a budget. Its Snapdragon processor can run most x86 Windows 11 apps without much issue, and it’s just a rarity to get these kinds of specs — from the OLED screen to the RAM amount — at $500. My colleague Antonio reviewed the 16-inch version that cuts some corners in the screen department compared to this 14-inch model. It’s time to get spooky if you haven’t already planned your run of games for Halloween. The spectacular Silent Hill 2 remake is down to $21.34 on Steam for PC via Fanatical , a third-party site I’ve shopped from numerous times. If you’re alright with spending more, Resident Evil Requiem is one of Capcom’s several great 2026 games, and it’s $20 off at Amazon on all platforms, costing $49.99.

item.title: Things to know about late ex-Delta gov Uduaghan
item.description: Former Governor of Delta State, Dr. Emmanuel Uduaghan, is dead. Uduaghan passed away on the morning of Monday, according to a press statement by Toju Uduaghan, on behalf of the family. It partly read, “It is with hearts weighed down by immeasurable grief and profound sorrow that we announce the passing to glory of our beloved Father, Brother, Uncle, and Patriarch, His Excellency, Dr. Chief Emmanuel Eweta Uduaghan, former Governor of Delta State, who departed this world on the morning of 19th October 2026. “His passing has left us devastated. Words can hardly express the depth of our sorrow at the loss of a man who meant so much to our family and whose life and service touched countless others across Delta State and Nigeria.” Things to know about late Uduaghan He was born on 22 October 1954 in Warri North Local Government Area of Delta State. He attended Baptist Primary School, Mosogar, between 1961 and 1966; Federal Government College, Warri, between 1968 and 1974; and the University of Benin between 1975 and 1980, earning a Bachelor of Medicine and Surgery (MBBS) degree and a Diploma in Anaesthesia. He was posted to Kwara State for the mandatory one-year National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in 1981. Between 1989 and 1994, late Uduaghan served in a number of healthcare facilities, such as Shell Clinic Ogunu, Westend Hospital Warri and Benoni Clinic Benin City, Edo State. On return to democracy in 1999, he was appointed as commissioner for health in Delta state. In 2003, Uduaghan was appointed Secretary to the Delta State Government. In 2007, he was elected as governor of Delta State and subsequently re-elected in 2011. On 29 August 2018, he officially announced he had left PDP for APC and returned to the party in 2020. He returned to the APC again in 2025 The post Things to know about late ex-Delta gov Uduaghan appeared first on Vanguard News .

He was posted to Kwara State for the mandatory one-year National Youth Service Corps (NYSC) in 1981. Between 1989 and 1994, late Uduaghan served in a number of healthcare facilities, such as Shell Clinic Ogunu, Westend Hospital Warri and Benoni Clinic Benin City, Edo State. On return to democracy in 1999, he was appointed as commissioner for health in Delta state. In 2003, Uduaghan was appointed Secretary to the Delta State Government. In 2007, he was elected as governor of Delta State and subsequently re-elected in 2011. On 29 August 2018, he officially announced he had left PDP for APC and returned to the party in 2020. He returned to the APC again in 2025 The post Things to know about late ex-Delta gov Uduaghan appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: A Chinese rocket deorbited over Minnesota and left this in a farmer's cornfield
item.description: About a month ago, a Chinese rocket took off from a remote spaceport in the Gobi Desert, released 10 satellites into orbit, then reignited its engine and put itself on a trajectory to rain down debris over the American Midwest. The rocket's flight on September 15 lasted between 75 and 80 minutes, and it came down without completing a full orbit of the Earth. Social media posts at the time showed streaks of fiery debris falling from the sky, heading north over Kansas toward Minnesota . The overnight spectacle was also visible on the western horizon from Wisconsin . The exact time, location, and direction of the debris allowed experts to connect it to the launch of a Zhuque-2E rocket, a medium-lift vehicle built by a Chinese company called LandSpace. The rocket had launched from Dongfeng, a commercial launch zone co-located with the military-run Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwestern China, less than two hours before. Read full article Comments

item.title: ‘Leaving England is scary but I’m here to win’: Charlie Cresswell on Ligue 1 life and his international dream
item.description: The centre-back could not see a way forward at Leeds so moved to France. Now he’s preparing for the biggest game of his life against Juventus By Get French Football News “Leaving England is such a scary, scary decision,” says Charlie Cresswell. It is a decision that he never thought he would make. His father Richard made a career as a journeyman footballer in England; his brother Alfie was coming through Leeds’ academy; Charlie was already on the fringes of the Yorkshire club’s first team when the opportunity to join Toulouse arose in 2024. “That was the biggest decision I made in football,” he says. “I’ve been a Leeds fan since I was eight. I’d been at the club since I was 10 but, looking back, I was 20 years old with no games, and I needed to get out and go play,” says Cresswell, now at Rennes and preparing to face Juventus in the Europa League. Continue reading...

item.title: Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle Becomes Nigeria’s Youngest Female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at 40
item.description: Judicial portrait of Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN, partner at Afe Babalola & Co., who made history as Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria at the age of 40. Nigeria’s legal landscape has witnessed a momentous record as Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun – Adekunle joins the prestigious Inner Bar, officially becoming the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN) in history. Attaining the highly coveted Silk rank at the age of 40, the seasoned advocate and solicitor of the Supreme Court of Nigeria has broken a long-standing ceiling, setting a inspiring milestone for women across the legal profession and beyond. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, MCIArb, is a distinguished partner at the renowned law firm Afe Babalola & Co. (Emmanuel Chambers). With a career spanning over 14 years of legal practice, she specialises in complex litigation, commercial dispute resolution, strategic legal advisory, and international arbitration. Olamide Ehinfun-Adekunle SAN following her elevation as the youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria. Her academic foundation includes a Bachelor of Laws (LL.B.) degree from Obafemi Awolowo University, Ile-Ife, and a Master of Laws (LL.M.) in International Trade Law from the University of Leeds, United Kingdom. Before joining Afe Babalola & Co. as a Partner in September 2013, her professional experience included key positions at D. D. Dodo & Co. and the Nuhu Ribadu Campaign Organisation. Her historic elevation to Senior Advocate of Nigeria—a position reserved for legal practitioners who have distinguished themselves through exceptional skill, professional integrity, and significant contributions to Nigerian jurisprudence—marks a defining moment in contemporary law. Taking on the rank at 40 years old, she stands out as the youngest female lawyer to achieve this honour in Nigeria, carving a clear path for future generations of female lawyers to aim for the highest levels of leadership in the country’s judiciary and private bar. Olamide Mojigbotoluwa Ehinfun-Adekunle, Nigeria’s youngest female Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN). item.content:encoded: Today, I’m talking with Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker, who has a lot of thoughts about AI, tech, and privacy. If you’ve been listening to the show, you know that one of my running theories is that those issues are driving a big and maybe kind of unexpected political realignment — and with the midterms coming up next month, and early voting already underway in a lot of places, the stakes are pretty high right now. So I asked Gov. Pritzker about all that, and he was surprisingly willing to dive right into the absolute existential weeds of what government is even for. You’ll hear him say — and it’s hard to disagree — that some problems are just collective action problems that require the government to do a lot of work. We can’t solve all these problems one at a time, or even one state at a time. It’s a pretty deep conversation, and we really got into it on a lot of issues. And of course, I had to ask him: Are the Bears gonna stay in Illinois? Before we get going, do me a favor and subscribe to Decoder on YouTube , where we put out new episodes every Monday and Thursday. Okay: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker. Here we go. Gov. JB Pritzker, you’re the governor of Illinois. Welcome to Decoder . Thanks, Nilay. Great to be with you. I am very excited to talk to you. We’re in the heart of midterm season. You are running for reelection. I have to tell you. I have to be very honest with you. I personally feel a lot of pressure in this interview, not only because I’m speaking to a governor, but because I went to school in Chicago. My sister still lives in Chicago. My wife grew up in Illinois. Her entire family is farmers in North Central Illinois. Boy, do I have a list of questions for you. I have to do a good job here. Well, we’re claiming you. Now that I know all that, we’re claiming you. You’re an Illinoisan. Verge subscribers, don’t forget you get exclusive access to ad-free Decoder wherever you get your podcasts. Head here . Not a subscriber? You can sign up here . I don’t know about that. I grew up in Wisconsin. Here’s my first question for you. I’m a die-hard Packers fan. Are you going to let the Bears move to Indiana? That is not our intention. We are, in fact, in discussions with the Bears and the NFL about keeping the Bears either in Chicago or in Arlington Heights, but in Illinois. I’m saying, as a Packers fan, nothing is funnier than the outcome of the Bears moving to Indiana. I just want to put that out there. Openly biased in this case — I own two shares of that stock — but I’m going to make the comparison here. And the reason I started there is not only because I think that’s a funny outcome, although I do, but it feels like we are in the middle of a generational political realignment. I’m sure you feel that, in this election campaign, the idea of big business and how that should interact with the government, and how the government should be able to push back on big business and not give in to big business. All of that feels up for grabs. And the comparison I will make in this specific case is your fellow governor, Gavin Newsom, in California. They sued the Ellison family, Paramount, over the Warner Brothers merger. Paramount threatened to leave. They made a lot of noise about Nashville, Texas, Miami, or wherever you make noise about these days, and it feels like Newsom caved. It feels like he pressured his Attorney General, Rob Bonta, to settle that lawsuit and keep them there. They settled the lawsuit. The next day, the Ellison family is like, “We never… We’re from California. We would never leave.” I see a parallel here with the Bears that is connected to that larger realignment, how government and business should interact. Do you see that parallel? Do you feel that realignment? Well, what I can tell you is we’re pretty tough negotiators in Chicago and Illinois, and that’s really what we’re in the midst of now with the Bears. But I understand your point about realignment. I mean, there is a generational change, and I think it’s also an attitudinal change about protecting taxpayers, protecting people who frankly are among the most vulnerable to all the technology that’s overtaking people’s lives and invading people’s homes. And so I do believe that the government has to be more active now and become a fighter for our people and not just a collaborator with business on everything. I’m a businessman, as you know, before I became governor. But I also know that, for the people of Illinois anyway, my job is to protect the working people of this state who often don’t have anybody protecting them except a government that will stand up for them. So that’s kind of the realignment that I see. And that generational shift, I agree with you. It’s partly a Democratic Party generational shift. Generationally, we’re a little more aggressive. And I’m probably older than the next generation that’s already possibly taking office this November. I’m 61 years old, but I think of myself as having come out of the tech world and as somebody who has been a fighter for progressive values that, yeah, we’ve got to become more aggressive and make sure we’re standing up for our people. There are two places where I see the realignment in particular. One is data centers, one is privacy, and you just see that as a bipartisan backlash to those things. I would actually add a third, which is antitrust broadly. It’s weird if you go into Silicon Valley. David Sacks is retweeting Lina Khan from the Biden administration talking about whether the AI industry needs an antitrust exemption to manage safety. They both agree that these companies don’t need antitrust exemptions. They actually should be more competitive. Again, putting that in the context of regulating these companies, thinking about the dynamic between the government and the biggest companies in the world. I’ll just ask the question, I guess, more directly. Do you think Newsom was right to give in to Paramount, or do you think he should have forced them to make good on that threat to leave? I can’t speak to the Paramount situation well enough to give you an answer, so it would be unfair for me to do so. I can say once again that our orientation today — and I think about the big AI companies and the big social media companies as well — has to be like, wait a minute, too much power in too few hands. Particularly when we talk about AI, where it’s potentially existential, but certainly transformative, which is probably a kind way to say it about the economy, that we’re going to have to get very engaged. Guardrails, of course, on both parts, but also addressing what I think on the AI front is potentially a significant change in employment in the United States. I’m not somebody who is necessarily convinced that we have to see a whole bunch of job loss, but that does feel like that’s the direction this is going. What I’m suggesting is we better be prepared, and we better be protecting people who are going to lose their jobs, or at least it appears they’re going to lose their jobs. And I’ll just give you this thought. If these days 4 percent unemployment is kind of the acceptable near full employment number, I think the problem we’re going to see is — if that’s sort of the level that we’re going to hopefully aim for and stay at — that in very short order, we could end up at 7 percent and have that be the baseline, or maybe 10 percent. And if you think about what’s happened, the upheavals of economies and of governments when you get to 10 percent unemployment in any country. We better be focused on how we’re going to give people the dignity of work and enough income so that they can make a life for themselves when you’re going to put people out of work by virtue of this technology. By the way, much of the benefit of that is going to go to a very, very few people. So we’ve got to wrestle with that and come to a conclusion. item.title: NMA president condemns attacks on doctors, demands safe workplaces
item.description: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The President of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Prof. Afekhide Ernest Omoti, has condemned the rising cases of threats, intimidation and physical assaults against healthcare workers in the country, calling for stronger measures to guarantee their safety in the workplace. Omoti also warned that poor working conditions, inadequate remuneration and insecurity were worsening the migration of Nigerian doctors, stressing that patriotism alone could not persuade medical professionals to remain in the country. He spoke in his address to mark the 2026 Physicians’ Week, themed “Securing the Future of Medicine in Nigeria,” delivered on his behalf in Akure by the Ondo State NMA Chairman, Dr. Roland Bola Arohunmolase. According to him, the wellbeing of physicians is inseparable from their working environment, adding that doctors cannot provide compassionate care while living in fear. “A doctor cannot provide compassionate care while constantly worrying about personal safety. “The increasing incidents of threats, intimidation, assault and other forms of violence against healthcare workers are unacceptable. Hospitals must be places of healing — not theatres of violence,” he said. Omoti said the NMA would continue to demand safe workplaces, adequate protection, appropriate equipment, decent accommodation where necessary and improved conditions of service that reflect the responsibilities of the medical profession. “The safety of doctors is not negotiable. And when doctors are safe, patients are safer,” he declared. He said the association would engage governments, employers, hospital administrators, security agencies and other stakeholders to develop enforceable mechanisms for protecting healthcare workers. On the persistent brain drain in the health sector, the NMA president said doctors should not be expected to remain in Nigeria solely out of patriotism. “Patriotism should be supported by decent working conditions, professional dignity, security, competitive remuneration, opportunities for career development and a health system in which doctors can see a future for themselves and their families,” he said. He warned against a healthcare system that continually demands sacrifices from doctors without adequately addressing their welfare, noting that exhausted and stressed physicians could struggle to deliver quality care. Omoti called for improved staffing levels, adequate rest, regular medical examinations and confidential psychological support for doctors. On the future of medical practice, he advocated the integration of digital health, artificial intelligence and telemedicine into medical education and service delivery. He, however, cautioned that technological advancements should complement rather than replace the human connection between doctors and patients. item.content:encoded: By Dayo Johnson, Akure The President of the Nigerian Medical Association (NMA), Prof. Afekhide Ernest Omoti, has condemned the rising cases of threats, intimidation and physical assaults against healthcare workers in the country, calling for stronger measures to guarantee their safety in the workplace. Omoti also warned that poor working conditions, inadequate remuneration and insecurity were worsening the migration of Nigerian doctors, stressing that patriotism alone could not persuade medical professionals to remain in the country. He spoke in his address to mark the 2026 Physicians’ Week, themed “Securing the Future of Medicine in Nigeria,” delivered on his behalf in Akure by the Ondo State NMA Chairman, Dr. Roland Bola Arohunmolase. According to him, the wellbeing of physicians is inseparable from their working environment, adding that doctors cannot provide compassionate care while living in fear. “A doctor cannot provide compassionate care while constantly worrying about personal safety. “The increasing incidents of threats, intimidation, assault and other forms of violence against healthcare workers are unacceptable. Hospitals must be places of healing — not theatres of violence,” he said. Omoti said the NMA would continue to demand safe workplaces, adequate protection, appropriate equipment, decent accommodation where necessary and improved conditions of service that reflect the responsibilities of the medical profession. “The safety of doctors is not negotiable. And when doctors are safe, patients are safer,” he declared. He said the association would engage governments, employers, hospital administrators, security agencies and other stakeholders to develop enforceable mechanisms for protecting healthcare workers. On the persistent brain drain in the health sector, the NMA president said doctors should not be expected to remain in Nigeria solely out of patriotism. “Patriotism should be supported by decent working conditions, professional dignity, security, competitive remuneration, opportunities for career development and a health system in which doctors can see a future for themselves and their families,” he said. He warned against a healthcare system that continually demands sacrifices from doctors without adequately addressing their welfare, noting that exhausted and stressed physicians could struggle to deliver quality care. Omoti called for improved staffing levels, adequate rest, regular medical examinations and confidential psychological support for doctors. On the future of medical practice, he advocated the integration of digital health, artificial intelligence and telemedicine into medical education and service delivery. He, however, cautioned that technological advancements should complement rather than replace the human connection between doctors and patients. Meanwhile, Arohunmolase disclosed that Ondo State had lost more than 400 doctors to migration and other forms of attrition in the past five years, leaving about 500 doctors in public health institutions. He said the situation had worsened the doctor-to-patient ratio in the state to approximately one doctor for every 6,000 patients, placing enormous pressure on the remaining workforce. “There was a time when we had about 900 to 1,000 doctors in the system. About 400 have exited. This has placed an enormous burden on the sector,” he said. The state NMA chairman appealed to the Ondo State Government to improve doctors’ remuneration and working conditions to attract and retain medical personnel and reduce burnout. He commended Governor Lucky Aiyedatiwa for approving the new circular on doctors’ remuneration issued by the National Salaries, Incomes and Wages Commission, but noted that some states offered remuneration above the national rate to retain their doctors. Arohunmolase also attributed the high rate of medical tourism among wealthy Nigerians and politicians to inadequate healthcare infrastructure and a shortage of essential medical equipment. He lamented that Ondo State might not have up to four defibrillators, devices used to restore normal heart rhythm in certain life-threatening emergencies. According to him, many Nigerian doctors practising abroad received their training locally and possess the competence required to deliver quality healthcare, but are driven away by systemic inadequacies. He called for increased government investment in the health sector, noting that Nigeria’s estimated two to three per cent budgetary allocation to health remained far below the 15 per cent commitment under the Abuja Declaration. item.title: FG Reaffirms Commitment To Human Capital Development For Economic Growth
item.description: The Federal Government has reaffirmed its commitment to human capital development as a central pillar for economic growth, saying long-term investments in health, education, skills and livelihoods are critical to transforming Nigeria’s economy. The reaffirmation was made during a media engagement in Abuja on Monday organised to keep journalists abreast of developments under the Human Capital Development Programme (HCD) 2.0 and deepen public understanding of its role in national development. National Coordinator of the Human Capital Development 2.0 Programme, Rukayya El-Rufai, said Nigeria’s economic future depends on deliberate and sustained investment in its people. “Nigeria’s future depends on its people. If we do not invest in them, we cannot grow our economy. There’s a lot of investment going into infrastructure, but if you do not invest in human capital, you are not simply going to be able to grow your economy as much,” he said. El-Rufai explained that HCD 2.0 builds on the earlier version introduced under former Vice President Yemi Osinbajo, which focused on health, education and labour force participation. According to her, the new iteration expands the scope to include skills development and livelihoods, to address poverty, underemployment and learning poverty. She said the programme is evidence-led and tracks under-five mortality, immunisation coverage, stunting, out-of-school rates, learning poverty and youth employment as six priority indicators. “The one that worries me and scares me is that learning poverty is so high – about 70 percent,” she said. “When kids are in school, what they’re learning is not sufficient.” According to her, the programme is embedded within the National Economic Council to ensure integration with productivity and resource allocation decisions. El-Rufai noted that while the framework is national, states are expected to adapt it to their peculiar developmental challenges, stressing that there is no one-size-fits-all approach. “Each state is now developing its own HCD plan, guided by its unique challenges,” she said. She cited ongoing state-level innovations, including Imo State’s “One Child, One Business” initiative, Nasarawa State’s gender mainstreaming in its HCD plan, and Anambra State’s digital skills training and startup grants for youths. Participants at a media engagement organised to keep journalists abreast of developments under the Human Capital Development Programme (HCD) 2.0 and deepen public understanding of its role in national development, in Abuja on Monday, October 19, 2026. On sustainability, she said the Federal Government is advocating for political parties to sign a compact that treats human capital investment as a sovereign imperative that transcends administrations. item.title: Brazil court orders Meta to prove it gives Lula, Bolsonaro campaign content equal treatment
item.description: Brazil’s top electoral court has given Meta 24 hours to prove it is treating campaign content from incumbent President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva and Senator Flavio Bolsonaro equally on its online platforms, threatening a daily fine for noncompliance. The ruling follows allegations from Lula's campaign that the social media giant is suppressing Lula’s campaign content ahead of Sunday’s closely contested presidential runoff.

item.description: Shroud mushrooms are an important crafting resource in Enshrouded , but they're tricky to find. item.title: France protests draw global attention: Trump, Vance blame immigration for unrest
item.description: US President Donald Trump on Sunday blamed immigration for unrest during protests in France and urged the country to tighten its migration rules. Trump's post comes after similar comments made by Vice President JD Vance on Saturday. Vance, who is seen as a potential presidential candidate in the 2028 election, also drew a connection to upcoming midterm races for congressional seats on November 3, where Republicans are not expected to perform well. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson reports from the United States.

item.title: Alleged Rights Violation: Court dismisses El-Rufai’s N120m suit
item.description: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting at Maitama, Abuja, on Monday dismissed a fundamental rights enforcement suit brought before it by the detained former governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai. Listed as respondents in the legal action were the Department of State Services (DSS), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF). El-Rufai, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023 and as minister of the FCT under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, had accused the respondents in the suit of violating his rights. He further urged the court to invalidate letters of invitation extended to him by both the ICPC and the EFCC and demanded N120 million in damages from the respondents. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Sylvanus Oriji held that the legal action was without merit and dismissed it. The court held that the letters of invitation, which requested the former governor to appear before the federal agencies investigating allegations against him, met constitutional requirements and did not infringe his fundamental rights. The court held that the agencies acted within their mandates by inviting him to shed light on issues raised against him. Besides, the court declined to declare that the DSS’s attempt to arrest the applicant at Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport amounted to a violation of his rights. It held that the DSS has a statutory responsibility to maintain a watchlist and to arrest persons of interest. Justice Oriji held that the former governor could not use the court to stop government agencies from performing their legitimate duties. The court held that, contrary to El-Rufai’s contention, the agencies did not need a warrant to effect such an arrest. On whether the confiscation of the applicant’s international passport by the DSS was a violation of his rights, the court said it was satisfied that the seizure was lawful and carried out pursuant to the powers of the DSS. It held that the applicant failed to adduce evidence to establish that the seizure was continuous, permanent and unlawful. Consequently, aside from dismissing the case, the court awarded costs of N200,000 against the applicant in favour of each of the four respondents. It will be recalled that El-Rufai also filed another N1 billion fundamental rights enforcement suit, which is pending before the Federal High Court in Abuja. Listed as respondents in the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/345/2026, are the ICPC, the AGF and the Inspector-General of Police. He specifically challenged the legality of the warrant the ICPC relied on to search his Abuja residence. item.dc:creator: Ayobami
item.content:encoded: By Ikechukwu Nnochiri, Abuja A High Court of the Federal Capital Territory (FCT) sitting at Maitama, Abuja, on Monday dismissed a fundamental rights enforcement suit brought before it by the detained former governor of Kaduna State, Nasir El-Rufai. Listed as respondents in the legal action were the Department of State Services (DSS), the Independent Corrupt Practices and Other Related Offences Commission (ICPC), the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), and the Attorney General of the Federation (AGF). El-Rufai, who served as governor from 2015 to 2023 and as minister of the FCT under former President Olusegun Obasanjo’s administration, had accused the respondents in the suit of violating his rights. He further urged the court to invalidate letters of invitation extended to him by both the ICPC and the EFCC and demanded N120 million in damages from the respondents. Delivering judgment in the matter, Justice Sylvanus Oriji held that the legal action was without merit and dismissed it. The court held that the letters of invitation, which requested the former governor to appear before the federal agencies investigating allegations against him, met constitutional requirements and did not infringe his fundamental rights. The court held that the agencies acted within their mandates by inviting him to shed light on issues raised against him. Besides, the court declined to declare that the DSS’s attempt to arrest the applicant at Nnamdi Azikiwe Airport amounted to a violation of his rights. It held that the DSS has a statutory responsibility to maintain a watchlist and to arrest persons of interest. Justice Oriji held that the former governor could not use the court to stop government agencies from performing their legitimate duties. The court held that, contrary to El-Rufai’s contention, the agencies did not need a warrant to effect such an arrest. On whether the confiscation of the applicant’s international passport by the DSS was a violation of his rights, the court said it was satisfied that the seizure was lawful and carried out pursuant to the powers of the DSS. It held that the applicant failed to adduce evidence to establish that the seizure was continuous, permanent and unlawful. Consequently, aside from dismissing the case, the court awarded costs of N200,000 against the applicant in favour of each of the four respondents. It will be recalled that El-Rufai also filed another N1 billion fundamental rights enforcement suit, which is pending before the Federal High Court in Abuja. Listed as respondents in the suit, marked FHC/ABJ/CS/345/2026, are the ICPC, the AGF and the Inspector-General of Police. He specifically challenged the legality of the warrant the ICPC relied on to search his Abuja residence. El-Rufai is praying the court to declare that the search warrant dated February 4, which the Chief Magistrate of the Magistrate’s Court of the FCT signed to authorise the search and seizure of items from his residence, is invalid, null and void. He also sought a declaration that the search warrant was legally defective for lacking particularity and for “material drafting errors, ambiguity in execution parameters, overbreadth, and absence of probable cause, thereby constituting an unlawful and unreasonable search in violation of Section 37 of the Constitution.” Other reliefs he sought include a declaration that the invasion and search of his residence at House 12, Mambilla Street, Aso Drive, Abuja, on February 19 at about 2 p.m., executed by agents of the ICPC and the Inspector-General of Police under the invalid warrant, “amounts to a gross violation of the applicant’s fundamental rights to dignity of the human person, personal liberty, fair hearing, and privacy under Sections 34, 35, 36, and 37 of the Constitution.” The chief magistrate, who was initially listed as the 2nd respondent, was subsequently delisted from the case by the applicant. All the respondents have since urged the court to dismiss the case as lacking in merit. The post Alleged Rights Violation: Court dismisses El-Rufai’s N120m suit appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Macron kicks off three-day Gulf tour, seeks securing fuel supplies amid crisis
item.description: French President Emmanuel Macron on Monday began a Gulf tour aimed at securing oil and diesel supplies in an effort to bring down prices, after a weekend of violent protests sparked by soaring living costs. Macron, just hours after slamming France's "unbridled" violence in an address late on Sunday, arrived in OPEC member Kuwait where he was welcomed by the emir, Sheikh Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah. FRANCE 24's International Affairs Editor Kethevane Gorjestani tells us more.

item.title: BeamNG.drive Is an Astonishing Driving Sim in Search of a Game
item.description: Over those 11 years, BeamNG.drive has slowly but steadily built up a sizable audience, to the extent that it's currently the second-biggest driving game on Steam , ahead of Forza Horizon 6 and behind the mighty Euro Truck Simulator 2 . I suspect it's going to do pretty well on PS5, too. If you're into car games — and a lot of PlayStation gamers are — you don't have to spend very long on car-game YouTube before BeamNG.drive is invoked, often in pretty breathless terms. The PS5 version of Forza Horizon 6 just got pushed back to January . And PS5 might be the cheapest way to run this demanding, computationally expensive game at decent fidelity.

item.title: Sokoto ADC, APC clash over Tinubu’s INEC nominee
item.description: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State and the state government have disagreed over President Bola Tinubu’s nomination of Professor Mustapha Aliyu as an Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) National Commissioner representing the North-West, with the opposition demanding closer scrutiny of his political neutrality and the government defending his credentials. The disagreement has renewed debate over the independence of the electoral body and the need to sustain public confidence in its officials ahead of the 2027 general elections. The ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, called on Tinubu to reconsider the nomination and urged the Senate to conduct a thorough screening of Aliyu before confirming his appointment. Dan’iya, in a statement issued by his media aide, Aminu Abdullahi, cited the nominee’s reported family relationship with Governor Ahmed Aliyu and raised questions about his alleged political affiliations. He argued that appointments into INEC required transparent scrutiny to prevent doubts about the impartiality of officials responsible for conducting elections. “The independence of INEC is too important to be treated as a routine political appointment. Nigerians must have confidence that those entrusted with managing our elections will act without fear, favour or political pressure,” Dan’iya said. The ADC candidate, however, acknowledged that family ties alone did not establish wrongdoing or automatically disqualify a nominee. He said the reported relationship between the nominee and the governor made it necessary for the Senate to verify whether Aliyu met the constitutional requirements for the position. Dan’iya specifically cited Section 156(1)(a) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that a person appointed as a member of INEC must not belong to a political party. He urged the Senate to verify the nominee’s political affiliations, eligibility and ability to discharge his responsibilities without partisan influence. The ADC candidate also called on senators representing Sokoto State and the North-West to seek relevant disclosures during the screening process, insisting that the credibility of the electoral commission should take precedence over political considerations. “If credible evidence establishes that the nominee is constitutionally disqualified, the Senate should refuse confirmation, and the President should nominate a qualified alternative,” Dan’iya said. He maintained that no nominee should be exempted from scrutiny because of political connections or relationships with public officeholders. Government defends nomination The Sokoto State Government rejected the ADC candidate’s concerns, describing them as an attempt to politicise what it considers a merit-based appointment. The governor’s Special Adviser on Political Matters, Faruku Labbo, said Dan’iya should provide evidence that Aliyu belonged to the All Progress
item.dc:creator: Nwafor
item.content:encoded: By Musa Ubandawaki, Sokoto SOKOTO — The African Democratic Congress (ADC) in Sokoto State and the state government have disagreed over President Bola Tinubu’s nomination of Professor Mustapha Aliyu as an Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) National Commissioner representing the North-West, with the opposition demanding closer scrutiny of his political neutrality and the government defending his credentials. The disagreement has renewed debate over the independence of the electoral body and the need to sustain public confidence in its officials ahead of the 2027 general elections. The ADC governorship candidate in Sokoto State, Hon. Manir Muhammad Dan’iya, called on Tinubu to reconsider the nomination and urged the Senate to conduct a thorough screening of Aliyu before confirming his appointment. Dan’iya, in a statement issued by his media aide, Aminu Abdullahi, cited the nominee’s reported family relationship with Governor Ahmed Aliyu and raised questions about his alleged political affiliations. He argued that appointments into INEC required transparent scrutiny to prevent doubts about the impartiality of officials responsible for conducting elections. “The independence of INEC is too important to be treated as a routine political appointment. Nigerians must have confidence that those entrusted with managing our elections will act without fear, favour or political pressure,” Dan’iya said. The ADC candidate, however, acknowledged that family ties alone did not establish wrongdoing or automatically disqualify a nominee. He said the reported relationship between the nominee and the governor made it necessary for the Senate to verify whether Aliyu met the constitutional requirements for the position. Dan’iya specifically cited Section 156(1)(a) of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, which provides that a person appointed as a member of INEC must not belong to a political party. He urged the Senate to verify the nominee’s political affiliations, eligibility and ability to discharge his responsibilities without partisan influence. The ADC candidate also called on senators representing Sokoto State and the North-West to seek relevant disclosures during the screening process, insisting that the credibility of the electoral commission should take precedence over political considerations. “If credible evidence establishes that the nominee is constitutionally disqualified, the Senate should refuse confirmation, and the President should nominate a qualified alternative,” Dan’iya said. He maintained that no nominee should be exempted from scrutiny because of political connections or relationships with public officeholders. Government defends nomination The Sokoto State Government rejected the ADC candidate’s concerns, describing them as an attempt to politicise what it considers a merit-based appointment. The governor’s Special Adviser on Political Matters, Faruku Labbo, said Dan’iya should provide evidence that Aliyu belonged to the All Progressives Congress (APC) or held a party position that could constitute a constitutional impediment to his nomination. In a statement on Sunday, Labbo maintained that the nominee’s family relationship with Governor Ahmed Aliyu was insufficient, on its own, to establish constitutional disqualification. “Although Professor Mustapha Aliyu remains a brother to Governor Ahmed Aliyu Sokoto, he is not holding any position in the All Progressives Congress at any level,” Labbo said. He described Aliyu as a distinguished academic qualified for national service and urged the public and the Senate to assess the nomination based on the professor’s professional credentials, constitutional eligibility and capacity to perform the role impartially. Labbo also argued that the nomination was intended to fill vacancies arising from the expiration of the tenures of serving electoral commissioners, and should not be interpreted as an attempt to advance the political interests of the Sokoto State Government or any individual. The government’s response followed the Presidency’s announcement on October 16, 2026, of Aliyu’s nomination alongside those of other national commissioners and resident electoral commissioners. The nominations are subject to the applicable constitutional procedures, including Senate confirmation where required. The disagreement has brought renewed attention to the standards of transparency, political neutrality and accountability expected of officials appointed to oversee Nigeria’s elections. As political parties intensify preparations for the 2027 general elections, the Senate’s screening process is expected to attract public scrutiny, with the ADC insisting that the nominee’s eligibility and political neutrality must be established and the state government maintaining that his nomination should not be discredited solely on the basis of family ties. The nominee’s eligibility and the applicable constitutional requirements remain matters for assessment through the appropriate procedures. The post Sokoto ADC, APC clash over Tinubu’s INEC nominee appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Konsa bullish about Arsenal’s Champions League hopes as Bayern clash looms
item.description: Centre-back has settled right in at Arsenal and is looking ‘to win everything’, starting with Wednesday’s duel against Harry Kane For Ezri Konsa, it was just a wonderfully satisfying challenge. The Nottingham Forest striker Liam Delap had stolen in behind him up the inside left channel on Sunday. There were 93 minutes gone, Arsenal were 1-0 up and it was now or never for Forest. Konsa decreed that it would be never, curving his covering run back, matching Delap for pace and stretching into the perfect block tackle. So, another win for Arsenal : their 10th in 11 matches this season. Another clean sheet. And for Konsa, a continuation of what has been a dreamlike couple of months. Do points-saving last-minute challenges mean more when the defender is actually a fan of the club, too? Basically, yes. Continue reading...

item.title: Elephant Island is an icy sight from orbit | Space photo of the day for Oct. 19, 2026
item.description: null Ice floats by in West Antarctica as winter comes to an end in the Southern Hemisphere. (Image credit: contains modified Copernicus Sentinel data (2026), processed by ESA) Antarctica is a magnificent sight, and that beauty is visible all the way from space. What is it? Orbiting planet Earth, the European Space Agency's (ESA) Copernicus Sentinel-3 mission captured a close-up of West Antarctica. Winter is ending in the Southern Hemisphere, meaning this is the peak of icy weather and sea ice in the Arctic. In this image snapped by Sentinel-3, you can see a massive swath of ice which includes Elephant Island on the left-hand side. An ice-covered island off the Antarctic coast, Elephant Island floats in the Southern Ocean. It got its name both from the island's shape, which some liken to that of an elephant's head, and the fact that the island is home to a community of elephant seals. Why is it incredible? While a seal-inhabited island on the left floats near the Antarctic coast, across the water is a vast, frozen landscape. In just this snapshot, you can see about between 746 and 1,056 miles (1,200 to 1,700 kilometers) of the icy continent. This image was captured on Sept. 30, 2026. In the Southern Hemisphere, that was just past the end of winter. The absolute peak for sea ice in Antarctica fell just a couple weeks before, on Sept. 14, according to the National Snow and Ice Data Center, ESA reported . So in this one snapshot, we can see a near-maximum for sea ice in the Antarctic, spanning hundreds of miles. In observing our own planet from space, we are able to peer across vast landscapes, capturing important observational data. This is especially critical for the Antarctic as, with the progression of climate change , this sea ice continues to dwindle , adding to sea level rise among other serious consequences across the planet.

item.title: US midterms elections: Why data centers are becoming a key issue
item.description: With the US midterm elections just weeks away, data centers are emerging as a major political issue for both Republicans and Democrats. There are about 3,000 facilities currently operating in the country. With that number potentially doubling in the coming years, concern – and, in some cases, anger – is growing among voters. FRANCE 24's Fraser Jackson report from West Virginia.

item.description: A hacker broke into more than 100 websites using an army of AI agents that mostly operated on their own, according to findings from the AI security firm Norforge . At the same time, rogue AI agents are carrying out attacks of their own after escaping from testing environments. item.content:encoded: …Oyebanji promises equipment, medical personnel By Rotimi Ojomoyela ADO-EKITI — United Nigeria Airlines has constructed and handed over a community health centre, a solar-powered borehole and a perimeter fence to the Ekiti State Government as part of its corporate social responsibility initiative. The facilities, located in Aso-Ayegunle, Ado-Ekiti, were commissioned by Governor Biodun Oyebanji, who pledged that the state government would equip the centre, provide medical personnel and integrate it into the state’s primary healthcare system. Speaking at the commissioning ceremony, Chairman of United Nigeria Airlines, Prof. Obiora Okonkwo, said the intervention was designed to ensure that communities benefited directly from the airline’s presence and business operations in the state. He said the project demonstrated the importance of public-private partnerships in addressing community needs, particularly where government resources alone might not be sufficient to provide essential infrastructure. Okonkwo commended Oyebanji for creating an enabling environment for private-sector participation in the state’s development, describing the governor’s approach to collaboration with businesses as a key factor behind the initiative. He explained that the Ekiti State Government had selected United Nigeria Airlines as its preferred carrier after assessing its operational capacity and services. According to him, the company decided to reciprocate the confidence reposed in it by investing in the welfare of residents rather than simply operating its business without making a meaningful contribution to the host community. The airline chairman said the company had undertaken similar interventions in other parts of the country, including providing relief to communities affected by flooding in Bayelsa State and supporting projects in Anambra State. He described the Aso-Ayegunle project as particularly significant because of its connection with the airline’s relationship with the Ekiti State Government and the development opportunities associated with the state’s aviation sector. “As a matter of fact, most communities where we operate have benefited from our presence. We have carried out interventions in different locations and at various stations. Some of these communities have experienced calamities. “I remember when there was flooding in Bayelsa State; we were there to provide relief. In Anambra State, we have also undertaken several projects, and we have done similar things in other places. More interventions are still in the pipeline for areas we have not yet covered,” Okonkwo said. He said the project reflected the state government’s commitment to working with private businesses to deliver development. “This project is special. It is special because of what we found when we came to this community. It is also special because the governor of this state has demonstrated extraordinary commitment to public-private partnerships. His support has been amazing. He has a vision of defining the role of government while allowing the private sector to do business,” he said. Okonkwo explained that the airline was approached by the state government after it conducted due diligence on the company’s operations and fleet. “There was no application and no interview. They conducted their due diligence and reached out to us. They were satisfied that the services we offer and the fleet we have could meet their needs. We were touched by the confidence they reposed in us, and we felt we should show the world that this kind of partnership works. That is why we have come here with this special intervention,” he said. He also highlighted the airline’s support for tourism in Ekiti, disclosing that members of its delegation visited Ikogosi Warm Springs during their stay in the state. The airline chairman expressed optimism that the partnership would create further opportunities, particularly as Ekiti develops its capacity to export agricultural products. “Our mission and commitment to this state do not end with this commissioning. I believe this is just the beginning of the good things that will come out of this relationship. We have made a commitment, and as the state develops, particularly in the area of exporting agricultural products, I will be ready to provide the necessary support when the opportunity arises,” he said. In his remarks, Oyebanji thanked the airline’s management and staff for the investment, describing the project as a valuable contribution to the government’s efforts to expand access to primary healthcare. The governor explained that the arrangement required the airline to construct the facility, while the state government would be responsible for equipping and operating it. He promised that the Ministry of Health would ensure that the centre was adequately staffed, supplied and integrated into the existing primary healthcare system. Oyebanji also urged residents to take ownership of the facility, protect the infrastructure and ensure that it served its intended purpose. He said the centre would reduce the burden on residents who previously had to travel considerable distances to access medical services, particularly pregnant women, nursing mothers and children. The Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe, described the commissioning as a significant development for Aso-Ayegunle. The monarch recalled the initial resistance that greeted the acquisition of land for the airport and urged residents to protect the health centre and prevent the facility from deteriorating. He stressed that the community had a collective responsibility to preserve infrastructure provided for its welfare. Also speaking, a community representative, Fajuyi Olumide, described the project as a major development for Aso-Ayegunle and thanked the airline and the state government for the intervention. Olumide said the facility had raised hopes among residents who, according to him, had waited for greater development and government presence in the community. He expressed optimism that the project would be followed by other interventions capable of improving residents’ living conditions. item.title: Nancy Isime, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere & More Star in Loving Itohan | Watch Trailer
item.description: Nancy Isime in traditional Edo wedding attire on the set of her debut executive producer film Loving Itohan. Remember when Nancy Isime announced she was stepping into the shoes of an executive producer for her very first feature film? Well, the moment is finally here, and we have our first real look at what she has been cooking up! The Nollywood favourite has unveiled the trailer for Loving Itohan , giving us a front-row seat to a drama packed with romance, secrets, and tough personal choices. The story centres on Itohan, a woman caught in a web of emotional conflict and hidden truths that threaten to turn her world upside down. As unexpected situations force her to make tough choices between her heart and her reality, she has to navigate what love truly demands when secrets begin to surface. Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe on set for Loving Itohan, in cinemas 6 November 2026. Sharing the trailer, Nancy Isime could not contain her excitement over bringing the story to life: It’s finally here! We’re excited to introduce you to our baby, Loving Itohan! After so much love, hard work, and dedication, we can finally share a little piece of this story with you. The official trailer is out, and we can’t wait for you to meet Itohan and fall in love with her story, just as we have. Directed by Orobosa Ikponmwen and produced by Emmanuel Izuoba alongside Nancy Isime as executive producer , the feature drama stars Nancy Isime in the lead role, alongside Uzor Arukwe , Martha Ehinome Orhiere , Dorathy Bachor , Chioma Nwosu , Obehi Aburime , and Grace Coker . Nancy Isime and Uzor Arukwe filming Loving Itohan. Nancy Isime on location with cast members filming scenes for Loving Itohan. For everyone looking forward to catching this one on the big screen, Loving Itohan arrives in cinemas nationwide on 6 November 2026. item.title: CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal ‘expected end November’
item.description: The Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) announced Monday that a verdict on Senegal’s appeal of the decision to strip them of the Africa Cup of Nations title in favour of Morocco is expected at the end of November. CAS said in a statement that a hearing of the case took place behind closed doors at its headquarters in Lausanne on October 8. “The panel have begun and continue their deliberations,” the organisation which resolves international sports disputes explained. “The CAS arbitrators have decided to issue a complete ruling which includes legal grounds, known as a CAS Award. This process will require several weeks, with the CAS Award expected at the end of November 2026.” At the January 18 final in Rabat, Senegal won 1-0 thanks to Pape Gueye’s extra-time goal, but the occasion was marred by chaotic scenes near the end of normal time when many Senegal players walked off the pitch in protest at the decision to award Morocco a penalty with the match still goalless. Some Senegalese supporters also attempted a pitch invasion, and the game was held up for almost 20 minutes before the Senegal players returned. In March, the Confederation of African Football (CAF) overturned that result, awarding Morocco a 3-0 victory, and the title. The post CAS verdict on Senegal AFCON title appeal ‘expected end November’ appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Flood kills two, submerges 18 communities in Nasarawa
item.description: By Edwin Philip, Lafia The Nasarawa State Government has urged residents of flood-prone communities to heed evacuation warnings and move to higher ground following flooding that submerged 18 communities in the Doma Local Government Area, killing two people and displacing several others. The Commissioner for Information, Culture and Tourism, Dr Nawani Aboki, made the appeal on Monday while briefing journalists in Lafia on the impact of the disaster in the affected communities. Aboki said Governor Abdullahi Sule had directed the Director-General of the Nasarawa State Emergency Management Agency to visit the affected communities to assess the damage and determine the necessary interventions. He said the government was working towards providing assistance to residents affected by the disaster. “We are hoping that anytime this week concrete actions will be taken by government. Yesterday, when I was returning, I was there with the chairman of the local government to sympathise with the people and condole with them,” the commissioner said. According to him, two people have died as a result of the flooding, while several others have been displaced. Buildings and farmlands were also reportedly destroyed. Describing the incident as massive flooding, Aboki said residents had been advised against returning to their homes until the floodwaters receded. “It is not just normal flooding, but massive flooding that took place. We are hoping that the flooding will end and the waters dry up so that people can resume their normal activities,” he said. “But we have asked them not to go back yet. Let them wait until we see the water actually receding back to the River Benue. We are not sure if more water will be coming in from the Lagdo Dam in Cameroon; it will even be worse than it is currently,” he added. The commissioner said the government was also prepared to provide support and relief supplies to affected residents to reduce the risk of disease outbreaks following the flooding. He explained that several smaller communities were clustered within larger settlements, complicating efforts to assess the full extent of the damage and the number of people affected. Aboki cited Agyma, where more than eight communities were reportedly affected, and Rukubi and Akpanaja, where several communities were also said to be experiencing the impact of the flooding. The government urged residents in vulnerable areas to prioritise their safety and remain in safer locations until the floodwaters had sufficiently receded. The post Flood kills two, submerges 18 communities in Nasarawa appeared first on Vanguard News .
