item.dc:creator: BellaNaija.com
item.content:encoded: Brutal Fruit’s The Pink Table brought Pan-African competition winners, their best friends and guests from across Africa together in Italy, making friendship the occasion for an international escape. Some experiences are made better by the person standing beside you. A beautiful view becomes the place you both promise to return to. A song becomes your song. Before you have found the words, she already understands. And when something feels almost too good to be real, one look at your best friend is enough: can you believe we are here? Much of the joy of female friendship lives in that shorthand. There is comfort in being known, in having someone who understands your sense of humour and shares the memories behind it. Taking that friendship somewhere new adds another chapter to a story already in progress. It can also make room for other people to enter it. Brutal Fruit’s The Pink Table Milan began with that feeling and an invitation to let the circle grow. From September 25th, competition winners and their best friends from across Africa and Brazil came together against the backdrop of Milan Fashion Week and Lake Como. The invitation had a simple starting point: bring your bestie. The consumer winners earned their places through retailer competitions, with each invited to bring her bestie. The details shaped the experience from the outset. A prize for one woman became an occasion for two, giving each pair someone familiar to share the excitement with as they stepped into a wider gathering. Born in South Africa, The Pink Table has travelled from home to Paris and now Milan with female friendships at its centre. The trip brought African women into an international setting alongside guests from elsewhere in the world, with time to find common ground through food, fashion and music. Female friendships have always been at the heart of The Pink Table and in Milan, bringing a bestie meant arriving with someone who knew you, while joining women from other countries and backgrounds offered the chance to get to know someone new. The South African spritzer brought them together through experiences designed to give connection room to materialize. A table is a good place to start and the welcome meal at Nonna’s captured that spirit. Generous Italian food, conversation and laughter brought warmth to a new setting. Sharing a table gave guests time to settle in and form camaraderie, creating an easy introduction to the women around them. The food belonged to Italy, but the pleasure of getting to know someone over a meal felt familiar. Fashion gave the conversation another kind of spark. At Barbara Rizzi’s show, where Brutal Fruit was the official drinks partner, winners, besties and creators experienced the work of a female-led Italian luxury label known for its craftsmanship and bold contemporary design. There were looks to admire and impressions to exchange, giving guests a shared experience to talk about beyond their own friendship pairs. Milan offered other points of discovery too. At Museo Bagatti Valsecchi, Renaissance art and antiques added another dimension to the city’s creativity. Alongside the fashion, these encounters gave women with different backgrounds something to discover together. Milan’s appeal was also its ability to create those openings: a new setting, a shared interest and a reason to start a conversation. Music made that common ground especially clear. A 19-member performance team led by pianist Julian Cohen brought songs including Coldplay’s “Viva la Vida”, “Bella Ciao” and Whitney Houston’s “I Wanna Dance With Somebody” into the experience. For guests who had not all arrived knowing one another, a familiar song offered something immediately recognizable to enjoy together. Brutal Fruit’s L’Orange Rossa , which was inspired by the Italian Riveria, added a flavour of the destination to the occasion. But the detail that held these different experiences together was the company; the best friend you came with, and the women you knew you had a reason to get to know. At Lake Como, the wider circle came together at The Pink Table itself. Around 75 guests from across the world including South African actress Siphesihle Ndaba , content creator and influencer Sni Mhlongo gathered at Villa Regina Teodolinda in Laglio, where sprawling gardens opened to private access to the water providing a romantic and intimate backdrop. Hosted by Italian actress Marina Valdemoro Maino, the occasion brought food, music and conversation into one setting. For all its beauty, the villa offered something simple; it gave women somewhere to gather and time to spend together. Besties could sit beside one another while becoming part of a larger table. The comfort of an existing friendship and the possibility of a new connection belonged in the same space. At The Pink Table Milan, female friendships were both the reason to gather and the starting point for new connections. Across countries and backgrounds, Brutal Fruit gave women the space to discover what they shared. Bringing a bestie was the beginning of the invitation. Making room for a wider circle was its promise. Because while the destination was Milan, the real currency of the trip was connection. item.title: Have any footballers ended their career with more own goals than goals? | The Knowledge
item.description: Plus: the earliest trophyless seasons, scoring off one’s backside (part II) and the origins of ‘shithousery’ Mail us with all of your questions and answers “How many professional players have ended their senior careers with more own goals than goals for their own team?” wonders Peter Clark. In the past we’ve looked at the players with the most own goals , but we haven’t looked at those who ended their professional career in debit. “Southampton cult hero Francis Benali scored only one ‘positive’ goal in his career and was legendary for banging in goal-of-the-month contenders at his own end, most notably a bullet header against Oldham in the 1993-94 season ,” writes Daz Pearce. We could only find a couple of OGs for Benali, the other being against Manchester United in 1999-2000 . But we were unable to find a comprehensive Southampton database, so there’s a chance we’ve missed some beauties. Continue reading...

item.title: Dettol Nigeria: Storytelling Wraps Up Challenge with 30 Winners
item.description: Dettol Nigeria has concluded its “12 Hour Protective Shield” storytelling challenge, recognizing 30 Nigerians for sharing personal stories about their experiences with Dettol Original Antibacterial Bar Soap. The Dettol Original 12hrs Protection Challenge ran from 13 July to 31 August 2026, and invited Nigerians to share personal Dettol stories ranging from childhood memories to family and personal hygiene routines. After the challenge closed, 30 winners were selected and rewarded with cash prizes for their entries. The challenge was part of the wider campaign for Dettol Original Soap, built around its 12-hour protective shield against 99.9% of illness-causing germs. Under the campaign idea, “ 12 Hours, Protection That Moves With You, ” Dettol highlighted the importance of consistent hygiene as people move through their daily activities. Beyond the digital campaign, Dettol brought the experience directly to consumers through in market activations across multiple states in Nigeria, combining product education and demonstrations with handwashing stations and consumer engagement. Commenting on the campaign, Boma Harrison , Marketing Director, Reckitt West Africa , said, “We were particularly pleased to give Nigerians the opportunity to share their personal Dettol stories and hear what protection means to them and their families. The stories shared through the challenge reflect the place Dettol has held in Nigerian households over the years, while reinforcing the importance of hygiene in everyday life. ” The campaign brought together digital storytelling, consumer engagement and on-ground experiences to reinforce Dettol Original’s role in everyday hygiene routines, while giving Nigerians an opportunity to share the personal experiences that have shaped their connection with the brand. item.title: Fashion Innovation Africa to Convene 300+ Stakeholders at Inaugural Conference in Lagos on October 22
item.description: Fashion Innovation Africa (FIA) 2026 will bring together more than 300 stakeholders from across fashion, finance, technology and government to examine the structures, investments and partnerships needed to build a stronger and globally competitive African fashion industry. Scheduled for Thursday, October 22, 2026, at Landmark Event Centre, Victoria Island, Lagos, the inaugural business conference is themed “From the Atelier to the Economy: The Architecture Behind African Fashion”. Endorsed by the Lagos State Government, FIA 2026 will focus on the systems and capabilities required to translate Africa’s creative talent into sustainable businesses, jobs and wider economic opportunities. The conference will convene successful fashion founders and business leaders alongside representatives from government, regulatory agencies, financial institutions, technology companies, logistics providers and other stakeholders across the fashion value chain. By bringing these groups together, FIA aims to strengthen connections between the creative, commercial and institutional players whose collaboration is essential to the industry’s growth. The full-day programme will feature a Government Keynote, fireside chats with leading founders, three panel discussions and concurrent masterclasses. Discussions will address critical industry issues, including access to growth capital, local manufacturing, supply chain resilience, quality standards, technology, trade frameworks and access to international markets. Uche Ajene , Convener of Fashion Innovation Africa, said the conference draws inspiration from the growth of Nigeria’s music and film industries, which have built stronger commercial structures and expanded their global reach over time. “There was a time when Nigerian music and Nollywood had immense talent but were still building the structures needed to support their growth and global reach. Today, both have made significant strides in taking Nigerian creativity to the world,” she said. “African fashion has similar potential, but realising it requires more than talent and visibility. We need stronger systems for financing, production, distribution, standards and market access. FIA is bringing the key players together to help build that architecture and position African fashion for sustainable growth and global competitiveness.” Beyond the conference programme, FIA 2026 will provide opportunities for businesses and industry stakeholders to showcase solutions, exchange ideas, build strategic partnerships and explore commercial opportunities across the fashion value chain. Fashion Innovation Africa is an initiative focused on strengthening Africa’s fashion ecosystem by connecting the people, businesses and institutions that shape its growth. item.title: Companies rushed in on AI. Now some are pulling back
item.description: Rapid AI adoption left workers cleaning up a flood of errors and low-quality work Employers around the globe are grappling with the fallout from rushing to adopt fast-changing artificial intelligence tools. Meta has scaled back plans to axe staff and use more AI agents after the company found employees were spending more and more time cleaning up technical and security errors, Reuters reported . And after thinning its workforce, especially middle managers , in a 2023 efficiency push, the company is expanding its managerial ranks again, LinkedIn posts from workers show. Continue reading...

item.title: Desperados and Young Jonn Create a Cross-Cultural Anthem For Living In The Moment With ‘Let It Go’
item.description: From the infectious rhythms of Latin music to the unmistakable pulse of Afrobeats, Desperados and Young Jonn are bringing two cultures together on “Let It Go, ” a new track inspired by living in the moment. Some moments are best enjoyed without overthinking them: a spontaneous night out, an unexpected link-up with friends, or the song that gets everyone moving. Capturing this spirit of freedom and self-expression, Desperados has teamed up with award-winning Afrobeats producer, songwriter and artist Young Jonn for “Let It Go.” Produced by Yung Willis , the Grammy-nominated music producer whose production credits span some of the biggest names in African music. Having worked with notable artistes including Falz, Wizkid, Kizz Daniel, Davido, Niniola, BNXN, Zlatan, Patoranking and Ice Prince , Yung Willis brings his production expertise to the collaboration, helping shape a sound that connects global influences with the energy of Afrobeats. Rooted in the brand’s identity and association with self-expression, Desperados continues to find meaningful ways to connect with the younger audience through music, culture and premium experiences. With “Let It Go”, the brand is using music as a touchpoint between its Latin roots and the energy of Nigerian culture. At the heart of the collaboration is “ Guao Guao ,” the reggaeton track Desperados created in partnership with Venezuelan artist Micro TDH and Colombian producer Ovy On The Drums. Built around a sample of this unique record, Let It Go brings a Latin-inspired sound into Young Jonn’s style, creating an Afrobeats song that reflects Nigeria’s vibrant music and nightlife culture. “Let It Go” is more than a fusion of two sounds. It is an expression of the Desperados vibe, where music becomes a way to encourage people to loosen up and enjoy moments that make life memorable. By connecting the global influence of Latin music with Afrobeats, the brand reinforces its place through music, culture, and self-expression. Young Jonn’ s ability to reinterpret global influences through a distinctive Nigerian style makes him a fitting partner for this expression. Rather than recreating the original, he gave the sound a fresh identity, shaped by the rhythm and movement of Nigerian music. Whether it’s the rhythm that takes over the dance floor, an ordinary link-up that turns into a memorable experience, the song captures the freedom of letting go and being fully in the moment. For Desperados, the brand’s involvement gives the song a cultural expression, connecting its identity to a sound that brings people together, encourages movement and creates room for memories. From recreating dance moves to sharing interpretations through lifestyle content, fans can join the “Let It Go” vibe beyond simply listening. item.title: Mark Your Calendars! Ecclesia Hills Church Announces 6th Ecclesia Word Conference, “Freedom in Christ”
item.description: Ecclesia Hills Church is pleased to announce the sixth edition of the Ecclesia Word Conference, themed “Freedom in Christ.” The conference will take place from Friday, 6th November to Sunday, 8th November 2026, at The Hall, 16 Musa Yar’adua Street, Victoria Island . The Ecclesia Word Conference has grown into a gathering where believers are taught, equipped, and stirred to live out the fullness of their faith. Last year’s edition explored the theme Custodian of Holy Oracles . This year’s edition turns to a question at the heart of the Gospel: What is freedom in Christ, and how can the Ecclesia arrive there? “This conference is crucial to bringing believers to the accuracy of freedom,” said Pastor Moses Ida-Michaels , Pastor of Ecclesia Hills Church. “Many people carry the name of Christ yet remain bound by religion, fear, habits, financial pressure, and generational patterns. This gathering is about seeing freedom clearly and walking in it. Together, we will hack the principles that bring true liberty to life,” he concluded. Conference Focus Across three days, sessions will address freedom in every area of life, including: Free a Generation: El-Shakar Freedom from Religion: Jabar Mckellar Freedom from Mammon: Chris Delvan Freedom in Illumination: Eva Dan Yusuf Freed Bloodlines, Cycles, Enchantments: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Freedom from Sinful Addictions / Fear of Consequence: Chris Delvan Free to Serve God’s Purpose: Chris Delvan Freedom in Innovation / Innovative Liberty: Moses Ida-Michaels (Host Pastor) Liberty Ideology: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Worship will be led by Hill Music and Moses Akoh , creating an atmosphere for encounter, response, and transformation. Last year’s edition explored the theme Custodian of Holy Oracles . This year’s edition turns to a question at the heart of the Gospel: What is freedom in Christ, and how can the Ecclesia arrive there? “This conference is crucial to bringing believers to the accuracy of freedom,” said Pastor Moses Ida-Michaels , Pastor of Ecclesia Hills Church. “Many people carry the name of Christ yet remain bound by religion, fear, habits, financial pressure, and generational patterns. This gathering is about seeing freedom clearly and walking in it. Together, we will hack the principles that bring true liberty to life,” he concluded. Conference Focus Across three days, sessions will address freedom in every area of life, including: Free a Generation: El-Shakar Freedom from Religion: Jabar Mckellar Freedom from Mammon: Chris Delvan Freedom in Illumination: Eva Dan Yusuf Freed Bloodlines, Cycles, Enchantments: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Freedom from Sinful Addictions / Fear of Consequence: Chris Delvan Free to Serve God’s Purpose: Chris Delvan Freedom in Innovation / Innovative Liberty: Moses Ida-Michaels (Host Pastor) Liberty Ideology: Edem Julius-Cudjoe Worship will be led by Hill Music and Moses Akoh , creating an atmosphere for encounter, response, and transformation. Event Details Event: Ecclesia Word Conference 2026 (6th Edition) Theme: Freedom in Christ Dates: Friday, 6th November to Sunday, 8th November 2026 Venue: The Hall, 16 Musa Yar’adua Street, Victoria Island, Lagos Schedule: Friday: 9:00 AM Saturday: 8:00 AM Sunday: 12:00 PM Admission: Free Registration (Required): Register Here Host: Ecclesia Hills Church Sponsored Content The post Mark Your Calendars! item.title: More Than Just a Glass of Milk: A Dietitian’s Perspective on Why Milk Matters
item.description: If you grew up in Nigeria in the 90s or early 2000s, chances are you didn’t learn about milk from a science class. You learnt about it from television. Back then, adverts were part of our childhood. We didn’t reach for a remote every time the commercials came on. We sang the jingles, quoted the catchphrases and years later, many of us can still remember them word for word. For me, one advert stands above the rest. It followed a young Kanu Nwankwo as he dribbled a football through the dusty streets of Owerri on an errand for his mother. He left home with nothing but a football at his feet, dribbling all the way to the market. Just as a tin of milk slipped from the market woman’s hands, he flicked it back into the air with effortless skill. She smiled and said, “Papilo, I know say one day you go make us proud.” As children, we believed her. Not because we understood marketing, but because those adverts made us believe that greatness could begin anywhere. They told us that a boy from Owerri, Nigeria could become one of Africa’s greatest footballers. They told us that ordinary children with big dreams could grow into extraordinary adults. And somewhere between that advert and my mum pouring Milk into my breakfast cereal every morning before school, I came to believe two things. The first was that milk helped build strong bones and teeth. The second was that maybe, just maybe, I could become whoever I dreamed of becoming. item.content:encoded: If you grew up in Nigeria in the 90s or early 2000s, chances are you didn’t learn about milk from a science class. You learnt about it from television. Back then, adverts were part of our childhood. We didn’t reach for a remote every time the commercials came on. We sang the jingles, quoted the catchphrases and years later, many of us can still remember them word for word. For me, one advert stands above the rest. It followed a young Kanu Nwankwo as he dribbled a football through the dusty streets of Owerri on an errand for his mother. He left home with nothing but a football at his feet, dribbling all the way to the market. Just as a tin of milk slipped from the market woman’s hands, he flicked it back into the air with effortless skill. She smiled and said, “Papilo, I know say one day you go make us proud.” As children, we believed her. Not because we understood marketing, but because those adverts made us believe that greatness could begin anywhere. They told us that a boy from Owerri, Nigeria could become one of Africa’s greatest footballers. They told us that ordinary children with big dreams could grow into extraordinary adults. And somewhere between that advert and my mum pouring Milk into my breakfast cereal every morning before school, I came to believe two things. The first was that milk helped build strong bones and teeth. The second was that maybe, just maybe, I could become whoever I dreamed of becoming. Years later, after becoming a dietitian, I realised that my childhood understanding wasn’t wrong, it was simply incomplete. Today, conversations about milk have become surprisingly complicated. Social media is filled with conflicting opinions. Some people insist milk is only for children. Others believe it causes weight gain. Some assume all milk is the same, while others believe dairy milk and non- dairy offer identical nutrition. As nutrition professionals, we know that the truth is rarely found in headlines or viral videos. It is found in evidence. So, let’s separate what we know about milk from what we only think we know. What Exactly Is Milk? From a scientific perspective, milk is the natural nutrient-rich fluid produced by mammals to nourish their young during the earliest stages of life. For humans, cow’s milk is the most widely consumed form of dairy milk and has been part of diets around the world for generations. But from a nutrition perspective, milk is much more than its definition. It is a naturally nutrient-dense food that provides a unique combination of high-quality protein, calcium, phosphorus, vitamin B12, riboflavin and other essential nutrients that work together to support growth, bone health, muscle function, energy production and overall wellbeing throughout life. Unlike many foods that contribute just one or two key nutrients, milk delivers several essential nutrients in one convenient food. This is one of the reasons it has remained a staple in many cultures and continues to play an important role in healthy eating patterns across different stages of life. Yet despite these nutritional benefits, milk remains one of the most misunderstood foods on our tables. Over the years, I’ve heard people say that milk is only for children, that it causes weight gain or that all milk products are the same. Social media has only amplified these conversations, making it increasingly difficult to separate evidence from opinion. So, let’s look at some of the most common myths about milk and what science tells us. Why Milk Matters One of the things I have learned after years of working as a dietitian is that conversations about milk often focus on just one nutrient: calcium. Yes, milk is well known for supporting strong bones and healthy teeth, but that’s only one part of the story. Milk provides a unique combination of nutrients that work together to support the body in different ways. Rather than contributing just one benefit, it supplies several essential nutrients in a single food, each playing its own role in maintaining good health. High-quality protein helps build and repair muscles, organs and other body tissues. It’s essential for growth in children and helps adults maintain muscle mass throughout life. Calcium and phosphorus work together to support strong bones and healthy teeth. These nutrients are especially important during childhood and adolescence, when bones are developing rapidly, but they also remain important throughout adulthood to help maintain bone health. Vitamin B12 plays an essential role in the production of healthy red blood cells and supports the normal functioning of the nervous system. Riboflavin (vitamin B2) helps the body convert the food we eat into the energy we need for everyday activities. Many Milk products are also fortified with vitamins A and D. Vitamin A supports healthy vision and the normal functioning of the immune system, while vitamin D helps the body absorb calcium effectively, making it an important partner in maintaining strong bones. What makes milk unique isn’t that it contains one remarkable nutrient. It’s that it brings many important nutrients together in one food. That combination is one of the reasons milk has remained part of healthy dietary patterns across different cultures and generations. A glass of Milk doesn’t provide just one nutrient. It provides a package of nutrients working together to support growth, development and overall wellbeing. Myth 1: “Milk Is Only for Children” One of the most common misconceptions I hear is that milk is something we eventually outgrow, that once we become adults, it no longer has a place in our diet. I understand where that idea comes from. Many of us first encountered milk as children. It was stirred into our morning pap, added to cereal before school or mixed into a warm cup of tea on rainy days. Over time, it’s easy to begin thinking of milk as a “children’s food.” But our bodies tell a different story. While our nutritional needs change throughout life, they never stop. In fact, the nutrients milk provides continue to support us in different ways as we grow older. For children, milk contributes high-quality protein, calcium and other essential nutrients that support healthy growth and the development of strong bones and teeth. During the teenage years, when growth accelerates and nutritional demands increase, these nutrients remain just as important. As adults, the focus shifts. Growth may slow, but maintaining muscle mass, preserving bone health and meeting our daily nutrient needs become priorities. The high-quality protein, calcium and other vitamins and minerals found in milk continue to contribute to those goals as part of a balanced diet. For older adults, maintaining muscle strength and bone health becomes increasingly important. Adequate protein helps preserve muscle as we age, while calcium and vitamin D, where milk is fortified with vitamin D, continue to support healthy bones. In other words, milk doesn’t stop being relevant because we grow older, its role simply changes. The nutrients remain valuable. What changes is how our bodies use them at different stages of life. Perhaps that’s a better way to think about it. Milk grows with us, not because every person must drink milk every day, but because the nutrients it provides continue to support health from childhood through older adulthood as part of a healthy, balanced diet. Myth 2: “Milk Causes Weight Gain” If you’ve spent any time on social media, you’ve probably come across someone confidently declaring that milk is “too fattening” or should be avoided if you’re trying to manage your weight. It’s a message that’s repeated so often that many people now accept it as fact. The reality, however, is much less dramatic. No single food causes weight gain on its own. Weight gain occurs when, over time, we consistently consume more energy than our bodies use. Overall dietary patterns, portion sizes, physical activity, sleep and othe

item.title: adidas x waf. Superstar ADV Brings Lagos Skate Culture to the Global Stage
item.description: On Monday, 12 October 2026, adidas and waf. (Wflsncrm ) release the Superstar ADV worldwide, marking the first time an African skate community has shaped the silhouette since its 1970 debut. Co-established in 2012 by Jomi Marcus-Bello, Nifemi Marcus-Bello, and KC Obijiaku, waf. has spent 14 years nurturing the Lagos skateboarding scene from the ground up, culminating in the opening of a skatepark at Freedom Park, located on the site of a former colonial prison, in 2024. This rich heritage is directly integrated into the sneaker’s aesthetic, featuring a dusty grey upper inspired by Lagos Island, breathable side panels crafted for the climate of Lagos, and a translucent pink outsole designed to evoke the city’s horizon at distinct moments of the day. The release begins at the waf. flagship in Lagos and across all adidas retail and e-commerce platforms worldwide at $110. Launch time at the Lagos flagship: 9:00 a.m. WAT. ABOUT WAF. waf. (Wafflesncream) is Nigeria’s pioneering skate community and the first hub for skate culture in West Africa, combining a retail space with a creative community. For fourteen years, it has grown Lagos’ skate scene through community programming, retail, fashion, and music. In 2017, waf. launched Nigeria’s first Go Skate Day, now one of the country’s largest annual skate festivals. ABOUT ADIDAS ORIGINALS Inspired by the rich sporting heritage of adidas, one of the world’s leading sports brands and a global designer and developer of athletic footwear and apparel, adidas Originals is a lifestyle brand founded in 2001. With the adidas archive at its foundation, adidas Originals continues to evolve the brand’s legacy through its commitment to product innovation and its ability to filter the creativity and courage found on the courts and sporting arenas through the lens of contemporary youth culture. BellaNaija is a Media Partner for adidas x waf. Superstar ADV The post adidas x waf. Superstar ADV Brings Lagos Skate Culture to the Global Stage appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: The biggest threat from AI is the sense that we have no say in it. To that I say game on | Peter Lewis
item.description: The tech bros and their highly paid sock puppets are banking on us giving in to their ‘inevitability doctrine’. But in Australia, and around the world, resistance is rising Of all the drivers of the populist wave, one of the most powerful is the sense of inevitability that surrounds what we are told is the march of progress. In presenting the future as a fait accompli, it poisons the civic well by dealing us out of the game. While the US clings on to its status as the oldest constitutional democracy, the unholy alliance between the tech overlords and the White House is creating its own AI reality untethered to the will of the people . Continue reading...

item.title: Emir of Kano to Lead Sustainability Leaders at STS’ 10-Year Milestone in Lagos
item.description: With four years remaining to the 2030 Sustainable Development Goals deadline, the Sustainability Table Discourse Series (STS) will mark its tenth anniversary on 15–16 October 2026 at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Federal Palace Hotel, Victoria Island, Lagos, with a deliberate shift from dialogue to delivery. Under the theme ‘Leading the Sustainable Development Agenda: People, Planet and Prosperity,’ STS @10 will bring together leaders from government, business, finance, development institutions, technology and civil society to address a defining question: how can Africa bridge the gap between sustainable development ambition and execution? Headlining the gathering is H.H. Muhammadu Sanusi II , Emir of Kano , who will deliver the Flagship Keynote, “People, Planet & Prosperity: The Decade of Delivery.” The gathering will also feature H.E. Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, Deputy Governor of Lagos State; Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State and Chairman, Forum of State Commissioners of Finance; H.E. Amb. Prof. (Mrs.) Olufolake AbdulRazaq, First Lady of Kwara State; Tenioye Majekodunmi, Director-General, National Council on Climate Change; Dr. Innocent Barikor, Director-General/CEO, NESREA; Rukaiya El-Rufai, Presidency / National Economic Council & Climate Change; Adam Boros, Vice President, Africa Finance Corporation; Ademola Ogunbanjo, President & CEO, Oando Clean Energy; Rolake Akinkugbe-Filani, CEO, EnergyInc Advisors Limited; and Dapo Otunla, Chief Corporate Services Officer, IHS Nigeria, among other leaders. The current programme also features a high-level dialogue on mobilizing capital and leadership for Africa’s sustainability transition. First convened in 2016, STS has spent a decade bringing together stakeholders around the green economy, climate finance, technology, circularity, food security, ESG and the Sustainable Development Goals. STS @10 marks an inflection point: a greater focus on bridging Africa’s sustainability implementation gap—the distance between commitments and action, innovation and scale, and viable projects and the investment required to deliver them. “Africa does not suffer from a shortage of ambition, declarations or conferences. The real deficit is execution—turning policy into implementation, innovation into scale and credible projects into investible opportunities,” said Kayode Olaniyan , Convener of the Sustainability Table Discourse Series. “Ten years of STS have shown us the power of bringing the right people to the table. But the next decade must be about what happens after they leave it. We are not convening another talk shop. The next decade must be aboutdelivery,” He added. The programme will focus on four critical conversations: Nigeria’s energy future and expanding energy access; Technology, AI and the SDGs; the circular economy and responsible production; and resilient food systems, smarter value chains and cold-chain infrastructure. Beyond the conversations, STS @10 will move from ideas to in

Dr. Kadri Obafemi Hamzat, Deputy Governor of Lagos State; Akintunde Oyebode, Commissioner for Finance, Ekiti State and Chairman, Forum of State Commissioners of Finance; H.E. Amb. Prof. (Mrs.) Olufolake AbdulRazaq, First Lady of Kwara State; Tenioye Majekodunmi, Director-General, National Council on Climate Change; Dr. Innocent Barikor, Director-General/CEO, NESREA; Rukaiya El-Rufai, Presidency / National Economic Council & Climate Change; Adam Boros, Vice President, Africa Finance Corporation; Ademola Ogunbanjo, President & CEO, Oando Clean Energy; Rolake Akinkugbe-Filani, CEO, EnergyInc Advisors Limited; and Dapo Otunla, Chief Corporate Services Officer, IHS Nigeria, among other leaders. The current programme also features a high-level dialogue on mobilizing capital and leadership for Africa’s sustainability transition. First convened in 2016, STS has spent a decade bringing together stakeholders around the green economy, climate finance, technology, circularity, food security, ESG and the Sustainable Development Goals. STS @10 marks an inflection point: a greater focus on bridging Africa’s sustainability implementation gap—the distance between commitments and action, innovation and scale, and viable projects and the investment required to deliver them. “Africa does not suffer from a shortage of ambition, declarations or conferences. The real deficit is execution—turning policy into implementation, innovation into scale and credible projects into investible opportunities,” said Kayode Olaniyan , Convener of the Sustainability Table Discourse Series. “Ten years of STS have shown us the power of bringing the right people to the table. But the next decade must be about what happens after they leave it. We are not convening another talk shop. The next decade must be aboutdelivery,” He added. The programme will focus on four critical conversations: Nigeria’s energy future and expanding energy access; Technology, AI and the SDGs; the circular economy and responsible production; and resilient food systems, smarter value chains and cold-chain infrastructure. Beyond the conversations, STS @10 will move from ideas to investment and innovation. Day Two will feature masterclasses, strategic investment engagements, the STS @10 Investment & Deals Room — Connecting Capital with Projects and Enterprise, and an Innovation Pitch Finale & Investor Showcase, creating opportunities to connect promising businesses and projects with financial institutions, investors and development partners. The anniversary will also feature ‘The Earth Speaks’ Sustainability & Arts Exhibition, the launch of the commemorative coffee-table book A Decade at the Table: From Conversation to Transformation, and the premiere of the documentary Nigeria 2030: The Sustainability Imperative — A Decade of Dialogue. A New Era of Action. The gala programme confirms both the book launch and documentary premiere as part of the anniversary celebrations. Ten years ago, STS created a table for the conversation. At STS @10, the question is no longer simply who is at the table—but what gets done because they were there. item.title: From Asake’s Oba to Omah Lay’s Canada Breeze: 5 Music Videos to Watch
item.description: On set for his Oba music video, Asake highlights his signature high-steeze look with a textured jacket and luxury travel accessories. Music is a daily business in Nigeria, both for the artists making it and the listeners who keep up with new releases. Almost every week, new songs drop alongside music videos that bring them to life visually. This week, we’re putting you on five new music videos to check out, featuring Asake , Omah Lay , FOLA , and Young Jonn . Here are five new Nigerian music videos that are worth adding to your watch list this week: Asake – Oba Asake takes fans into the creative process behind “Oba,” trading elaborate street scenes for a more intimate look at a late-night recording session. Directed by Director Buise, the video features the singer alongside producers and backing vocalists, while his signature style and confident presence reinforce the royal theme of the song. The track appears on his M$NEY album. Omah Lay – Canada Breeze Omah Lay’s “Canada Breeze” captures the singer’s reflective side, touching on personal growth, spirituality and finding peace after periods of worry. The song, from his Clarity of Mind album, pairs his signature melodic delivery with lyrics about moving beyond past struggles. Its music video gives fans another way to experience the record’s introspective mood. FOLA – miss you ii FOLA returns to matters of the heart with “miss you ii (nriri),” a release that speaks to longing and missing someone. The track features the Nigerian singer’s melodic Afropop style and arrives as part of a busy period for the rising artist, whose 9 album was released in October 2026. Fans can check out the song’s lyric video and follow its story through the lyrics. Omah Lay – Artificial Happiness Omah Lay takes a cinematic approach to “Artificial Happiness,” the opening track of his Clarity of Mind album. In the video, the singer awakens in an abandoned warehouse with a white tree at its centre, surrounded by mysterious figures whose movements give the scene an unsettling quality. Co-directed creatively by Omah Lay and his longtime collaborator NWSPK, the visual explores the song’s introspective world and the search for genuine happiness. Young Jonn – Glass in the Air Young Jonn brings dancefloor energy to “Glass in the Air.” The song reflects the excitement of navigating new territory and celebrating personal milestones, with the producer-turned-singer leaning into an upbeat, dance-ready sound. It is another opportunity to experience the infectious energy and melodic style that have become central to his evolution as an artist. The post From Asake’s Oba to Omah Lay’s Canada Breeze: 5 Music Videos to Watch appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: I’m a pediatrician. Loss of human connection is the biggest threat to kids, not AI | Megan Moreno
item.description: Amid worries about children’s relationship to tech, the solution is often spending more time talking openly with each other We have become obsessed with the idea that screens are destroying human connection. The evidence seems to be everywhere. Each week headlines warn of teenagers addicted to phones , a loneliness epidemic and the dangers of AI . The release of The Social Reckoning leads us to ask, “How bad were those guys at Meta?” and then ultimately wonder, “ How bad am I if I still use Instagram?” In our day-to-day, we observe workers eating lunch alone while scrolling and friends choosing online games over offline gatherings. Continue reading...

item.title: 5 Films Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson Have Featured in Together
item.description: Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson in western bridal styling for “My 30th Wedding”. If it were rumoured that Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson are getting married, you’d hardly dismiss the rumour because of the times the duo have shared the stage in films, and their synergy and connection each time they appear together in a film. With their latest YouTube release , “My 30th Wedding” going viral, with over 22 million views in 11 days, it is informative to look at some of the films they have both featured in together. In each film, you will find that connection. While they have mainly featured together in romance movies, the genre has not limited the creativity and energy they bring into each film. Let’s look at some of the films Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson have both featured in. Breaded Life In this 2021 movie, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson navigate life in the ghetto after Timini’s character, Sunmi, is forced out of his wealthy existence. The film showcases the duo’s varying personas, highlighting themes of vulnerability, strength, and love. They demonstrate how two actors can continuously interact on screen while still delivering distinctly different vibes. Reel Love Produced by Timini Egbuson and directed by Kayode Kasum, Reel Love explores the relationship between love, celebrity and social media. Timini plays Tomide Jobi, a relationship influencer whose public image suffers after a heated confrontation with Rachel, played by T.J. Omusuku, goes viral. To repair the damage, Tomide agrees to stage a fake relationship with Rachel, but the arrangement becomes complicated when genuine feelings begin to develop. Bimbo Ademoye appears as Chizaram in the film, which also features Funke Akindele, Shaffy Bello and Dakore Egbuson-Akande. Released in Nigerian cinemas on Valentine’s Day in 2025, the film examines the pressure to maintain a public image and the difference between performing love for an audience and experiencing it in real life. Big Love In Big Love, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson play Adina and Adil, two young people who meet while pursuing their ambitions and eventually fall in love. Adil is determined to achieve his dreams, while Adina is an independent woman focused on making a living. As their relationship develops, they must confront personal fears and a secret that threatens to come between them. Directed by Biodun Stephen, the romantic drama explores love, trust and the difficult choices that can test a relationship. The film also gives viewers another opportunity to see the chemistry between the two actors as romantic leads. Unexpected Places Bimbo Ademoye plays Prosper, the daughter of a housekeeper who steps in to manage the household while her mother recovers from surgery. Her new responsibilities bring her into contact with Chris, played by Timini Egbuson, a wealthy playboy whose irresponsible behaviour has become a concern for his father. Bimbo Ademoye appears as Chizaram in the film, which also features Funke Akindele, Shaffy Bello and Dakore Egbuson-Akande. Released in Nigerian cinemas on Valentine’s Day in 2025, the film examines the pressure to maintain a public image and the difference between performing love for an audience and experiencing it in real life. Big Love In Big Love, Bimbo Ademoye and Timini Egbuson play Adina and Adil, two young people who meet while pursuing their ambitions and eventually fall in love. As their relationship develops, they must confront personal fears and a secret that threatens to come between them. Directed by Biodun Stephen, the romantic drama explores love, trust and the difficult choices that can test a relationship. The film also gives viewers another opportunity to see the chemistry between the two actors as romantic leads. Unexpected Places Bimbo Ademoye plays Prosper, the daughter of a housekeeper who steps in to manage the household while her mother recovers from surgery. Her new responsibilities bring her into contact with Chris, played by Timini Egbuson, a wealthy playboy whose irresponsible behaviour has become a concern for his father. Their relationship begins on difficult terms, but Prosper’s presence gradually challenges Chris to reconsider his choices and take responsibility for his life. Produced by Ademoye and directed by Great Val Edochie, the romantic drama explores personal growth, love and the unexpected circumstances that can change people’s lives. The film also takes a more emotional turn as the couple’s relationship develops. Introducing the Kujus Directed by Biodun Stephen, Introducing the Kujus is a family comedy-drama set in Badagry, Lagos. The film follows five siblings who are reluctant to return to their hometown for the fifth anniversary of their mother’s death. Mausi Kuju, played by Bisola Aiyeola, and her brother Maugbe, played by Timini Egbuson, devise a plan to bring the family together, but their complicated relationships threaten to get in the way. Bimbo Ademoye plays Ebi, one of the siblings whose relationships and family history contribute to the story. The film explores family bonds, old disagreements and the things that can bring people back together. item.title: Christian Pulisic is no longer a focal point for the US or Milan – and that’s OK
item.description: The winger is 28, and younger teammates are rising into the high-pressure spots he has usually occupied Usually, the second weekend of October sees Christian Pulisic flanked by compatriots as the Star-Spangled Banner plays. Last year, he was involved in US friendlies against Ecuador and Australia. But this year, with Fifa having folded the October window into September, Pulisic didn’t have the chance. On Sunday, his pre-match music was O Generosa, the Serie A anthem, which he observed with a soft smile. Mark Twain’s first visit to Italy left him describing the country as “a vast museum of magnificence and misery”, and it’s a fitting summary of Pulisic’s three-plus years with Milan. The magnificence: 43 goals and 25 assists in 138 appearances. The misery: just one trophy since he arrived in July 2023, a 2025 Supercoppa Italia held in Saudi Arabia. Continue reading...

item.title: Midea Launches WIN 9JA WIN Promotion with Guaranteed Rewards and Chery Tiggo 2 Pro Grand Prize
item.description: Midea has announced the launch of WIN 9JA WIN , a nationwide consumer promotion designed to reward Nigerians who choose Midea home appliances during the 2026 festive shopping season. Running from 10 October to 31 December 2026 , the promotion gives every qualifying shopper an instant opportunity to win, with a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro positioned as the ultimate grand prize. Under the promotion, consumers who purchase any Midea product worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer receive a scratch voucher at the point of purchase. The shopper scratches the voucher to reveal the reward won, creating a simple and immediate link between purchase and reward. Every qualifying shopper is a winner, subject to the approved campaign terms and conditions. The campaign combines retail participation with radio, digital, public relations, in-store visibility and an extensive on-ground Promo Tour Truck programme. The touring activation will carry the excitement of WIN 9JA WIN into selected markets and dealer locations, with the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro prominently showcased to give consumers a close view of the campaign’s headline prize. A Consumer Promotion Built Around Instant Reward WIN 9JA WIN is designed to make the festive purchase journey more rewarding while strengthening engagement between Midea , its dealer network and consumers across Nigeria. Its central proposition is straightforward: make a qualifying purchase, receive a scratch voucher and discover the reward immediately. The approved reward pool spans Midea home appliances and branded consumer gifts. These include side-by-side refrigerators, chest freezers, air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, air fryers, microwave ovens, kettles, standing fans and blenders, as well as branded T-shirts, caps and pens. The ultimate reward is a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro, presented in the campaign materials as the car to be won. MIDEA NIGERIA | MEDIA RELEASE How Consumers Can Participate Step Consumer action Purchase Buy any Midea product or combination of eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer between 10 October and 31 December 2026. Receive Collect the campaign scratch voucher issued for the qualifying purchase. Scratch Scratch the voucher to reveal the reward. Claim Follow the verification and prize-claim guidance provided by the participating dealer in accordance with the approved campaign terms and conditions. Additional Midea Air Conditioner Offer Alongside WIN 9JA WIN, Midea is also offering free installation and a free copper kit to consumers who purchase any Midea air conditioner from 1 October through 31 December 2026. The offer extends the campaign’s value beyond the product purchase by helping eligible AC buyers with installation support, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Promo Tour Truck Takes WIN 9JA WIN Closer to Consumers A major feature of the campaign is the branded Promo Tour Truck programme, developed as a mobile visibility and engagement platform.

A Consumer Promotion Built Around Instant Reward WIN 9JA WIN is designed to make the festive purchase journey more rewarding while strengthening engagement between Midea , its dealer network and consumers across Nigeria. Its central proposition is straightforward: make a qualifying purchase, receive a scratch voucher and discover the reward immediately. The approved reward pool spans Midea home appliances and branded consumer gifts. These include side-by-side refrigerators, chest freezers, air conditioners, refrigerators, washing machines, air fryers, microwave ovens, kettles, standing fans and blenders, as well as branded T-shirts, caps and pens. The ultimate reward is a Chery Tiggo 2 Pro, presented in the campaign materials as the car to be won. MIDEA NIGERIA | MEDIA RELEASE How Consumers Can Participate Step Consumer action Purchase Buy any Midea product or combination of eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more from a participating dealer between 10 October and 31 December 2026. Receive Collect the campaign scratch voucher issued for the qualifying purchase. Scratch Scratch the voucher to reveal the reward. Claim Follow the verification and prize-claim guidance provided by the participating dealer in accordance with the approved campaign terms and conditions. Additional Midea Air Conditioner Offer Alongside WIN 9JA WIN, Midea is also offering free installation and a free copper kit to consumers who purchase any Midea air conditioner from 1 October through 31 December 2026. The offer extends the campaign’s value beyond the product purchase by helping eligible AC buyers with installation support, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. Promo Tour Truck Takes WIN 9JA WIN Closer to Consumers A major feature of the campaign is the branded Promo Tour Truck programme, developed as a mobile visibility and engagement platform. The vehicle format is designed to operate as a moving billboard and activation hub, carrying Midea branding, product communication and WIN 9JA WIN messaging through high-traffic retail corridors and participating dealer locations. The Chery Tiggo 2 Pro will be prominently showcased as part of the tour, allowing shoppers and local communities to see the campaign’s ultimate prize at close range. At scheduled dealer stops, consumers will be able to discover Midea products, receive clear information about the promotion and understand the qualifying purchase and scratch-voucher process. The programme is intended to support participating dealers, stimulate retail interest and bring the promotion into the communities where consumers shop. Selected Tour Markets and Dealer Locations The supplied tour schedule covers selected locations across Lagos, the South-West, South-South, South- East, North-Central and Northern Nigeria. The dealer activation routes are scheduled from 10 October to 1 November 2026, subject to final operational confirmation. The market clusters are listed below; the detailed dealer-location appendix forms part of this release pack. East Route : Port Harcourt, Aba, Umuahia, Uyo and Oron, Owerri, Nnewi, Onitsha, Awka, Asaba and Enugu. Lagos and adjoining markets : Lekki, Victoria Island, Ikoyi, Ajah, Lagos Island, Idumota, Apapa, Festac, Alaba, Ojo, Ikotun, Igando, Idimu, Ipaja, Abule Egba, Agege, Ikeja, Allen, Maryland, Ogba, Yaba, Surulere, Ebute Metta, Ikorodu, Badagry, Ota, Agbara and Isheri. South-West and South-South route: Ibadan, Iseyin, Ogbomoso, Ilorin, Osogbo, Ilesa, Ile-Ife, Abeokuta, Sagamu, Ijebu-Ode, Ago-Iwoye, Mowe, Warri, Effurun, Ughelli, Sapele, Benin City, Irrua, Uromi, Akure and Ondo. North and North-Central Route: Abuja, Mararaba, Lokoja, Makurdi, Lafia, Kaduna, Kano, Yola and Jimeta. Supporting Retail Engagement and Household Choice The campaign reflects Midea’s focus on making home-appliance technology more accessible and relevant to Nigerian households. By combining guaranteed rewards with a wide dealer footprint and direct market engagement, WIN 9JA WIN gives consumers another reason to explore Midea’s range of air conditioners, refrigerators, freezers, washing machines, cooking appliances and small domestic appliances during the year-end season. Executive Comment / Quotation “WIN 9JA WIN is our way of thanking Nigerian consumers and making every qualifying purchase more rewarding. The mechanic is simple, transparent and immediate: buy, receive a scratch voucher and reveal your reward. Through the Promo Tour Truck programme, we are also taking the campaign closer to our dealer partners and consumers in markets across the country, while giving shoppers the opportunity to experience Midea products and see the Chery Tiggo 2 Pro grand prize up close.” – Ashok Dimri, Business Head, Africa, of Care Global Consumer Ltd. Call to Action Consumers can visit participating Midea dealers nationwide between 10 October and 31 December 2026, purchase eligible Midea products worth ₦100,000 or more and collect a scratch voucher to reveal their reward. Consumers purchasing any Midea air conditioner can also access the free installation and free copper kit offer through 31 December 2026, subject to the applicable terms and conditions. About Midea Group Midea is one of over 10 brands operating under the Smart Home Business of Midea Group. Midea Group , with the vision of “bringing great innovations to life”, is an international tech-leading company which specializes in seven major business areas: Smart Home, Industrial Technologies, Building Technologies, KUKA, New Energy, Midea Healthcare and ANNTO Logistics. Midea’s products and services have served more than 500 million customers worldwide, including key clients and strategic partners across various industries. Midea operates more than 400 subsidiaries, 41 R&D centres and 65 major manufacturing bases globally, with a business network covering over 200 countries and regions. item.title: Apple AirPods 5 review: the best open-fit earbuds yet
item.description: Upgraded, cheaper AirPods have noise cancelling, sound and controls to rival many plugged-in buds but without tips Apple’s latest AirPods set a new standard for open-fit buds with upgraded noise cancelling that now rivals many plugged-in designs of the same price. The AirPods 5 have the same design the popular AirPods 4 offering an option for those that do not like silicone ear tips used by most noise cancelling earbuds. They come in two versions, with or without a wireless charging case and swipe controls, costing from £119 (€149/$129/A$219) – £10 cheaper than the launch price of their predecessors . Connectivity: Bluetooth 5.3, SBC, AAC, H2 chip Battery life: four or five hours with ANC (22 hours with case) Water resistance: IP57 (up to 1 metre for 30 minutes ) Earbud dimensions: 30.2 x 18.3 x 18.1mm Earbud weight: 4.3g each Charging case dimensions: 46.2 x 50.1 x 21.2mm Charging case weight: 32.3g/34.7g Case charging: USB-C or wireless (Qi or Watch) Continue reading...

item.title: Winning is not enough for Manchester City to move on from this crisis | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: It’s not just that the club’s recent charges themselves are unprecedented – it’s the language used to describe them too Sign up for our free newsletter here The language of football is a fine and highly nuanced dialect. The majority of people involved in the game speak it with a high degree of sophistication. Minor deviations from the familiar, almost imperceptible to outsiders, can set off alarm bells: what’s really going on there? Why isn’t he happy? What’s she hinting at? But it’s an argot developed to talk about football, and when applied to other subjects, it can sound extremely jarring. Erling Haaland is one of the brighter, more engaging players. There’s an appealing quirkiness to him that suggests he has a higher-than-usual level of self-awareness. He doesn’t mind stepping outside the norms, being a bit different. But consider his assessment of Manchester City’s 3-0 win at Liverpool on Sunday. Continue reading...

item.title: Welcome home, Sophie Adenot
item.description: Video: 00:02:54 After 237 days and over 3,700 orbits around Earth aboard the International Space Station, Sophie Adenot is back on Earth! Following a handover to Crew-13, Sophie and her Crew-12 crewmates undocked on 7 October and splashed down off the coast of California the next day. Now back in Europe, Sophie will begin her post-flight data collection and rehabilitation while readjusting to life on Earth after the longest mission in space by a European astronaut so far. Welcome home, Sophie!

item.title: TCL West Africa Regional Launch in Côte d’Ivoire: Showcases 2026 SQD Mini LED TVs and Smart Home Innovations
item.description: TCL , a global leader in consumer electronics and No.1 Mini LED and Ultra Large Screen TV Brand (75”+)¹, has showcased its latest consumer electronics and home appliance portfolio for Nigeria during its West Africa regional launch event in Côte d’Ivoire. Bringing together media, business partners, retailers, distributors, industry stakeholders and content creators from across the region, the event provided a closer look at TCL’s 2026 display innovations alongside new solutions across air conditioning, refrigeration, laundry and monitors. The launch reflects TCL’s continued investment in Nigeria and its focus on introducing technologies that respond to the way consumers across both markets live today. From larger screens for sport and family entertainment to energy conscious cooling, high capacity appliances and connected home experiences, the new portfolio has been developed to combine performance, convenience and accessibility. Daniel Ray , Director of Sales, TCL West Africa, said: “ Nigeria are important markets within TCL’s West Africa growth strategy, with consumers increasingly looking for technology that delivers strong performance while remaining relevant to their everyday needs. Through this regional launch, we are bringing together entertainment, cooling and home appliance innovations designed around how people live, connect and enjoy content across both markets. Our ambition is to continue making advanced technology more accessible while giving consumers greater choice across the home. “ A New Era of Premium Big Screen Entertainment Large screen entertainment continues to grow across Nigeria, with consumers increasingly seeking more immersive experiences across sport, movies, streaming and gaming. Leading TCL’s latest television portfolio is the C7L SQD Mini LED range, available from 65 to 98 inches, bringing enhanced colour precision, brightness control, deeper blacks and improved halo control. Complementing the C7L is the 98 inch C6K QD Mini LED TV, delivering an ultra large screen experience with advanced Mini LED performance for movies, live sport and gaming. It features TCL All Domain Halo Control Technology, up to 512 Precise Dimming Zones, a 144Hz native refresh rate, an AiPQ Pro Processor, a Matte HVA Panel and an ONKYO 2.1 Hi Fi audio system. Smarter Cooling Designed for Local Climate Needs With warm temperatures forming part of everyday life across Nigeria, cooling performance, energy management and convenience remain important considerations for households. TCL highlighted two air conditioning solutions designed to address these priorities, the FreshIN 3.0 and SaveIN AI Series 24K. TCL FreshIN 3.0 FreshIN 3.0 expands the air conditioning experience beyond temperature control by introducing fresh outdoor air into the room while supporting improved indoor air quality. Key technologies include FreshIN Technology, T AI Energy Saving, Smart Voice Control, QuadruPuri filtration, Visible Air Quality and Gentle Breeze. The system is also engineered for stable operation in high ambient temperatures, making it especially relevant for consumers across Nigeria seeking reliable cooling performance during hotter periods of the year. TCL SaveIN AI Series The TCL SaveIN AI Series is designed around efficient everyday cooling, combining T AI Energy Saving, smart Wi Fi control and Coanda Airflow. Its intelligent energy management technology dynamically adjusts compressor performance based on temperature conditions, helping consumers manage cooling more efficiently while maintaining indoor comfort. Refrigeration Designed for Local Households For many households across Nigeria, refrigeration needs extend beyond everyday food storage to larger family shopping, meal preparation and the need to keep food fresh for longer. Its larger format makes it particularly suited to family households looking for greater storage flexibility without compromising on contemporary kitchen design. TCL C7 Cross Door Refrigerator The TCL C780CDN introduces a spacious four door format that allows households to organise groceries, frozen food and everyday essentials more easily. Combining No Frost cooling with inverter performance, the model has been designed around flexibility, capacity and convenience, responding to the needs of households looking for practical food storage alongside a premium kitchen aesthetic. Smarter Laundry for Busy Households with the TCL C5 Washer Dryer The TCL C5 washer dryer combines a 12 kg washing capacity with TCL Super Drum technology, providing additional washing space and improved fabric movement. Its feature set includes Auto Dose, jetBubble technology, Wi Fi connectivity, Steam Wash, activeFresh, Dynamic Rinse and quick wash programmes. The large capacity format is particularly suited to family households, while its connected features and automatic washing functions help reduce the effort required for everyday laundry and fabric care. Strengthening TCL’s Presence Across Nigeria The regional launch underlines TCL’s strategy to strengthen its presence across Nigeria through a broader product ecosystem and closer collaboration with local distributors, retailers, media and technology communities. By combining global product innovation with a stronger understanding of local consumer priorities, TCL aims to deliver products that are relevant across different areas of everyday life, from entertainment and cooling to food storage, laundry and connected displays. Daniel Ray added: “Our focus is to strengthen TCL’s presence market by market, with products that respond to the needs of the consumers we serve. In Nigeria, that means bringing together larger and more immersive entertainment, efficient cooling, greater household capacity and smarter connected experiences. We see significant potential across both markets and will continue working closely with our partners to make TCL technology more widely available.” Availability Product sizes, specifications, pricing and availability may vary by market. item.title: “A Girl Who Learns Is a Girl Who Is Not a Bride” – Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili
item.description: A girl who learns is not a bride. Today, the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage ; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent. In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North, the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry. The cost of inaction is high . Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Centre for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress. Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly. Progress is possible . An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong: Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more. In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage. If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated. Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet, a girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out. Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has. item.dc:creator: BellaNaija Features
item.content:encoded: A girl who learns is not a bride. Today, the world is asked to end child marriage and invest in girls’ rights. I join that call wearing three hats: as a member of the advisory council behind Columbia University’s report Accelerating Efforts to End Child Marriage ; as Civil Society Representative on the Steering Committee of the African Union’s Decade of Accelerated Action for the Transformation of Education and Skills Development in Africa (2025–2034); and as the leader of Human Capital Africa, an organisation that has spent years arguing that Africa’s human capital crisis begins in the early-grade classroom. UNICEF’s 2026 estimates show that about one in five girls worldwide is married before 18. That adds up to roughly 650 million women and girls alive today who were married as children. More than 12 million girls are still married each year, about one every three seconds, and sub-Saharan Africa has the highest prevalence at 31 per cent. In Nigeria, 23.6 million women and girls were married before 18, the largest number in West and Central Africa. In parts of the North, the situation is a national emergency: in Jigawa, 78 per cent of women aged 20–49 were first married before 18, and 63 per cent of women left school to marry. The cost of inaction is high . Our Columbia report includes new analysis by the Centre for Global Development. It estimates losses of up to $175 billion a year, or almost $2.5 trillion by 2040, from lost productivity and higher health risks caused by child marriage. The report also warns that aid cuts, weakening global commitment to women’s rights, and rising conflict could slow or reverse progress. Child marriage is not a side issue in development. It drains a nation’s human capital directly. Progress is possible . An estimated 68 million child marriages have been averted over the past 25 years, through girls’ education, legal reform and social protection. The evidence on what works is strong: Each year of secondary education lowers a girl’s chance of marrying before 18 by five percentage points or more. In Niger, when the government removed the direct costs of middle school for rural girls, each additional year in secondary school was associated with a 19 percentage point lower probability of marriage. If every African girl completed secondary education, child marriage could be almost eliminated. Where HCA’s mission and this campaign meet, a girl cannot stay in secondary school if she never learned to read. Today, 89 per cent of children in sub-Saharan Africa are in learning poverty, unable to read and understand a simple text by age ten. A girl who cannot read by ten falls behind, then drops out. Once she is out of school, she is at the greatest risk of marriage. That is why we say schooling is not learning. Foundational literacy and numeracy are the first and cheapest protection a girl has. At the Columbia launch, I said that community programmes and advocacy are not enough on their own. Governments must lead. On this Day of the Girl, Human Capital Africa calls on African governments to: Make foundational learning a girl-protection policy. Every girl should be reading with comprehension by age ten, using proven methods such as structured pedagogy and Teaching at the Right Level. Guarantee the move into secondary school. Remove fees, uniform and transport costs for girls, especially in rural communities with high rates of child marriage. Enforce 18 as the minimum age of marriage in law and in practice, in every state and every community, with traditional and religious leaders as partners. Fund this domestically. As foreign aid shrinks, African budgets and African philanthropy must take over. Measure and publish. Track girls’ learning, their transition to secondary school, and child marriage rates in national accountability systems. The AU Decade of Education gives Africa ten years and a continental mandate. As a member of its Steering Committee, I will press for girls’ learning and retention to be at the centre of how the Decade’s success is measured. A Decade that does not end child marriage will not have transformed African education. The Columbia report sets a realistic target: cutting child marriage prevalence from one in five to one in seven within five years. Africa can lead the way to that target, but only if we treat every girl’s classroom as the place where her childhood is protected. Any girl-child should be a student, not a bride. She should learn, then lead. The post “A Girl Who Learns Is a Girl Who Is Not a Bride” – Obiageli “Oby” Ezekwesili appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Aspira Nigeria Celebrates Three Wins at Marketing Edge Awards 2026
item.description: Aspira Nigeria Limited, manufacturer of Viva detergent, Viva Dishwashing Liquid, and Oracare Toothpaste, among other household-care brands, has received three recognitions at the 2026 Marketing Edge Awards, with its brands recognised across the liquid dishwash, bar soap and detergent categories. The company received the Outstanding Liquid Dishwash Brand of the Year award, while Viva Multipurpose Soap was named Outstanding Bar Soap Brand of the Year. Aspira also received the Outstanding Detergent Brand of the Decade award, recognising its longstanding presence in Nigeria’s detergent category. The awards ceremony was held on Friday, September 25, at Ten Degrees Event Hall, Billings Way, Oregun, Ikeja, bringing together brands, marketing professionals and stakeholders from across Nigeria’s marketing, advertising and communications industry. The Marketing Edge Awards recognise brands and professionals across the marketing and communications sector, with categories covering different aspects of brand building, consumer engagement and industry performance. For Aspira, the three recognitions span different areas of its household-care portfolio. The liquid dishwash and bar soap awards recognise its presence in two competitive household categories, while the Detergent Brand of the Decade award acknowledges the longer-term journey of its detergent business. Speaking on the recognitions, Barbara Onianwah, Head of Marketing, Aspira Nigeria Limited, said the awards acknowledged the consistency required to build and sustain brands in a competitive market. “These recognitions are meaningful because they reflect the consistency and work that go into building brands that remain relevant to consumers. We are pleased that the awards recognise different areas of our portfolio, as well as the longer journey of our detergent business. For us, it is an encouragement to continue listening to consumers, learning from the market and evolving our approach,” she said. The recognitions come as brands in Nigeria’s fast-moving consumer goods sector continue to respond to changing consumer preferences and increased competition across household-care categories. With the three awards spanning liquid dishwash, bar soap and detergent, Aspira’s recognition at the 2026 Marketing Edge Awards reflects its presence across multiple segments of the household-care market, while the decade award highlights the longer history of its detergent business. The Marketing Edge Awards provided an opportunity for brands and industry professionals to come together and celebrate notable work and achievements within Nigeria’s marketing and communications landscape. item.title: Some of Ayra Starr’s Iconic Live Performances
item.description: Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London There are not many great live performers in music. Some artists are very good but are only comfortable in the studio, which is understandable because music, like writing, is a solitary work and would require extra force or pull to stand before an audience and perform. But there are also great live performers who, despite how good they are in the studio, are also comfortable bringing the music to a live audience. There is something special about that, watching an artist bring their music to life on stage. The vocals, the choreography, the stage presence, the connection with the audience — sometimes, a live performance makes you appreciate a song in an entirely new way. There aren’t many with the artistry in Afrobeats. But Ayra Starr has made herself one of Afrobeats’ most exciting performers, and has constantly used the stage as another place to show the world her sability . From commanding festival stages and performing at major international music events to delivering memorable renditions of her biggest hits, Ayra Starr has continued to prove that her talent extends beyond the recording studio. She knows how to bring her music, personality, and energy together in a way that keeps audiences watching. As her global profile continues to grow, with her recent 2026 NFL Halftime International Games performance in London, we’re looking back at some of Ayra Starr’s most iconic live performances: Ayra Starr – Rush | Glastonbury 2024 Ayra Starr & ZAYN – Heaven Baby (Live Performance @ All Points East 2026) Ayra Starr – Rush (Live Performance in Paris) Ayra Starr – Live at Global Citizen Festival 2025 (Full Performance) Ayra Starr | Live – Les Ardentes 2024 Ayra Starr Lights Up Eden Park with “Commas” | Coldplay’s Music of the Spheres Tour (Auckland) The post Some of Ayra Starr’s Iconic Live Performances appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .

item.title: Watch Ayra Starr’s 2026 NFL Halftime Performance!
item.description: Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London Since Ayra Starr emerged into the music scene with her debut EP, “Ayra Starr”, in 2021, she has gone on to break and set many records. But of all the records broken and set, none might top the feeling of being the first African artist to headline an NFL International Games Halftime Show. On Sunday, the 11th of October, 2026, at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium in London, Ayra Starr made the dream a reality. Before 61,322 people in attendance, Ayra dazzled on stage and not only made herself proud, but also made her country and language proud. She opened her performance with an emotional performance of “H eaven Baby”, her fan-favourite song featuring Zayn Malik , followed by a soulful performance of her Grammy-nominated song, “Rush.” She concluded the performance with songs from her latest album, “Starrgirl”, such as “D angerous,” “H ot Body,” and “Ms Paper.” Ayra Starr performing at the NFL Halftime Show in London Watch the full performance below: The post Watch Ayra Starr’s 2026 NFL Halftime Performance! appeared first on BellaNaija - Showcasing Africa to the world. Read today! .
